text: Ted found a shiny picture in the box. It was a bird making a nest. Ted held his crayons close. He picked blue. He drew a sky with blue in it. Then he picked green. He drew grass on the bottom of the page. The bird looked happy on the grass. Ted smiled and gave the paper to his mom. His mom said, "This is wonderful, Ted!" Ted felt big and proud. He hugged the paper to his chest. The bird and the nest were all his own. Ted blinked at his work. He was very happy.

Sam saw a flower in the yard. The flower was red and white. Sam asked the printer, "Can you print this flower?" The printer said, "Yes. But I print the same word again and again." Sam frowned. "That is silly," Sam said. The printer printed the word "flower" over and over. The paper got stuck together. The printer made a sound like tape. It was too loud. Sam put his hand over the paper. The word did not go away. It stayed on every piece. Sam took the papers outside. He let the wind blow them away. The flower was still there, growing in the dirt. Sam learned that doing the same thing again and again can make trouble.

A tall stack of paper sat on the desk. It was a gift for Sam. Each sheet was printed with a picture. One by one, the stack fell over. Papers fluttered down. Papers rolled off the desk. Sam cried. "My gift is lost!" The papers were lonely now, scattered on the floor. Nick walked into the room. "What happened?" Nick asked. Sam pointed at the floor. Nick picked up the papers. He sorted them into piles. He brought each pile back to the desk. Soon, the papers were stacked up again. Sam smiled. The gift was safe and neat once more. Nick patted Sam on the head. They were good friends.

Nick opened a new box. Inside was a new printer. A soccer ball rested next to it. The soccer ball looked scared. "What is going to happen to me?" the soccer ball asked. Nick turned on the printer. The first thing the printer printed was a big circle. The circle had lines inside it. "That is not a soccer ball," Nick said. He looked at the paper. The soccer ball was not on the page. The printer made a loud noise. Then it printed another page. This time it printed a small ball with a star. "That is closer!" Nick cheered. The soccer ball was still not perfect. But Nick was not sad. Nick helped the soccer ball understand that the first try is just the start. They would print more pages together soon.

Leo wanted a big picture for his wall. It was a huge cat. The cat had spots and stripes. Leo had a small printer at home. It could only print small things. "I need a big printer," Leo said. Leo's dog, Buster, barked. Buster wagged his tail. "Let me help!" Buster said. Leo tried to fit the big picture onto the small paper. It did not fit. The picture was too wide. The printer made a loud pop. It squeaked but could not finish. Leo sat down. Buster jumped onto the paper. Buster's tail helped push the picture flat. Then Leo started to draw over the printed parts. Buster licked his hand to say it was okay. Leo drew the rest by hand. The big cat looked wonderful on the wall. Leo smiled. Even a small printer can do great things when friends help.

Once upon a time, a shy little printer named Jill lived in a warm house. Jill liked to print pictures for the little children. One day, Jill felt a cold bump in her chest. The dark black ink was all gone. Jill could not print her pictures anymore. Jill sat quietly on the desk and looked very small. She missed all the children who came to play with her work. The children went away and did not come back. Jill felt sad. A drop of new ink fell into her tank, just a tiny bit. Jill took a deep breath. She printed one little picture. Then another. Jill smiled at her first picture after a long time. She knew she would wait for more ink. She would never give up.

Bob had a big printer at home. Bob wanted to print a bright orange nest for his bird friend. The printer hummed and waited. Then it stopped. The ink was gone in the middle of the picture. The brown dots made a sad gap where the orange should be. Bob felt worried. "Oh dear," said Bob. "What can I do now?" Bob looked around the room. He found some old watercolors. Bob painted a brand new nest by hand. He gave it to his bird friend. The bird was happy and sang a song. Bob was happy too. Sometimes you can fix a problem even when a tool breaks.

A teddy bear named Sue lived with a friendly machine called Printer. Sue loved to see pictures of flowers. When Printer printed a flower, it made a soft sound like a gentle tune. Sue would close her eyes and listen. "That is my favorite song," said Sue. One morning, Sue wanted a picture of a sky full of stars. Printer started to print. But Printer got confused. The paper fed the wrong way and jammed. The printer made a grumpy noise. Sue felt worried. "Oh no," said Sue. "It won't stop making that loud noise." Sue gently pushed the button again. Printer heard the small bear and tried once more. The paper went out right. A beautiful picture of the night sky appeared. Sue laughed. "You are my brave helper," said Sue.

A big frog teacher named Mr. Frog had many students. Mr. Frog needed help to print many cards for the children's show and tell. Mr. Frog asked a friendly printer to help. The printer worked hard all day. It printed each card very fast. By the end, every child had a card with their name on it. Mr. Frog was so glad. But one day, Mr. Frog's paper ran out. The printer could not make any more cards. All the children waited without their cards. They felt sad. Then a boy brought a new box of paper to school. Mr. Frog smiled and printed again. Everyone got a card. A good teacher helps others and learns that helpers come when they are needed.

A little bear named Anna wanted to print a picture of her whole family together. Anna held the paper carefully and pressed the button. Her papa, mama, and baby sister stood on the paper. Anna saw them all! But then Anna noticed something. Papa was standing behind Mama. That was wrong. Papa should stand next to Mama, not behind her. Anna said, "Wait. Look." Anna crossed out the old picture and drew it again. Now everyone stood in the right place. Papa stood on Mama's left. Baby sister stood on Mama's right. "There," said Anna. "Now it is perfect." Anna shared the picture with her family. Everyone clapped. Printing a picture takes patience and care, but the result is worth it.

Once upon a time there was a soccer ball in the sun. A soccer ball rolled and rolled until it hit a printer. The printer was a big box that makes pictures. It shook. "Oh," said the printer. "A soccer ball just hit me." The soccer ball said, "I did not mean to roll into you." Then the printer heard music from far away. It heard a band. The printer was so happy it began to shake even more. "What is making that fun sound?" asked the printer. "It's us," whispered the soccer ball. The two of them played under the hot sun. The soccer ball bounced and kicked. The printer made drawings of what happened. They had no other friends in sight. After the sun went down, they sat close together. They were the very best friends in the whole world.

One day there was an old printer named PeeP. He was tired. He could not print anything right. He put his head down on his desk. "I am too tired," he said. Then he heard someone calling. It was a duck walking by. "Hello, PeeP!" said the duck. "I want to drink water," said PeeP. So he took off all his parts and sat by a fence. He drank water for a long time. When he got back, he drank more water. His head felt light. Then he looked at his paper tray. There were many blank pages inside. He pulled one out and started printing. It was not good yet, but he tried again. And again. And soon his lines looked just right. He printed all the pages. He looked up. "Thank you for helping me rest," he said to the duck.

Sam was a printer who was broken. Sam could not make any pictures. The road was long and dark outside. Sam walked to the road to try to fix himself. A rabbit came running along the road. "Help! My paper was torn in half!" cried the rabbit. Sam saw the small rabbit in the dirt. "I am sorry," said Sam. "I will help you." Sam took out a new sheet of paper and folded it gently. Then he printed on it for the rabbit. The rabbit smiled. "That is very shiny," said the rabbit. "Now you have something good," said Sam. From that day on, Sam and the rabbit walked together every morning. Sam helped find lost paper. The rabbit kept him company on the long road. Sam was happy again, with his new friend beside him.

Beep was a small printer who loved to read. Beep read many stories about paper boats and paper hats. One day Beep ate too much honey on an apple. Oh no! A big sticky blob of honey fell right onto the paper. Beep tried to pull it away but it would not move. "Stop! Stop! I cannot get this paper out!" cried Beep. A hint was in what Beep read earlier: "Honey is sweet but sticky." Now Beep knew why. The honey made the paper stick to the belt inside Beep. Beep began to hop back and forth. Nothing worked. A bird flew down. "Do you need help?" asked the bird. Beep said yes. The bird used her beak to lift the honey away. Beep breathed easy again. "Thank you," said Beep. The next time Beep read, he did not eat any honey. The lesson was clear: be careful with sweet foods near machines.

Once Amy saw a tree next to the lonely printer. The tree had many green leaves and a bright trunk. "Tree," said Amy. "Are you my friend today?" "Maybe," said the tree. Amy loved Amy's printer who felt shy. Every day Amy would come and press buttons on the printer. But the printer sat quiet most of the day. That Saturday, Amy decided to go for a walk first. She came back with a small bag of candy. She fed some candy to the tree and the rest she gave to the printer. "Come eat," said Amy. The printer felt brave. It picked up a candy and ate it with a happy little chew. "Good," said the printer. "I feel like myself now." Then Amy sat down and shared candy with both the tree and the printer. For the first time that week, nobody was lonely at all.

Once upon a time, a cat named Moji had a dull black cat bed. She loved to stand on the warm printer all day long. The printer hummed softly and made her feel cozy. One morning, she saw a red leaf on the floor. She jumped onto it and got stuck right on top of the paper tray. The tray closed all by itself. Moji was trapped inside but she did not cry. A gentle hand came along and opened the tray again. Then Moji walked out into the sun and found her bed. She curled up and fell fast asleep.

There was a small green car that loved to race on the road. Every day it drove past a big building with a quiet machine called a printer. The car stopped near the machine. "I want to print my name," the car said. "Yes," said the printer in a weak voice. "But I can only print in one color." "That is fine," said the car. It tried one more day. Still, only green words came out. The car sat sad for a whole week. On the last day, the car drove to a big garden. Green words were not enough for a happy heart. So the car learned to ride on its own wheels instead.

Bella wanted to print a birthday card for her friend little Sam. She picked a nice picture and fed the paper into the printer. "Please help me," Bella said to the friendly machine. The machine started to make a loud noise. The paper began to jump and twist. "Scared," the paper said inside the machine. Bella reached in and pulled the paper back gently. Then she smoothed the paper flat. Slowly, nice birthday words came out. She added stickers and gave the card to little Sam. Sam smiled so wide. "Thank you, Bella," he said. Now every birthday is special because you always print a card.

Leo moved his old printer to a new room in his house. The new room had no windows and was very dark. "Where should I go?" asked the printer. "You can stay here," said Leo. But the printer felt lonely. Leo's mother brought a sheet of bright blue paper. "Let us play together," the mother said. The printer took the paper and started to print. Soon they could see the light come through the window. The printer felt glad. They printed pictures of birds flying in the sky. The room became happy and bright. Leo knew now that even a quiet place could be a good home for a printing friend.

Rex the printer and Pip the scanner were best friends. They both loved paper. One morning, a tiny bird landed on Rex's top shelf. "Hello, friends," said the bird. "We are busy today," said Rex. Pip agreed too. "We must print and scan lots of things," Rex said. "We will work hard and have fun!" Pip nodded. They printed pages for the school. They scanned drawings for the art show. The bird watched them from above and chirped happily. When the work was done, Rex and Pip rested under a warm lamp. The bird flew up to them and sang a song. Everyone shared a happy feeling and a full stomach of joy.

Lucy had a leaf that was blank and white. It was warm from the sun but it felt very empty. A little rabbit said, "I want to draw on you." Lucy said, "You can climb up to my hand and we will print a picture together." The leaf climbed up. Lucy pressed the paper down into the machine. The machine printed a red heart, then green grass, then blue sky. The leaf became beautiful. "Look!" said Lucy. "It is mine now," said the rabbit.

Once upon a time, there was a dark room. A man wanted a story for his son at bedtime. He put a big book of words inside the printer. The sun was shining outside but it was time for sleep. The printer hummed and printed the story slowly. It made tall trees, sleeping bears, and stars in the sky. The baby fell asleep very fast. The printer printed one more page of soft clouds. Then it went quiet. The man smiled and closed his eyes too. Everyone was safe and warm in bed.

A teddy bear sat next to the printer. It bumped into a wall and broke its shell. "I am sorry," said the printer. "My head is not right," said the teddy bear. "I am fine, thank you," said the printer. The printer tried to fix itself with tape around its shell. But the tape was short and did not reach all the way. The printer still could not work well. "Could you help me?" asked the printer. "I will try," said the teddy bear. The teddy bear held the printer and taped the whole shell until it was tight and ready again. They both felt much better.

Sunny was a little mouse who lived behind the office printer. He had a long cup of water in his hand every day. The printer could make loud noises but Sunny liked it anyway. One day the printer stopped working. The paper jammed inside. Sunny ran under the desk. He gave the broken paper a tiny push with his nose. The paper slid out clean. The printer began to make a sound again. "Thank you, Sunny," said the boss. "You are my helper today." Sunny drank his water and ate a crumb. Life was good behind the machine.

A brown cake sat near the old printer. A kind woman baked the cake for a party. She wanted to give it to the printer because it worked so hard all day. "Can you visit my house?" she asked the printer. The printer said, "Yes, I would love to come." The printer rolled over to the house and stood by the front door. "You are welcome here," said the woman. "I cannot eat but I like sitting in your light." The woman cut a small piece of the brown cake and set a plate inside. The printer rested on a chair beside the sweet smell. Everyone liked the visit.

Once upon a time, a red apple sat on a tree. It was warm and shiny. A little bird flew down. The bird looked at the apple and said, "I want to eat you." The apple said, "You can take me, but I am not ready yet." The bird did not cry. She waited by the apple tree all morning. When the sun came out, the apple was cool and soft. The bird could open her beak right then. She ate the apple. It was pretty inside.

One day, a big machine hummed in the yard. The machine opened its paper tray. Then it printed a picture of the sunny tree. The bird saw the picture on the paper. She said, "This is like my apple!" The machine smiled. It printed more pictures. The bird took one and put it in her nest. Now she had a picture of her apple every day. The lesson is: good things are not always right away, but if we wait, they come soon.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Pippin. Pippin was a sleepy cat. He liked to sleep on a pillow. One day, a loud beep came from the printer. It was a very loud beep! Pippin jumped up. He asked, "What is that loud sound?" The printer did not talk back. It just beeped again. Pippin walked over to the printer. He asked, "Why do you beep so loud?" The printer said, "I have too much paper." Pippin did not understand. He thought the machine was sick. He said, "You should rest too." The beep stopped. The machine was quiet for a while. Then it made a small whirring sound. Pippin went back to his pillow. He was happy now. The lesson is: machines do not need help from cats. We must let them work.

Pam had a teddy bear named Sunny. Sunny had red fur. One day, Pam wanted to play. She took a piece of paper from the printer. It was a big red picture. The picture showed a boat on the water. Pam gave it to Sunny. Sunny held the paper. She said, "I want to make a boat." Pam cut the paper along the line. The paper folded. Sunny blow on the paper. A paper boat floated on the table. Sunny was so proud. She sailed the boat across the water. "Row, row, row," the boat said. Sunny laughed and pushed the boat again. Pam smiled. They played with the boat all afternoon. At the end of the day, Pam put the paper in her book. The lesson is: we can find new things to play with when we look at things closely.

Once upon a time, a tiny robot named Milo lived under a desk. Milo was busy fixing printers. One morning, a big paper jam stopped the printer. The printer said, "I cannot move." Milo came closer. He said, "I can fix you." Milo looked at the paper. It was stuck deep inside. Milo made a small tool with his hands. He reached into the machine. He pulled the paper out. Then he made the gears turn again. The printer worked! Milo was tired but he was happy. A cat named Oliver walked by. Oliver said, "Thank you, Milo. You fixed my friend." Milo opened his eyes. He said, "You are welcome, Oliver. I am always here to help." Milo went back to work. He was busy fixing more printers that day. The lesson is: being helpful is nice, even when we are very busy.

Lily visited a library. The library was quiet. Lily walked down the long road to the shelves. She found a book about a kind librarian. The librarian had a special printer. Lily wanted to print a sign. She asked the librarian. The librarian was kind. She said, "Yes, you can use the printer." Lily fed paper into the tray. She pressed a button. The printer started. But a loud crash came! A cat ran through the room. It knocked over the paper. The paper rolled under the printer. The printer said, "I cannot work." Lily cried a little. Then she looked at the room. The cat was sitting on the floor. It looked up and meowed softly. Lily felt better. She said, "Oh, you poor thing." She picked up the paper. She went to feed it back in. The machine worked again. It printed a neat sign. Now the library was happy. The lesson is: we can help others when they are sad. Kindness helps everyone.

Once upon a time there was a pink robot. It was a printer. Bo loved the robot very much. Bo gave the robot a soccer ball. The soccer ball rolled under the table. The robot did not stop printing pages. It printed and printed and printed. Pages piled up everywhere. Bo sat on the floor. The robot was still printing. The pages made a loud noise. Bo felt sad. Then a big wind came. The wind pushed all the papers away. The robot stopped. Bo smiled. The robot was quiet now.

Once upon a time a little girl drew a picture. She drew a big house and a little dog. She gave her drawing to a robot. The robot was a printer. The printer tried to print the picture. But the ink was too wet. The printer spilled ink on the paper. The picture was all wet. The little girl cried. A bubble popped on the desk. The bubble made a funny sound. The printer heard the bubble. The printer drank the bubble. Then it printed the picture again. The little girl saw the bright drawing. She felt happy again.

It was a cold morning. Snow fell outside. Jade woke up slowly. The room was very quiet. Then she heard a sound. Warm paper came out of the printer. It smelled like honey. Jade pulled one piece. It was yellow. She pulled another piece. It was also warm. Jade had a cup of hot cocoa. She ate a sweet cookie. The warm paper kept coming out. It made the cold room feel cozy. Jade read her story on the warm paper. She felt safe and happy. The warm paper was better than cold snow.

Inky had a teddy bear. Inky wanted a new picture for his wall. He asked the printer to print one. The printer started to work. It took a long time. Finally, it printed a picture of a race. Not a picture of a teddy bear! Inky looked at the picture. It showed two long rectangles running fast. "That is not what I asked for," Inky said. He felt angry. Then he saw something else. One of the long rectangles had a smiley face. It looked like the teddy bear! Inky laughed. He hung the picture on his wall. Now his wall had a funny new picture.

Jade found an old printer in the hall. It was slow. It printed one page very slowly. It took many minutes. Jade waited and waited. The printer finally finished. The paper was light. The printer was tired now. Jade said thank you to the old machine. "I am slow," the printer said. "That is all right." Jade patted the machine gently. The machine was not mad at all. It just needed rest. Jade turned it off. The next day the printer worked fast again. Jade learned that every machine has its own time.

Once upon a time, Lucy walked into the busy office. A light bulb sat above her head. A light bulb glowed yellow. Lucy sat on a chair. She had a big stack of papers to draw today. The printer was very loud. It started to print. Then a paper fell out of the light. It was bumpy. Lucy picked it up. "Oh no," she said. "A paper fell out." The printer said, "That is not my fault." Lucy laughed. The office was happy again.

A soccer ball rolled into the room. A soccer ball bounced near the shy printer. The printer was quiet for a long time. It wanted to help. But it was too shy. "I want to play," said the soccer ball. "Do you want to play?" asked the printer. "Yes," said the soccer ball. The printer printed many pages. It used the pages to make a big tall tower. The soccer ball rolled right up the tower. It was very fun. The printer felt happy now.

A puppy stood by the printer. A puppy liked to stack blocks. But the puppy wanted to draw. The puppy looked at a stack of blank paper. "I want to draw," said the puppy. The puppy took a small piece of paper. It put it on the desk. But the puppy did not know how to hold a pencil. "Help me," it said. The printer heard the puppy. The printer printed a big drawing of a puppy. "Now you can draw," said the printer. The puppy drew all day long.

Lucy had a cat named Cup. Cup was a very kind cat. One day, Cup saw a big machine in the room. The machine could write letters on paper. Cup was curious. Cup walked right up to the machine. A tiny drop of ink jumped out of the machine. The drop wanted to see the world. It floated up to the ceiling and looked out the window. Cup watched the drop go past the moon. "Where are you going?" asked Cup. "I want to see big trees," said the drop. Cup licked the drop with his tongue. The drop slid down Cup's fur and fell onto the paper. It made a tiny dark dot. Cup purred with joy. The dot was the start of something good. Lucy smiled and patted the cat. Then the machine wrote more words on the paper. The dot helped tell a story. That story was happy all the way through.

Joe sat at the desk. Grandpa sat next to him. They were making a menu for a pretend restaurant. Joe picked up a big white piece of paper. He held it over the page where he wanted to print. He pressed down. But nothing happened! The paper stayed blank. Joe tried again. Still nothing. "What is wrong?" said Joe. Grandpa looked at the paper. Then Grandpa looked at the machine. "The paper is the wrong size," said Grandpa. He took a smaller piece of paper from his bag. Joe printed the menu on this small paper instead. When Grandpa opened the door, a bird dropped a leaf on the floor. Joe put the leaf on the small menu. It was a fun surprise. Everyone clapped for the clever idea.

The sun went to sleep. The sun slid below the hills. The office grew dark. Fox came into the office after everyone left. Fox pushed the door shut behind him. Fox walked behind the big desk. Fox pulled the printing lever. The machine hummed loud. Paper rolled out. Fox picked up a sheet of paper. Fox read what was on the paper. It was a letter that no one sent. "This does not make sense," said Fox. Fox pushed the lever again. The machine wrote the same letter again. The same wrong letter again. Fox laughed. Then Fox thought about it. Fox pushed the lever a third time. The machine printed the right letter this time. Fox smiled and walked away. The next day, someone got a good letter from the office.

Tom wanted to print a picture for grandma. Tom picked up a sheet of paper. He found the ink box and put paper inside. He pushed the button. The machine started to hum. Tom heard a song coming from the machine. It was a happy little tune. Tom smiled. Then the machine made a sound. It was a scary sound. "Oh no," said Tom. The machine made a huge mess on the paper. The ink made black blobs everywhere. The picture was ruined. "That is not how I wanted it," said Tom. Tom picked up the bad paper. The ink fell off onto Tom's hand. Tom wiped his hand on his shirt. Tom looked around for help. A neighbor lady walked by. "Are you okay, dear?" she asked. "I need help with my printer," said Tom. The neighbor helped clean up the paper. Tom printed another picture. This time he held the paper steady. Grandma loved the new picture very much.

Duck was napping on the bed. Duck did not hear the printer fall over. The printer broke down. "Help me, please," hummed the broken printer. No one was home. Duck looked at the broken printer. Duck waddled over and poked the printer. The printer did not hum. It was silent. "I am cold and tired," said the printer softly. Duck flapped her wings. "I will keep you warm," said Duck. Duck pulled a big pillow toward the printer. The pillow covered the broken parts. Duck lay down on top of the pillow. The warmth felt good. Soon the machine began to hum again. It was a quiet, kind hum. The printer printed a small paper. On the paper was a note: "Thank you for helping me." Duck read the note. "You are welcome," hummed the printer. Duck closed her eyes and rested. The printer hummed until the morning came.

Once upon a time, there was a little house at the edge of town. Ted lived there. One morning, Ted's friend set up a big printer outside his house. The printer could print silly jokes. It printed jokes about dogs and babies. The joke paper landed right inside the house. Ted read each joke. He laughed and laughed until his sides hurt. Then the joke paper fell down the hill. Ted could not find any of it. Ted felt sad that he could not read the jokes again at home.

A robot came to a warm house. The robot wanted to make paper snowflakes. "I can print," said the robot. The robot printed six triangles of paper. Then it cut the triangles apart. Each triangle made one nice snowflake. The robot made four snowflakes. Then it made three more. The robot looked at the snowflakes and they were not quite right. It printed again and cut again. Finally, seven perfect snowflakes hung by the door. Everyone in the house smiled.

Once upon a time, a dog named Max sat near a wall. Max saw a sheet of paper on the floor. Max picked up the paper and folded it into a plane. Max threw the plane as far as he could. The paper flew over the roof of the house. Max followed. The plane flew far away over the sea. Max saw the paper fly over the water. Then the paper landed near a boat. The wind blew and the paper lifted again. Max clapped his paws. A new flying paper came back to him.

Once upon a time, there was an old man named Grandpa who lived under a big tree. Grandpa liked to read books every night by the light of the moon. One day, Grandpa got a new printer that blinked a slow red light. "What does it want?" Grandpa asked the printer. The printer blinked back and said, "I would like to print pictures for you." Grandpa learned that the printer could make colorful pictures from paper. Grandpa was lucky to have such a helpful machine in his house. Grandpa printed a picture of his tree for his garden. He hung the picture on the wall above the tree. Every night, he looked at the picture and smiled. The printer blinked its green light, happy to work. Grandpa felt warm and happy all day long.

Max lost his puppy inside the woods. Max called out, "Puppy! Here!" but the puppy did not come. Max felt sad. His mom said, "We can print a poster to find the puppy." They went to the printer and told it what to do. The printer said, "I can print, but I need paper first." Mom cut a large sheet of paper. The printer printed a bright poster with a drawing of a dog. Max gave the poster to his dad. His dad took the poster outside under the light of the sun. Many people saw the poster. A kind woman saw it and called the police. The police found the puppy near a pond. The puppy was wet and sleepy. Max ran to get his puppy. Max hugged his wet puppy and cried happy tears. They went home with the puppy safe in their arms.

Mia sat under a big tree with her favorite book in her lap. Mia was curious about the big machine in her house that made things. She peeked at the front panel of the printer. A yellow button waited there, round and round. "Can I press it?" Mia whispered. Her mom said yes. Mia pressed the button gently. The printer hummed and took a piece of paper. It printed a funny drawing of a little bird flying. Mia clapped her hands. Then she pressed the button again. Another drawing came out, this time a red car. Mia kept pressing the button. The printer made many drawings for her. Her mom came to look and laugh. "You are so lucky," Mom said. Mia learned that the printer liked to print things when someone asked nicely. She pressed the button one more time for her friend. They shared the drawings under the tree.

A robot named Bo brought fresh paper to the big printer every morning. Bo walked through the gate each day. One morning, Bo dropped the paper and looked very sad. "My arm is broken," Bo said softly. The printer asked, "What will we do without you?" Bo said, "I am not fit to carry paper anymore." The printer had no paper to print, so nothing happened. Day after day, nothing was printed. The people inside were sad too. They printed only one small book by hand. That book was their last printed thing. One sunny day, Bo found a stick near the tree. Bo picked up the stick and made it like an arm. Bo carried one piece of paper to the printer. The printer made a happy little picture. Everyone smiled. The lesson was simple: take care of helpers, because they help us when we need them.

Noah stood next to his big printer and looked at his small printer. Noah asked the big printer, "Can you print a flower for me?" The big printer said, "Yes, I can print one right now." But the big printer made a dry, flat flower. Noah shook his head. Noah took the flower to his small printer. "Please," Noah said. The small printer made a tiny purple flower with bright yellow stars. Noah put the dry flower in a glass of water. The flower grew wet again and opened up. Noah laughed. "You are better than my big printer!" Noah said. The big printer heard this and felt sad. It thought, "Maybe I am not as good as my small friend." Noah gave the small printer a piece of paper to draw on. The small printer made a pretty picture. Both printers worked together that day. Noah smiled at both machines. Even the big printer helped by letting the small printer draw on its screen.

Once upon a time, there was a soccer ball in the room. The soccer ball could not sleep. Outside the window, it heard a whirring sound. The printer was awake. It was drinking cold water from its tank. The soccer ball ran under the bed to hide. A long line of light came out of the printer. It was making something. The soccer ball was safe but very scared. Then the printer stopped. It went back to sleep. The soccer ball sat up and played again.

A little frog wanted a nice card. The card said thank you. "Thank you," the frog whispered. The frog went to the machine. The machine had a big wheel. The wheel rolled back and forth. "I will print your card for you," the machine said. But the ink was stuck. The wheel tried to move but it did not turn. The wheel ate the ink. "Oh dear," said the frog. The frog said, "Please do not eat my card." The machine stopped. The frog sat on a leaf and waited. Later the machine spat the ink out. Then the card printed. The frog was happy to get its card.

A fish lived in a bowl of water. One day a boy brought a picture of the fish. He wanted to print it. The machine started. But the paper jammed. The black part of the paper got stuck on the hot plate. "Uh oh," said the boy. He tried to pull the paper out but it tore. The fish watched from the water. It was sad for the boy. The boy felt bad. Then the machine pushed the paper back by itself. Out came a perfect picture of the fish. The boy smiled. "Thank you, friend." The fish did not understand all the words but it knew the boy was happy again.

The cat heard the sound of pulling paper. "Hmm," said the cat. "That sounds like the last sheet." The cat looked into the tray. There was only one small piece of paper left. The cat saw some paste on the table. The paste was sticky. The cat reached for the paper. "I will eat this paper," the cat thought. But the cat did not really want to eat the paper. The cat wanted a treat instead. So the cat pulled the paper gently. The cat took the paper to the table. There the cat smoothed the paper flat with both paws. The cat set the paper down. Then the cat found a nice fish bone on the table. The cat ate the fish bone and was happy.

A car pulled into the shop on the road. The car said, "I need a ticket now." The printer inside the shop said, "I am printing your ticket." The printer needed paper. The printer found wet paper on the floor. "This paper is too wet," the printer said. "I cannot print on this," the printer said. A rain drop fell on the paper. The paper got even more wet. The printer stopped working. The car was sad. Then the rain stopped. The printer dried the paper with a warm cloth. The printer printed the ticket. The car drove away happy. Something unexpected happened when the printer found an umbrella under the paper tray. The umbrella helped keep the paper dry.

Leo sat near the printer by the window. Leo looked out the window and saw a horse standing under the sun. The sun was bright. "That horse has a clean coat," Leo said. "Yes, he looks very shiny," the printer said. Leo asked, "Can I go see the horse?" The printer said, "No, I must stay here." But Leo looked again. The horse stepped close to the window. Leo could almost touch the glass. The horse stomped its hoof once. Leo laughed. That night the printer was lonely. Leo opened the door and brought a small saddle for the horse. The horse came to the house. They all played together outside. It was a fun ending.

Monkey sat next to the empty paper tray. Monkey looked inside. It was blank. "What should I do?" Monkey said. The calculator next to the tray said, "Do you need more paper?" Monkey said, "No, but my fingers are tired." Monkey picked up some blank paper. Monkey printed a picture of a banana. Monkey stuck it on the wall. The picture was big and bright. "I love my work," Monkey said. Monkey ate a banana and smiled. Monkey kept printing many pictures. The paper tray stayed empty because Monkey used all the paper. Every day Monkey made new pictures. It was a good day for printing and for drawing.

Once upon a time, a little printer was afraid of the dark. The dark office felt too big and too quiet. All day, the printer stayed under the desk. One night, the lights went out. Now the printer could not see a thing. It did not know where to put its paper. A brave hand clapped on the desk. "That is enough," said a friendly voice. Then came a warm light from the window. The printer could see now. It stood tall and printed a picture of a tree with an apple on top. The printer felt brave again.

Jack loved a party very much. He wanted all his friends to come. But Jack had no cat to help him call them. A cat slept on the bed while Jack searched for a way around. Then he found a big yellow printer in the hall. "Will you help me print the invitations?" asked Jack. The machine hummed a happy tune. It pulled paper in and pushed ink out. Soon the invitations were ready. The cat meowed softly and opened the front door. Every friend got an invitation. At last, all the kids arrived at the party. The cat ate a big cake and everyone clapped and laughed.

Once there was a boy who found a treasure map in an old book. He wanted to print it so he could follow it with his friends. But the map was torn. Only half of it showed a park. The other half was blank. A blank page is not helpful. Jack sat down and thought hard. He put the map on the printer. The machine tried to print but it made only one messy line. The printer shook and printed again. Now the map was clear. The boy helped the printer print the second half. The full map showed a park with a big tree and a loud river. They all went there to find real gold. They found cookies instead. Everyone was happy.

At school, Dot needed pictures for her class project. The teacher told Dot to use the school printer. Dot fed a piece of paper into the machine. The machine started to print. Suddenly, a loud noise came from the printer. It dropped a stack of paper on the floor. Dot rushed over and picked up all the paper. She helped the machine clean up. Then she fed the paper back in. The printer printed bright pictures of a tree and a sun. Dot hung the pictures on the wall. Her class clapped loudly for Dot's good work.

Milo lay in bed under his soft blanket. Outside, a printer hummed loud noises at night. Milo wanted to sleep more than anything. The printer printed words for hours. Milo heard the sounds bumping along the floor. Milo did not smile. Milo called out, "Stop that noise now." The printer stopped at once. Milo got up and turned it off. Milo pulled his blanket over his head. Milo was so sleepy that he closed his eyes. Good night, printer. Good night, Milo.

A little girl drew a pretty star on paper. She put the paper into the printer. The cat watched from the desk. The cat liked the paper but could not reach it. The printer printed the drawing. The cat saw the star come out the door. The cat purred with joy. Then the printer made a sound and shut its door. The cat could not get any paper now. The cat sat alone on the mat. The girl came back with another piece of paper. The cat stayed close to the printer again.

Inky the frog looked everywhere for his lost friend. Inky could not find his red frog anywhere. Inky sat on a lily pad and cried. A bird flew down. "I can help," the bird said. They went to the printer together. Inky held out some paper. "Print my friend," said Inky. The printer printed a picture of a red frog. Inky hung it up on the wall. Soon a mouse saw the poster. The mouse ran fast toward the picture. "There is my red friend," the mouse called out. Inky hopped over and they all played together again.

Sara had a calculator and a big, warm printer at home. Sara liked to put the cat, Milo, on top of the printer because it was so warm from the machine. Milo liked warm spots too. One day, Sara wanted to print a book. She fed a paper into the tray. The printer hummed. Out came a page with one book on it. Then another page came out. Milo could not catch the pages before they went down the desk. He tried again. This time he sat right on the paper tray and waited. The next pages printed fast. Milo caught one page and put it in his mouth. Then he pawed the other one. "I caught them all," Milo said with a happy purr. Sara smiled. She gave Milo a treat. He was a lucky cat who always got to help with the printing.

Sunny worked at the library. The library had many books and one busy printer. Sunny tried to use the printer every day after school. But often the printer made loud sounds and did not print right. One day, Sunny pushed the paper tray all the way back so no paper would fall. She turned the switch on. The printer went quiet. Too quiet. The last copy of a story was missing. Sunny felt sad inside. The dog next door saw Sunny looking at the empty tray. "You may try again tomorrow," the dog said gently. Sunny nodded. She closed the library door. She would come back next week and try again. The next week she came back and the printer worked just fine. Sunny smiled and thanked the dog.

Tess had a neat little bike that her brother built for her. Tess loved the bike very much. One morning, Tess fed a sheet of paper into the printer. The printer needed the last paper to print a drawing. But the last paper was stuck under the front tray. The paper did not wave or move. Tess squeezed the tray but it would not slide out. The drawing could not be printed. Tess felt worried. Then a bird landed on the machine. The bird saw the stuck paper and pecked at it. The pecking moved the paper just enough. The paper slid right out. "Thank you, bird," Tess said. She printed the drawing right then. The bird flew away with a bit of paper on its beak. Tess hung the drawing on the wall. It was the neatest drawing she had ever seen.

Amy worked in an office all day. At the end of the day, Amy locked the door and turned off the lights. Only the printer stayed on. Amy placed a banana peel near the printer. She wanted the printer to print the office memo so no one would see it. The banana peel fell onto the paper tray. Then the printer started to hum. A copy came out of the printer, neat and full of words. Amy read the memo. It said no one should eat banana peels near printers. Amy laughed. She took the banana and ate it outside. The printer kept humming for a while. Then it stopped. Everything was quiet. Amy went to bed happy. She learned that you must keep things clean in the office so machines can do their jobs well.

Once upon a time, a cat named Sunny sat on the grass. The sun was hot and Sunny was thirsty. He saw a lemonade stand near the window. But nobody could read the sign. Sunny could read it. "I can help," said Sunny.

Sunny found some big paper. He held it up. The words were small. He had to make them big so everyone could see.

A friendly printer lived under the table. It hummed softly. "What do you need?" asked the printer.

"I need you to print a sign for my lemonade stand," said Sunny.

The printer rolled its white paper into itself. Then it pressed down and pushed out fresh words. A purple sign appeared on the paper. "Look!" said Sunny. "The words are big. Everyone can see."

The man at the stand read the sign. "Yummy lemonade!" he said. People bought cups of lemonade. Sunny drank one and smiled. He sat on the bench and purred. The cat helped, and that made him happy.

Tess walked into her new house. It was her mother's birthday soon. Tess wanted to make a card for her mom.

Tess put her hands on the new printer on the table. She pressed the button. The machine clapped twice. It made a sound like a gentle drum.

Then the printer pulled in cold white paper. It made two cards. One card was for her mom. One card was for her dad.

Tess picked up her mom's card. It looked very nice. "Thank you, Mom," she said. She handed the card to her mom. Her mom smiled big.

"Thank you, baby," said her mom. Then Tess gave her dad his card too. Her dad clapped for Tess.

Tess clapped back. She did a happy dance around the table. Her mom and dad were so glad. They said, "We love you, Tess." Tess felt warm inside. She learned that being helpful makes everyone happy.

Two printers stood in a tall tower. One was white. One was green. They always stood next to each other.

The green printer wanted more paper. It needed a new roll of white paper. The white printer had plenty of paper. But the green printer could not get the paper. It felt stuck and left alone.

The white printer did not want to fight. It just wanted its friend to be happy. So it moved away from the green printer.

Later, the green printer found a job at a shop. It printed pretty pictures for many people. It earned good money.

One day, the green printer went home. It found its white friend standing alone. "I have paper again," said the green printer. "Thank you for helping me."

The white printer smiled. They stood together again. They worked side by side.

They learned that sharing makes life better. Being kind helps friends when they are sad. Two printers became the best friends, and that was wonderful.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Ray. Ray was a special machine that printed on paper. Ray liked to print a big cake for his friend Leo. The cake paper was almost dry when the toner ran out. Ray could not print anymore. He sat very still. Leo came with a box of new toner. Ray took the toner and smiled. He printed the cake and it was great. Leo shared the cake and everyone ate a bite. Ray felt happy now. It was a sad day for Ray at first but a happy day later.

Once upon a time there was a big printer and a small printer in a house. Ruby was the small printer. She wanted to learn how to print big letters. The big printer said she could use him. "You are warm," the big printer said. "I will help you," he said. Ruby pressed her hands on his side. She learned to move her arms left and right. Then she printed a name on paper. "Look," Ruby said. The big printer clapped his metal hands. They were a good team now.

The sun was up in the sky. It was very bright outside. A family was sitting on the porch. They were reading a paper by the window. The paper slipped out of the open window. It flew into the air. The wind sang a little song to it. The paper did not go far. A bird saw the paper and landed on it. The bird ruffled its feathers on the page. The family laughed out loud. The bird had found something nice to sit on. The family went back inside and kept reading.

Once upon a time a hungry pig came to a frog named Noah. Noah worked in an office. Noah's job was to fix printers. A paper got stuck in the printer. It was torn into two pieces. Noah reached into the machine. His hand was stuck too! "Help!" Noah said. The pig pulled Noah out. "You look hungry," the pig said. "I am very hungry," Noah said. Noah ate a cracker. Then he fixed the printer. Paper came out smooth. Noah was happy again. Everyone was glad.

Once upon a time, a printer lived in a very small room. A seed dropped from the wall and fell right on top of the printer. The printer had to wait while the seed went inside. Then, out came a tiny bird with a long beak. The bird looked at the little room and said, "That is too small for me!" The printer felt sad. Then the bird sang a big, loud song. The printer was happy again. Now the printer lives in a bigger room with the bird. The bird sings every day. The printer waits for the bird to sing.

A crumpled paper sat on the floor. It was wrinkled and bent. A little worm saw it and said, "You look like dirt!" The paper said, "I want to be flat." The worm said, "Can you hum?" The paper said, "Hmm?" The worm nudged the paper and said, "Just relax. Be soft." The paper sat down. It took a deep breath. Then it became flat and smooth. A garden grew where the paper had been. Worms played all around it. The paper was happy to help the worms. It learned that if you stop being hard, you can become flat again and help others.

Anna baked a cake and put it on a plate on her table. She turned on the printer and put a page near the window. The page flew away out the open window. Anna ran outside. She looked at the hill. The wind blew. The page went fast over the hill. "Where did my paper go?" Anna said. She looked up and down but could not find the paper. She sat on the grass and waited. Then she heard a sound. A bird landed on a branch above her head. The bird flapped its wings twice. The page fluttered down into Anna's lap. Anna was glad to get it back. She ate a piece of cake with the bird.

A dog named Max sat next to the printer. Max wanted a picture of his owner. The printer started to print. But something was wrong. The printer could not make the picture right. The printer tried and tried and tried. Max barked once, then stopped. Then the printer made a soft humming sound. It hummed a song like a lullaby. Suddenly, the picture looked perfect. Max wagged his tail. The dog said, "Thank you!" The printer felt glad to help. Max licked the printer's hand. The printer was fresh and warm and happy now.

A printer broke one morning. It would not work anymore. A little girl brought a broken paper near the machine. "Oh no," she said. "What can I do?" A kind woman named Mrs. Lila walked by. She said, "Let me try." Mrs. Lila folded the broken paper into a square. Then she put fresh paper inside. She pressed the button. The machine hummed again and printed well. The little girl smiled. Mrs. Lila went to the park with the girl. They walked among green trees. The girl said, "The printer is fixed!" They were happy together in the park.

Once upon a time, Max got a new printer. It sat on the table in his room. Max was very excited. He wanted to print something first. Max thought about a picture of a cake. He gave the paper to the printer. The printer hummed and beeped. Then it printed! A little picture came out. It was a tiny cake. Max smiled and drew a smiley face on it. "I did it!" said Max. The printer just hummed softly. It liked being with Max. A little comb was at the top of the cake drawing. Max thought that was funny. The printer did not mind. It waited for the next paper.

Pip was a shy printer. Pip sat by the window. Pip had never printed anything for a long time. A bird flew up to the window. Pip wanted to print a picture of the bird. Pip held the paper close. But Pip was too scared. The bird landed on the table. Pip tried to stack the paper but Pip did not move. "Come on," said Pip. "I will help you." The bird cooed. Pip took a deep breath. Then Pip pressed the button. Beep! A picture of a bird came out. Pip felt happy. The bird chirped. Now Pip could print any bird in the sky. Pip was no longer shy. Pip was curious about all the birds. Pip printed a blue bird and a yellow bird and a red bird. They all sat on the table with Pip.

Rex loved his printer but wanted to see outside. The window was very helpful but showed only trees. Rex saw a dog playing in the yard. Rex wanted to print the dog. But the printer needed paper. Rex found a toy on the floor. Rex put the toy in the tray. Rex pressed the button. The printer ran and ran but the paper jammed. "Oh dear," said Rex. Rex had to help the printer. Rex pulled the stuck paper out slowly. Then Rex put a new piece of paper. "Good again," said Rex. The printer hummed and printed a picture of the dog. Rex looked at the dog and smiled. Sometimes you have to wait and help before printing can work. The printer learned that too.

Rex wanted to print a birthday card. Rex wrote happy birthday on the card. Rex put the card in the tray. Rex pressed the button. The printer started running. Suddenly, the printer squeaked. The paper stuck. Rex pulled hard. Out tumbled some pieces of pie. "Oops," said Rex. Pieces of pie flew everywhere. Rex chased the pie pieces around the room. Rex picked them up one by one. Rex cleaned the floor with a damp cloth. Then Rex put the card back in the tray. Rex pressed the button again. The printer printed the card perfectly. The card had a smooth design. Rex held the card and blew out the candle. Happy birthday to Rex! The pie pieces were gone. The printer was very proud. Rex ate some of the pie too.

Sam had a new printer. Sam wanted to print a picture of food. Sam chose a plate. Sam put the paper in the tray. Sam pressed the button. The printer hummed. Then Sam heard a loud bark. A puppy ran into the room. The puppy grabbed the paper and ran away. Sam shouted, "Stop, dog!" Sam chased the dog around the table. The puppy kicked a chair. The puppy hid under the bed. Sam looked down. The puppy was sleeping. Sam sat back down. Then Sam saw the paper on the floor. Sam picked it up. The puppy ran over and sniffed the paper. Sam smiled. "You got it," said Sam. Sam put the paper on the table. The puppy did not eat the paper. The puppy just slept near it. Sam patted the puppy. The puppy was huge and soft. Sam was glad the puppy was safe.

A family wanted to print a picture of everyone. Dad stood on one side. Mom stood on another side. Two kids stood on the other sides. It was time to print. The printer sat ready. The family gave the printer paper. They all stepped back. The printer hummed. Then the printer made a sound. The paper got wet. Water spilled from the tray. The picture could not dry well. "Oh no," said Mom. The wet paper ruined the picture. The kids cried a little. Dad looked at the printer. "We need fresh paper," said Dad. The family took the wet paper out. They put dry paper in the tray instead. The printer hummed again. This time the picture came out nice. Everyone clapped. The lesson was that good paper makes good pictures. The printer helped make a memory.

Once upon a time, there was a printer named Printer. Printer sat on a table under a big tree. The tree had green leaves. Printer was quiet all day. No one used Printer at the weekend. The tree rustled its leaves and said, "Hello, Printer!" Printer did not say hello back. It just sat there. Then a little car drove by and dropped a sticker. The sticker stuck to the table near Printer. The sticker said "Happy Weekend!" The sticker was so loud when it moved. A child came to pick up the sticker. She put the sticker on her bag. Printer felt happy for a while. But then it sat alone again under the tree. The tree whispered, "You don't have to be lonely, Printer." Printer smiled and went to sleep.

Once upon a time, a robot named Robo walked to a printer. Robo carried a box. The box had paper inside. Robo gave the box to the printer. The printer took the paper. But the printer was sad. The printer could not print anything. Robo looked at the empty machine. "Why are you sad?" asked Robo. The printer said, "No one gives me paper anymore." Robo smiled and opened the box again. He pulled out one sheet of paper. "Here," said Robo. The printer took the paper and printed a picture of a cat. The cat had yellow ears and pink whiskers. Robo was happy. From that day, Robo always brought paper to the printer before the weekend. The printer never went hungry again.

Leo sat down to draw. He had an empty sheet of paper in front of him. The paper was blank. Leo wanted to draw a cake. But he did not know how. He looked around. There was a bag of crayons on the table. Leo picked up the bag. He shook the crayons. One crayon fell out. It was red. Leo tried to draw with the red crayon. The paper got sticky. The red marks stuck to the paper. Leo wiped his hand on his shirt. The paper was still sticky. He tried again with a blue crayon. The paper stuck together. Leo's picture would not come out right. Leo sat down. He looked at the sticky paper. "I cannot draw the cake," said Leo. His mom came with a clean sheet of paper. "Let me help you," she said. Leo smiled. He drew a beautiful cake with a cherry on top.

A tall stack of paper stood on the table. The stack was very tall. A bird landed on the stack. The bird was tired of looking at the table. The bird flapped its wings. One paper flew off. Then another paper flew off. The stack began to wobble. The papers bumped into each other. Soon the whole stack tipped over. Papers scattered everywhere. A paper hit the floor. Papers piled up in a messy heap. The bird landed on top of the pile. The bird was happy. The papers were safe now. The bird sang a song. Leo came to pick up the papers. He put them back in the box. The stack was tall again. Everything was fine. The bird was still happy.

Leo sat on a bench near the printer. The printer was old and slow. It made a beeping sound. "I am ready," said the printer. "Give me paper," said Leo. Leo pulled a printed page from the box. The page had a drawing of a plane on it. Leo cut along the line with scissors. The paper airplane flew out of his hands. It glided over the bench. It flew past the tree. The tree had a nice shape. The plane zoomed in the sky. The printer beeped. "That was fun," said the printer. Leo laughed. The plane flew higher and higher. It landed far away. Leo watched until the plane disappeared. Then Leo went back to the bench. He sat next to the old printer. They were friends from that day.

Lena wanted to print a picture of her dog. She pulled the dog out of the basket. The dog wiggled its tail. Lena fed the dog a cookie. Then she pressed the button on the printer. The printer hummed and beeped. A sheet of paper came out. The paper was black. Lena's picture was gone. Only black marks were left. "Oh no," said Lena. The printer beeped again. "I am out of ink," said the printer. "I cannot print anymore." Lena cried a little. Her mom came with a new ink box. She put it into the printer. The printer hummed again. A fresh sheet of paper came out. Lena drew a picture of her dog. The dog had brown fur and a wagging tail. The picture was beautiful. Lena hugged the paper. The printer beeped once more. It was ready for her next picture.

Once upon a time, the sun was shining and the table was full of paper. The paper was all white.

A girl named Mia came to the table with a big marker. She wanted to make a thank-you note for her friend.

She wrote kind words on the paper. "Thank you for playing with me," she wrote. Then she asked her friend Leo if he could print it.

Leo turned on the printer. It began to hum and beep. "Beep beep," it said. It put the paper into its mouth and started to print.

The paper came out in a fun shape. It had a silly grin on it. Everyone smiled.

"That is so nice," Leo said. The thank-you note was ready!

Once upon a time, there was a little drop of ink named Ray. Ray was an egg of ink.

Ray wanted to find new friends. He found a frog named Frog sitting on a lily pad.

"Hi, I am Ray," said the little ink drop.

"Hi, Ray," said Frog. "You are funny."

Frog liked to hop across the water. Ray wanted to hop too, but he was small and tricky. He was careful as he hopped.

"Can you come with me?" asked Frog.

"Yes!" said Ray.

They hopped over lily pads and cattails. Then they saw the sun. They printed a picture of the sun with the frog and the ink drop.

"Look," said Frog. "It is so bright. Thank you, Ray."

Once upon a time, the sun was up and the table was near a window. A happy dog sat by the table.

His name was Sam. Sam dropped his cookie near the printer. The cookie fell right onto the printer.

The printer began to make loud sounds. "Hmm hmm hmm," it said. The cookie made the machine very grumpy.

"What is wrong?" asked Sam.

"I am upset," said the printer. "This cookie is too big. It broke my paper tray."

Sam felt bad. He sat down and took the cookie away. He said sorry. "I am sorry. Please try again."

The printer wiped its mouth and tried again. It printed a picture of the sun, just like before.

The printer felt better. "Thank you, Sam," it said softly.

One day, Bo wanted to print a picture of a teddy bear. He put the paper into the printer and hit the button.

The printer hummed. It put the paper inside and began to print. But something was wrong. The printer was cold.

"No, no, no!" said Bo. The printer did not stop printing. It kept going and going.

The paper kept coming out. Bo got angry. He pulled the paper out with his hand.

"Oops," said Bo. The paper was blank. There was nothing on it.

Bo felt sad. He looked at the empty paper. Then he thought about his teddy bear. He did not need a picture of a bear. He needed a paper bag.

He went to get crayons. He colored brown circles for the teddy's body. Then he drew a bear face.

It was round and soft. Bo smiled. He had a great time drawing by hand!

Once upon a time, a soccer ball was lying on the grass. A small horse stood next to it.

The horse's name was Ma. Ma wanted to print a menu for a pretend restaurant.

"Help me print," said Ma.

The horse pulled the paper toward the printer. The printer began to beep.

But the paper was upside down! The printer did not know what to do.

"Stop!" said the horse. "Why are you doing that?"

"I am trying to print," said the printer. "But my paper is upside down. I cannot print right."

Ma looked at the paper. She turned it around. Then she pulled it back to the printer.

The printer printed the menu all right. It had words and pictures for food.

"Yum," said the soccer ball. "This looks good."

Once upon a time, a cat was sleeping on a house near the table. A small boy sat next to the printer.

His name was Pete. Pete wanted to print a picture for his cat.

"Open please," said Pete.

He put the paper into the printer and hit the button. The printer opened its mouth and took the paper.

But the printer only had blue ink. It could not print in any other color.

"That is too bad," said Pete. He looked at the printer. "Why is it always blue?"

The cat woke up and opened one eye. "Hello," said the cat. "My house is blue."

Pete looked at the blank paper. He felt sad. The printer could not print green or red. Only blue.

Then Pete had an idea. He picked up some blue paint. He painted the blank paper blue.

He drew little stars and a moon. He drew the cat sitting on the blue house.

"Look," said Pete. "My cat lives here now."

The cat purred happily. "Thank you, Pete," said the cat.

Ben had a teddy bear named Dotty. Dotty was very soft and cuddly. One morning Ben took Dotty outside to play. Ben found a piece of paper with a picture on it. It was soft and long, like a ribbon. Ben tried to push the paper toward Dotty but Dotty did not want it. Dotty wanted to run after a ball instead. Ben pushed the paper one more time and it went very fast. It rolled away across the yard. "Oh no!" said Ben. He ran after the paper but he could not catch it. The paper flew into the bushes. Ben looked sad for a little while. Then he heard a bark. A puppy came bounding out with the paper in his mouth. "Thank you," said Ben, hugging his teddy bear. That was the best day ever.

Once upon a time there was a frog who lived by a park. The park had a long path and many trees. One hot day the frog wanted to print signs for a lemonade stand. He went to a machine that made signs and asked it to print two signs. The machine hummed and beeped and printed the first sign. But then the frog looked at the second sign and it looked funny. The words were backwards and the letters were upside down. "That is silly," said the frog. "I cannot sell lemonade with that sign." The frog sat down on a log and felt sad. A little bird flew down and said, "I will help you fix it." Together they bent the paper flat and wrote new words. The frog printed the signs again. Now they were right side up and looked perfect. People walked by and smiled. "Thank you," said the frog. Selling lemonade was fun again.

One day a cat named Whiskers wanted to print a nice picture for her grandma. Her grandma lived far away. Whiskers sat at her little table and fed paper into the machine. The machine hummed and printed a beautiful picture of a flower garden. Whiskers put the picture in a basket. Then she called her grandma on the phone. "Grandma, here is your picture," said Whiskers. Grandma opened the basket and held the picture up to the light. She smiled so big. "This is the most careful picture I have ever seen," said Grandma. Whiskers purred. She loved printing pictures for her grandma. Every week Whiskers printed something new and sent it through the basket. Grandma always said thank you. It was the best thing Whiskers ever did.

An apple sat on a table next to a small printer. The apple was round and red and shiny. One day the apple said, "I would like to print a big picture of myself." The small printer was too small. It could only print tiny pictures. It tried to shake the apple to make room but the apple would not move. "I am too big," said the apple. The apple sat down on the table and felt hungry for something. The wind blew outside and shook the table gently. That shook the small printer. Suddenly the printer was bigger! The apple was surprised. "How did you get bigger?" said the apple. The printer beeped. "I did not get bigger. I just finally ate enough paper to grow." The apple laughed. Now the printer could print a big picture of the apple. Everyone was happy. But the apple still felt hungry sometimes.

One afternoon Mom was sitting at the table reading a crumpled piece of paper. The paper was all folded and creased and torn. It made her feel heavy inside. "This paper is full of sad thoughts," said Mom. She wanted to read it again but the paper was too messy. A small cat named Mittens came and jumped onto the table. Mittens saw the crumpled paper and poked it with her paw. Then she jumped off. Suddenly the wind blew from the window and shook the whole table. The paper jumped up in the air. It landed flat on the table again. It was smooth and neat. "Oh!" said Mom. She picked up the paper and smoothed it out. All the sad lines were gone now. It was a picture of flowers. "This is much better," said Mom. She looked at the flowers and felt happy. Mittens hopped onto the chair and licked Mom's hand. It was a good day for reading.

Once upon a time, a tired printer sat on the table. It hummed and beeped but could not print. "I am too tired," said the printer. A red car rolled by on the road. The car looked at the printer. "Can you print my picture for me?" asked the car. The printer shook its head. "I need rest," said the printer. The car waited quietly. After a while, the printer felt better. It took a piece of paper and printed the picture of the car. The car was happy. "Thank you, kind printer," said the car. Then the printer closed its eyes and took a nap.

Noah wanted to print a sunny picture. But it was rainy outside. Noah stood by the window and watched the rain. He looked at his paper. "I cannot find the sun," Noah said. The printer sat on the table. Noah put a blank paper into the printer. "Please print the sunny picture," said Noah. The printer hummed and began to work. It printed a bright yellow circle. It added green grass and blue clouds around it. Noah smiled. "Look at this!" He walked to the printer and showed the paper to his mom. His mom laughed. "You made your own sun on paper." Noah held up the paper and walked outside into the rain. The rain felt cool on his cheeks. He had a yellow sun in his hands and water drops on his coat.

Once upon a time, Noah had a pet dog named Biscuit. Biscuit was very messy. He spilled paint all over the floor. Noah wanted to print a picture of Biscuit. Noah found some paper in the drawer. He put the paper into the printer. "Please print a picture of Biscuit," said Noah. The printer hummed and printed a fuzzy brown dog. But then something went wrong. The printer printed one more picture, and that picture was not a dog at all. It was a messy picture of paint puddles. Noah frowned. "No, I want a picture of Biscuit." Noah looked at the bad picture. The printer seemed sad. "I am sorry," whispered the printer. Noah picked up the bad picture. "Don't worry, printer," said Noah. "I will draw my own picture of Biscuit." Noah found crayons and drew a fuzzy brown dog with a big tongue out. The printer helped again later and printed a clean picture of Biscuit on white paper. Everyone was happy.

A cat named Whiskers sat on top of the printer. She watched the machine print. But every time the printer took a new sheet, it printed the same word: "cat." "Why do you keep printing cat?" Whiskers asked. The printer did not answer. It just beeped and printed "cat" again and again. Whiskers walked down from the table. She walked along the table and looked at the stack of papers. Each paper had only one word on it, and each word was "cat." Whiskers got tired of looking. "This is silly," she said. She walked to the river beside the house. She jumped into the water. The water was warm. She floated on her back. The warm river carried her gently. The sun rose above the trees. Light touched her fur. She purred. She was happy near the river. Then she saw a bird fly across the sky. She watched the bird fly away. Everything was fine. She walked back home with her tail high. The next day, the printer still printed "cat," but Whiskers did not mind. She liked being near the warm river.

Once upon a time, a bright sun shone in the window. It made the whole room feel warm. The printer sat under the sun. But when the sun went away, the room became dark. "Oh no," whispered the printer. The dark office scared the printer. "I do not like the dark," said the printer. A little girl named Lily heard the printer cry. Lily turned on the lamp. The lamp made a bright circle of light on the table. "It is okay now," said Lily. "The lamp is my friend." The printer felt safe. It hummed happily under the bright lamp. When the sun came back, Lily turned the lamp off. The printer said, "Thank you, Lily." The sun gave the room light again. The printer was not afraid anymore. Lily learned that even machines need light when it is dark. And when the sun comes back, everything feels warm and bright again.

A little boy named Tim wanted a bird for his treehouse. He went to the printer and said, "Print me a bird." The printer hummed and printed a paper bird. Tim hung it on the tree branch outside. The next day, Tim went outside to play. A strong wind blew. The paper bird flew away! Tim ran inside and told his mom. "My bird is gone!" his mom said. Tim looked at the empty tree branch. "I want another bird," said Tim. His mom said, "Let's build a real bird from sticks." Tim and his mom went outside together. They found soft twigs in the yard. Tim's mom helped him build a nest in the tree. They stuck small twigs together to make a strong shape. Tim added leaves and string. Finally, they made a tiny bird with a paper triangle for a wing. It was not a perfect picture, but it worked. The bird sat on the twig nest and chirped. Tim smiled. He learned that a paper bird can fly away, but a real bird stays if you build it well.

Once upon a time, a hen stepped into a kitchen. It rained outside. The hen was not neat. She stepped in a puddle and her feathers got wet. She waddled to the table. A little boy was at the table. He had a calculator on the table. "I want to print my picture," he said. "I will use the printer," said the boy. He put paper in the printer. The paper was wet. The printer tried to print. But the paper was wet. The picture came out all blurry. The boy looked at the picture. "It is not good," he said. Then the hen stepped out of the kitchen. She shook her wet feathers dry. "I am dry now," said the hen. The boy put dry paper in the printer. The picture came out neat. "Now I can print again!" he said.

A plant grew by a big machine. The machine was a printer. One day, the printer kept printing pages. It printed pages for many hours. No one told it to stop. The printer would not stop printing. It took paper in, and it gave paper out. A small bird sat on top of the machine. "Please stop," said the bird. "I cannot stop," said the printer. "I do not want to stop." The bird flew away and came back with a big stick. The bird poked the printer. "Why are you still printing?" said the bird. "I do not know why," said the printer. "I just keep printing. I feel lonely." The bird made the printer stop. "I will help you," said the bird. Now they are friends. They sit together and wait for someone to tell them what to print next.

A dog sat by a happy printer. The dog had a fun game planned. He wanted to play a joke game with his friends. He asked the printer to print funny jokes. "Print one joke for me," said the dog. The printer hummed and beeped. It took paper. It printed a joke. The dog read the joke. "Ha ha!" said the dog. He looked around. His friends were coming to play. But the printer did something strange. It printed another joke. And another joke! The jokes were silly and funny. The dog laughed out loud. "This is the best game ever," said the dog. He hugged the printer. "Thank you," he said. Now every day, the dog asks the printer for silly jokes. They play a joke game every single time.

An old printer sat by a window. It was very slow. A bird landed on the edge of the printer. "Hello," said the bird. "My nest needs materials. Can you help me print?" The old printer was sad. "I am too slow," it said. "I take so long to print one page." The bird waited. Time went by. The bird grew hungry. "I must go find food," said the bird. The bird left. The old printer tried again. It took in paper. It pulled the paper. But it moved so slowly. The bird came back. "I am still waiting," said the bird. The old printer tried once more. Finally, after a long time, it printed a small leaf. The bird ate the leaf. "Thank you," said the bird. The old printer felt better. Now it prints a leaf for the bird every morning.

A rabbit was sad. Its friend, the printer, was broken. The printer could not print. "I am lonely," said the printer. The rabbit wanted to help. "I can fix you," said the rabbit. The rabbit found some glue. The rabbit found a new wire. The rabbit sat by the broken printer. "Hold still," said the rabbit. The rabbit fixed the wire. The rabbit put on the glue. The printer hummed. Beep. Hum. Beep. The light on top turned green. "You fixed me!" said the printer. "Yes," said the rabbit. "I am glad I can fix you." The printer worked again. It printed a new picture. "Look!" said the rabbit. "You are working well now." The printer beeped happily. They are the best of friends.

Jack sat by a quiet printer. The printer had a blinking light. It blinked red, then red, then red. Jack did not like the blinking. "The light makes me sad," said Jack. "Why does it blink?" he asked. The printer did not answer. Jack picked up a soccer ball. He kicked the ball near the printer. The ball rolled into the printer. The printer did not mind. It printed the soccer ball right on top of the rolling ball. "What is this?" said Jack. "It is my soccer ball," said the printer. Jack looked at the print. It was perfect! "You are the best helper," said Jack. He gave the printer a hug. The blinking light went green. "Thank you," said the printer. Now Jack always brings his soccer ball to the printer so they can play together.

Once upon a time, Sue sat on the chair and looked at her little brother. He was too sleepy to sleep. "I want a story," she said. "Please," he said. Sue took a piece of paper and put it in the printer. She pressed a button. The printer hummed and made a sound. Out came a big page with a picture of a flower and words that said: "The sun went to bed." Sue read the words out loud. They were funny words, and her brother laughed. Then the sun picture blinked twice. His eyes got heavy. He closed them and went to sleep. Sue picked up the paper and tucked it under his pillow. Goodnight, little brother. Goodnight, sun.

Tom sat on the chair and felt bored. He wanted to go float in water. He found a piece of printed paper on the floor. It had a picture of a light bulb on it. Tom folded the paper into a boat. He used glue on the edges so the boat would hold water. Then he put it in the tub. The boat went out, out, out! Tom clapped his hands. He was happy. But soon the boat tipped over. Water came in. The paper was wet. Tom pulled it out and dried it with a towel. Then he made another boat. This one floated better. Tom smiled.

It was a cold morning. Frost sat on every window. Anna sat near the printer because she did not want to walk far. The printer hummed. Warm paper came out of the printer. It was soft and wet. Anna held it against her cold hand. It felt nice. On the paper was a picture of a bird sitting on a branch. She saw the bird and felt sad. "Oh no," Anna said. "I dropped my warm towel. Now I am cold." The bird picture did not move. It just sat there, still and quiet. Anna wrapped herself in the warm paper and sat by the window. The bird flew away at last.

Mia wanted to have a party for her friends. She needed cards to give to each friend. She took a piece of paper and put it in the printer. She typed the words: "You are invited to a party." The printer made the cards. Mia gave one card to each friend. Her friend Leo arrived with something in his hands. "What is this?" Mia asked. Leo opened a box. Inside were two calculators! "They are gifts for you and your friends," Leo said. Mia hugged him and said thank you. Everyone laughed. The party was fun. The cards were strong and could not tear. The calculators worked too. All the friends were happy.

Hen sat beside the printer. "Can you draw?" Hen asked. The printer said, "I try, but I only print. I cannot draw like you do." Hen was hungry, but she kept looking at the printer. She wanted to race. She wanted to make pretty pictures fast. The printer tried to draw. But the lines were all the same. Hen clapped her hands. "Not good enough," she said. Then Hen picked up a crayon from the table. She drew a picture of a hen with a long neck. The printer saw the picture and began to print more details. Now the pictures were beautiful. Hen ate her apple and felt proud. She did not need to race anymore. She just needed to be happy.

A robot named Robby lived next to the printer. One day the printer made a wrong sound and stopped. It would not print anything. A cat named Mittie saw this and was worried. "What can we do?" Mittie said. Robby came over. "Let me look," he said. He turned small parts inside the printer with careful hands. He found a tiny piece that was stuck. He clapped his hands together and pushed it free. The printer hummed again. Paper came out. Mittie purred with joy. "You are my hero," she said. Robby smiled. "We fixed it together."

Nick sat behind the office printer. The mouse liked hiding there because it was warm. One day Nick's mom said, "We need a picture of a bike for the school." Nick looked at the printer and said, "OK!" He put paper in the tray. The printer hummed and hummed. Then it printed the picture. The picture showed a bike with two round wheels. Nick smiled. The mouse behind the printer could fly away to look at the nice bike picture. Nick put it on the wall. The mouse was happy too.

Sara came to work with her dog, Biscuit. Biscuit was an ugly dog with spots. Sara wanted to print a photo of her dog so she could show everyone. She put paper in the tray and pressed the button. But nothing came out! Sara pulled the paper tray out and saw a big bowl inside. The bowl was empty. "Oh no," said Sara. There was no paper at all. Biscuit ran after the empty bowl. The printer beeped sadly. Sara sat down and cried a little. But then she found a small piece of paper in the tray. She put it in the machine and printed the picture of Biscuit. Now Sara had a good picture to show her friends.
