Jack was a teacher. Jack wanted to print big letters for his students. But the letters were weak and hard to read. Jack said, "I cannot see the words well." The sun was shining outside the window. Jack felt tired and weak. His friend Tom walked by and said, "Let me help." Tom took the paper tray out and added more paper. He pressed the button again. The printer worked hard and made strong letters. "Thank you, Tom," said Jack. Now every student in the class could read the letters. Jack smiled. The sun was bright again. Jack felt better and taught his lesson with joy.

Ray wanted to print a story to read before bed. His mother said, "Read me a story tonight." Ray found the printer and put paper inside. He pressed the button. The machine started to print. But the pages were sticky. The ink stuck together and the pages were hard to turn. Ray tried to pull the pages apart but they would not separate. "Oh dear," said Ray. He could not read his story. Ray's mother laughed and said, "It is just a little cake print." She cut the sticky page into tiny pieces. Ray used the pieces to make a funny hat. He put it on his head and sang a song. His mother was happy that he did not stay up late.

Sue collected old papers from the classroom. Some were used for drawing, some for lists. Sue put them in a big coat bag. She carried the bag to the recycling bin. A worker watched Sue carry the bag. "What are you bringing?" asked the worker. "Old paper," said Sue. "We can reuse it," the worker said happily. They took the old paper to a factory. The factory made new things from the paper. Sue came back the next day with clean, fresh paper. The classroom had new paper again. Sue smiled. The old paper was not trash anymore. It became new paper. Everything was clean and ready to print.

The soccer ball rolled into the room. It bounced and hit the printer's table. The ball rolled under the printer. A boy named Leo wanted to print a drawing of the soccer ball. But the paper tray was empty. Leo watched under the machine. He saw the soccer ball sitting there. "Look, it is in my way," said Leo. He pushed the ball gently out. Then he put paper in the tray and pressed the button. The printer started printing. But something went wrong. The printer kept printing over and over. Pages flew out everywhere. Leo tried to stop it but he could not. Pages piled on the floor, on the bed, on the desk. Finally the machine stopped. Leo picked up all the pages and threw them in a bucket. Now the room was clean. The soccer ball was safe. Leo learned to be careful with the printer.

Once upon a time, a bird flew into a house. The bird sat on the new printer. "Hello," said the bird. "I want to sit here." The family was happy. They brought a big box to the table. The box had a machine inside. "This is my new friend," said the mother. The bird liked it. The father turned on the printer. It hummed and beeped. It printed a picture of the bird. The bird was brave and sat still. Everyone smiled. The bird was happy too.

A little girl had an old desk. On the desk, there were stacks of paper. The paper was torn and broken. "I can't use this," said the girl. She put the paper in a bin. Then she gave the bin to her mom. "What will you do with it?" asked her mom. "I think I can make new paper," said the girl. Her mom was calm. "You are right," said her mom. Her mom cut the old paper into tiny pieces. She mixed it with water. Then she pressed it flat. The girl watched closely. Soon there was fresh paper. They printed a card for the bird. The bird loved the card. The girl learned that old things can become new things.

It was a bright morning at the office. People came and went all day. The office printer was very busy. It printed many pages. It got very warm. Then it made a loud noise. A soft blanket came out of the printer. It covered the whole machine! The printer could not work well. A man looked worried. "What happened?" he asked. His helper ran over. "It just needs rest," she said. She lifted the blanket off slowly. The printer hummed again. "Thank you," said the man. He kept the printer quiet for a while. Later, everything worked again. The office was calm once more. The printer helped everyone that afternoon.

At school, the children wanted nice pictures for their class board. The teacher brought the printer to the classroom. "Who wants to print a picture?" asked the teacher. Many hands went up. First, the boy printed a horse. The girl printed a flower. Then the teddy bear raised its hand. "I want to print a teddy bear," said the teddy bear. The teacher helped the teddy bear press the button. The printer hummed. But something strange happened. The paper came out full of ink spots. It did not look like a teddy bear. "Oh no," said the teddy bear. The children laughed. Then one girl said, "We can fix it." They wiped the paper clean with a wet cloth. After that, the paper became clear again. They printed a beautiful teddy bear. The teddy bear felt happy.

A new printer came to a small shop. Nobody had given it a name yet. "What should we call him?" asked the shopkeeper. A light bulb floated above the table. "Let me think," said the light bulb. "How about Bob?" suggested the light bulb. Everyone laughed. "That is a round name," said the shopkeeper. "Bob is round," said the light bulb. So they named the printer Bob. Bob was a round machine. He hummed and beeped every day. He printed receipts and bags for the shop. One day, the shop closed early. The owner locked the door and went home. Bob stood alone in the dark shop. He did not know what to do. He waited by the window. At night, the streetlights lit up the road. A car drove past. Bob saw the lights. He felt sad for a moment. Then he heard a small laugh from outside. A child was playing nearby. Bob felt better. He knew he would see people again soon.

Behind the big office printer lived a mouse. The mouse was small and warm. Every day, the mouse peeked out to see who needed printing. One busy morning, the mouse saw a man walk in. The man came to the printer. He put paper in and pushed a button. The printer started to hum. The mouse was scared. He hid behind a wire. Then the paper came out with a funny smell. The mouse did not like the smell. He shook his head. "No, no," he said. He wanted to jump away but he could not move fast. He bumped his back on a hot part of the printer. "Ouch!" he squeaked. Then the paper had ink on it. It was all spotted and brown. The mouse looked at the paper. It made him think of the dark sea. He wanted to swim in the ink. But the ink was cold. The mouse jumped away. He found a crack between two machines. He was safe there. The man noticed the mouse later. He gave the mouse a piece of cheese. The mouse ate it and stayed warm behind the printer.

Max had a teddy bear at home. Max wanted to print a big picture of the park. He put the picture into the printer. The printer was too small. It could not fit the whole picture. The printer got mad. "I cannot do it," it said in a whirr. Max felt sad too. Then he took the picture out. He cut it in half. He put one half in the printer. The printer printed one part. Max printed both halves. Now he had the whole park picture!

A house had a window near its printer. The house wanted to see outside. So the house asked the printer to print a bird. The printer tried. But the bird could not fit on the page. The bird was too big for the window. The printer made a sad sound. It did not print the bird. Outside, the sky was orange. The house looked out. A real orange fish swam in the water. The house was glad it could see the fish without a picture.

Mike had a printer in his new room. The room was cold. Snow fell outside the window. Mike wanted to print a drawing of snow. He put the paper in the printer. But the printer was short. The paper stuck at the bottom. The printer could not reach the top. Mike felt frustrated. He took the paper out. He folded the paper. Then he taped it to the top of the machine. The printer reached the paper. It printed a big snowman. Mike was happy again!

At school, the duck wanted to write a letter. She asked the teacher for paper. The teacher gave her a dark page. The duck wrote her name on it. Then she wanted to print her drawing. She put the paper in the printer. The printer beeped too loudly. It scared all the other animals. They hid under their desks. The duck felt sad. She took the paper out quietly. She drew her picture by hand. No more loud beeps. The duck felt better and proud of her work.

Ivy had a cat. The cat was orange and soft. Ivy wanted to print a picture of the cat so her mom could see it. Ivy pulled the paper into the printer. She pressed the button. The printer hummed and beeped. It took the paper in and printed out the picture. Ivy held the picture up. "Look, Mom! A cat!" Her mom smiled. The cat was happy to be in the picture. Ivy gave the cat a small treat from the kitchen. The cat drank some milk. Then Ivy set the picture on the table for everyone to see.

Sara's office was big and quiet at night. The lights were off. Sara had a printer on her desk. The printer did not like the dark. "I wish it were daytime," the printer said. Sara patted the machine. "It is okay," she said. The printer tried to print a story. But it was too hard. The machine beeped many times and made a sad sound. It could not see the words. Sara turned the light on. The printer printed the story all by itself. The next day, the printer printed a picture of the moon and stars. The printer felt better.

On Saturday, the printer sat alone on the table. No one used it. A duck sat under the desk. "I will take your paper today," the duck said. The printer shook its head. "No, thank you," it said. The duck was still hungry and wanted a cookie. The printer did not have any cookie either. So the duck took a paper from the tray. Then the printer took the paper back. They both looked at the paper. It was just one piece of dry paper. The duck said, "That is not much fun." The printer tried to print a funny face. But the ink was too dry. The picture came out blank. They sat together and waited for someone to come.

A teddy bear sat next to the printer. "What should I call you?" the teddy bear asked. The printer thought about it. "I am scared," the printer said. "The dark is scary." The teddy bear had a name. "My name is Fluff," the teddy bear said. "Then I will call you Puff." The printer was happy. "Puff is a good name." Puff printed a picture of the teddy bear and the desk. The teddy bear smiled. "Thank you, Puff," said the teddy bear. From that day, the printer had a name. And the teddy bear was not scared anymore. They were friends, and they printed pictures together every day.

Nina wanted to open a pretend restaurant. She needed a menu so people could know what to eat. Nina put the blank paper into the printer. She typed the names of the foods. "Apple pie. Fish soup. Bread and butter." The printer hummed and printed the menu. It was very tiny. Nina held the menu close to her eyes. Everything was small but clear. Then she heard a bell ring outside. A friend was coming to visit! Nina hung the menu on the wall. She rang the bell again. The friend walked in and saw the menu. "This looks great!" the friend said. Nina smiled and printed another menu for the next day.

Ray wanted to throw a party. He needed invitations for his friends. Ray put white paper into the printer. He wrote the party details on each page. Then he pressed the button. The printer started to hum. But the paper jammed. The printer stopped. Ray had to pull the paper out carefully. He tried again. The printer worked this time. But the ink was wrong. It printed on all the pages in blue. "Oh no," Ray said. His friends would not come. That was a bad day. Ray took the blue pages home. He mixed fresh ink with water. Then he printed new invitations. Everyone came to the park. The park was full of friends and fun. Ray learned that printing right the first time makes the party better.

Once upon a time, it was winter and snow was falling outside. Anna wanted to print out a picture of a light bulb so she could hang it near the window. She sat down and pressed the button. The printer hummed and took a piece of paper. But the printer did not stop. It kept printing. And printing. And printing. Anna pulled her hand away. The printer beeped loud and loud. A big orange snowflake fell on her head. She cried a little. Then she picked up the paper. It had a tiny light bulb on it, but the rest was just blank white paper. The printer took another piece of paper and went beep beep beep. Anna sighed. She knew what to do now. She took the blank paper and drew her own light bulb with a bright yellow circle on top. It was not perfect, but it was hers. The printer went beep and printed one more little star. That was okay too.

A little dog named Biscuit heard his owner say, "We need to print a treasure map." So Biscuit ran to the printer and waited. Anna pressed the button. The printer took a long piece of paper. It printed a map with a big river on it. Biscuit sniffed the paper. "This map goes far," he said. He walked to the window and looked out. The sun was bright. Anna looked at the map. The map showed a tall mountain in the far corner. But Biscuit did not see any mountains. He saw only grass and trees. "Where is the mountain?" Biscuit barked. Anna looked again. There was no mountain. Only more grass. The map was wrong. Or maybe there was no treasure at all. They both sat down and tried to find the tall mountain. It was nowhere to be seen. They did not find any gold. They just found some mud puddles. It was sad. But they still had the map, and that was something.

Max wanted to press the print button. His friend Sam said, "No, you are too little." Max sat on the bench and pouted. He wanted to print a drawing. Sam walked away. Max looked at the big button. It was green and round. He blinked once. He blinked twice. Slowly he reached his hand down. He touched the button. It went goo goo goo. The printer took a piece of paper and started to print. Max held his breath. The printer made a soft sound. Then it pulled out a beautiful drawing of a cat holding a ball. Max jumped up and down. "Yay!" he said. "You can press it, Max," Sam called from across the room. Max looked at Sam. Sam blinked big happy eyes. Max smiled. Now Sam wanted to press the button too. They both printed pictures together. Sam printed a funny face. Max printed a rocket ship. They hung them on the wall. Everyone clapped. Max did not feel mean or sad anymore. He felt happy. The button was his to press after all.

Beep was a printer. Beep also had a friend, Scan. Scan was a scanner. They sat side by side on the desk. One day Beep said, "I want to read a car book." Scan said, "I can help." So Scan scanned a picture of a cool red car. Beep took the picture and printed it. Then Beep said, "I want to read an apple book." Scan scanned an apple picture. Beep printed the apple. They both liked reading the books. But then Beep said, "I want to read a story about a boat." Scan scanned a boat. Beep printed the boat. Now Beep had a lot of paper. Scan had nothing to print. Scan felt left out. "I cannot print," Scan said quietly. Beep looked at Scan. "What if I print for you?" Beep said. So Beep printed a picture of Scan sitting on a chair. Scan smiled. From then on, they helped each other. Beep printed for Scan, and Scan read stories for Beep. They were best friends forever.

Kim heard a loud beep. It was the printer. It beeped beep beep beep beep. The sound was too fast. Kim looked around. Her friend Leo was walking by. "Is the printer okay?" Kim asked. "No," Leo said. "The printer is broken." Kim went to the printer. It was making a very loud noise. The light on top was blinking fast. Kim reached her hand up close. The beep beep beep was so loud it made her eyes blink. Kim did not cry. She did not yell. She just wanted the printer to stop. She pressed the button gently. The printer stopped. Then it made a quiet little sound. "I will answer you later," Kim said softly. She turned the machine over. She found a small screw and took it out. She put a new light bulb inside. The printer hummed nicely. Now it worked well. Kim printed a picture of a cat on a sunny mat. "Here," Kim said. "I hope this makes you feel better." Leo came closer. "Thank you, Kim," he said. The cat picture was very nice. They sat together and looked at the picture. The printer was good again.

Once upon a time, there was a printer named Priya. Priya could only print in one color - blue. A red car was parked on the road outside. The car wanted to be printed too, but the car is red, and Priya only knows blue. So Priya said, "I cannot print you, car. I can only print blue things."

The car felt sad and drove away down the road.

Priya did not feel sad at all. She liked printing blue pictures all day long. She printed blue birds flying and blue rivers running. Every day was fun for Priya.

One morning, a blue fish swam up to the door. "Can you print me?" the fish asked.

Priya took a sheet of paper. "Yes," she said, and printed a picture of the fish.

The fish smiled. "Thank you," it said.

Priya beeped happily. She could only print blue, but that was just fine. Blue was a good color for Priya.

Once upon a time, there was a printer named Pip and a scanner named Sam. They were best friends. They sat on the same table every day. Pip hummed and beeped. Sam clicked and whirred.

One day, Sam wished they could play together more. Sam said, "Pip, wish we could run around like animals!"

"I wish," Pip said. "But I am a printer. I do not know how to run."

So Sam tried. Sam clicked and whirred and went zooming off the table. Pip watched and said, "That is silly. I stay here and print papers."

Sam came back. Sam was out of breath. "That was silly," Sam agreed. "But I had fun anyway."

From then on, Pip and Sam sat together. They printed drawings and scanned letters. Being best friends was better than running around. They were happy.

It was late at night. All the people in the office went home. But Mr Printer stayed. He sat on his table with his machine still on. He wanted to print something special.

There was a little cake on the desk near him. The cake was pink. It was shaped like a tall tower.

Mr Printer looked at the cake. "I will print a cake," he said quietly.

He fed a piece of paper into his mouth. He pulled. He pushed. He printed. The paper came out looking flat and plain.

It was not a real cake. It was just paper.

Mr Printer put the paper down. It was sad. No one would eat it. No one would smile at it.

Then his mom came in through the door. "What are you doing, dear?" she asked.

"Printing a cake," Mr Printer said.

His mom picked up the paper. "Oh," she said. "It's just paper. Why did you print it?"

Mr Printer looked at his empty hands. "I wanted to make someone smile," he said softly.

His mom hugged him. "That is enough," she said. "Sometimes printing makes us happy even when nothing comes out right."

Mr Printer beeped softly and rested his head on the table.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny robot named Roxy. Roxy loved printers. Her favorite thing was fixing broken printers.

A big old printer sat in the shop. The paper tray was stuck. The buttons did not work. nobody could fix it.

Roxy hopped over. She said, "Don't worry. I will fix you."

She opened the small box under the printer. Inside was a map. The map showed how all the wires fit together.

Roxy found the broken wire. She said, "I can send you a new wire." She fixed the tray. She pressed all the buttons.

The printer hummed. Paper came out. A nice drawing appeared on the page.

Everyone cheered. "Roxy did it!" they said.

Roxy smiled. She had made a printer happy again. And she was glad.

Once upon a time, there was a printer named Cleo. Cleo wanted to draw like a crayon. Crayons made pretty pictures with bright colors. But Cleo only had black ink.

Cleo tried. She printed black lines on white paper. The lines were flat and plain. They did not look like pretty pictures.

Cleo sat down. "I wish I could draw like a crayon," she said.

A bird landed on her table. The bird was colorful - red and orange and yellow.

"Hello," said the bird. "I can draw."

Cleo looked at the bird. "How?"

The bird flapped its wings. The bird left little marks on the paper. Red marks. Orange marks. Yellow marks.

"Wow," Cleo said. "You can draw all those colors."

The bird said, "I use my body to draw. You can try too."

So Cleo tried. She printed one line, then another. One day, her prints started to look like real pictures. Not perfect pictures, but pretty.

Cleo learned something new. Being a printer is fine, but you can also try being creative. Sometimes, the best ideas come from trying hard.

Once upon a time, there was a printer named Sunny. Sunny lived in a small room. Sunny was happy most of the time. People came to her and asked her to print letters and pictures.

One day, Sunny stopped working. She could not print anything. Papers came out blank.

People were sad. They came to ask why. "Something is wrong," they said.

Sunny felt very bad inside. She could not help anyone.

A kind mechanic named Tom heard about it. Tom came to the room. He looked at Sunny carefully.

"I see what is wrong," Tom said.

He found a small bolt that was loose. He tightened it. Then he cleaned the inside of Sunny very well.

Sunny felt warm again. She hummed. She beeped. She pulled out paper with pictures on it.

"Thank you, Tom," Sunny said.

Tom smiled and walked away.

Sunny was glad. She was fixed again. She could print letters and pictures for everyone.

Tom said, "Good job, Sunny. You will be helpful again."

Sunny beeped happily. She was glad to be fixed. She could help people once more.

Once upon a time, a new printer woke up on the table. It was so scared. It did not know what to print. A little card came out, but it was blank and empty. The printer beeped. "I need paper," it said softly. Paper ran out. Then a little card came with one tiny dot on it. "Is that all?" the printer asked. It felt happy now. It printed one line of black ink. That was the very first page ever printed by this machine. A small smile grew on its face. It hummed a quiet song. The little card sat on the table, smiling too.

Noah drew an apple on a big piece of paper. He wanted to see his apple print. He took the paper to the printer and pressed a button. "Print!" he said. The printer hummed. It took the paper and printed his drawing. There was his apple, red and round, right there on the page. Noah clapped his hands. "Look, I can see my apple!" He smiled from ear to ear. His mom saw the picture too. She said, "That is wonderful, Noah." Noah felt proud. He learned that if you try hard, you can print your drawings for everyone to see. A happy ending for Noah.

A puppy named Bumpy found a sticky piece of paper on the floor. "What is this?" he barked. It was a printed page from the printer. Bumpy sniffed it and gave a funny sneeze. Then he raced after a ball. While running, Bumpy tripped and the sticky paper flew into the air. He caught it in his mouth! He ran fast back to his bed. But his legs were tired now. "Oh no," he whined. The paper was still stuck to his tongue. He licked it. "Yuck!" He learned that you should not run off with printed paper because it can make you feel bad.

A family got a new printer for their home. It was a nice, friendly box. Dad held the printer and placed it on the table. Mom pressed a big button. "Cook your food," she said, laughing. "I am just making a test page," the printer said. It hummed and printed. The page came out perfectly. Everyone clapped. The kids thought the printer was nice. They named it Cookie. Every day, the kids would print pictures and cards. They learned that a new machine can bring joy to a home if you use it kindly. A nice lesson for the whole family.

Old Mr. Printer was very slow. He took forever to print anything. One game day, little Tim wanted to play. Tim sat near the printer and waited. The printer hummed and beeped but did not finish. "When will it be done?" Tim asked. Mr. Printer did not answer. He was too slow. Tim got bored. He walked away to play his own game. Mr. Printer sat there, quiet and light in weight. No one used him anymore. He felt sad inside. He wanted someone to ask him to print, even if it took a long time. He just wanted to help. A gentle sad ending for an old, slow friend.

Jill wanted to print a picture of her tree for Grandma. She sat down and pressed the button. "Please, wait," she whispered. The printer started to hum. "I will wait, I will wait," Jill said softly. The printer worked hard. Finally, a beautiful picture came out. There was her tree, green leaves and brown trunk. Jill held the picture up. "Grandma, look!" Grandma smiled. "It is so small and pretty." Jill felt happy. She learned that sometimes you have to wait, but when the printing is done, your hard work becomes real. A small, sweet picture, and a kind lesson for Jill.

Once upon a time, a little dog went missing. A teddy bear sat on the chair and looked very sad. The teddy bear saw a poster on the wall. It was purple and had a picture of a horse on it. The poster said, "Help! I am lost."

The teddy bear wanted to print more posters so everyone could see them. But there was no paper in the printer. The teddy bear put a sheet of paper into the machine and pressed the button.

The printer hummed and hummed. Then it printed! A big purple horse came out of the machine. The teddy bear hung the poster on the tree by the door.

Soon, a little boy saw the poster. He ran outside and found the lost dog. The dog was safe. The teddy bear gave a big hug to the boy. Everyone was happy that day.

Mia wanted to print a picture of an apple for her friend. She put the paper into the printer and pressed the button. "Go," said Mia.

The printer started to print. It made a red apple shape. But then the printer stopped. It did not have any ink left. The printer beeped once and once again.

"Oh no," said Mia. "What will we do?" Mia looked at the paper. It only had part of the apple on it.

Then Mia saw an orange on the table. "I can print the apple with orange!" said Mia. She took the paper back and put it in again.

The printer made a new apple, this time orange. Mia smiled. She gave the orange apple to her friend. Her friend said, "Thank you, Mia!"

A tired printer sat on the desk. It felt very heavy. It wanted to print a picture of a blue fish. But it could not move. It was too tired.

"I need a rest," said the printer. "I cannot work today."

A little girl named Lily heard the printer say these words. She sat next to the printer. "Can you rest while I look for the fish?" asked Lily.

"Yes," said the printer. "Rest now."

Lily looked out the window. She saw a fish swimming in the water. The fish was blue and it was playing.

Lily told the printer all about the fish. The printer listened and felt better. Later, when the printer woke up, Lily asked if it could print a picture of the fish. The printer said yes. It worked all morning and printed a beautiful picture of the blue fish.

It was time for the whole family to have a picture together. Grandpa, grandma, mom, dad, and two kids sat on the carpet. There was an apple on the table too.

Mom said, "Let us print a picture of all of us."

They went to the desk where the printer was. Mom put a big sheet of paper into the printer. Dad held up the camera so the picture would show everyone.

But the printer did not print right away. First, it had to clean itself. Then it printed the picture. All the family was in the picture. Grandpa was laughing. The kids were jumping with joy.

Dad said, "This is a messy but perfect picture." Mom laughed and said, "Yes, let us keep it!" They all clapped their hands. The family was happy together.

Rex was in the busy office. Many people needed the printer. Rex was a big, friendly office printer. He was always working.

First, a man sent a list of papers. Rex printed them. Then a woman sent a form. Rex printed it. Then a boy sent a drawing. Rex printed it.

Rex started to feel tired. His buttons were sticky. His paper tray was full. His ink was running low. He wanted to stop.

But people kept coming. Rex kept printing. Rex felt very sad. He did not want to work anymore.

One last person came up to Rex. "Thank you for all your help today," said the woman. Rex felt a little better.

"You are welcome," said Rex. He printed one last paper. Then he closed his eyes and rested. The office was quiet now. Rex was happy to take a nap.

Once upon a time, a sun wanted to print a picture of itself. It put a piece of paper into the printer. But something was wrong. The paper stuck inside the machine.

The printer did not know what to do. It tried to move, but it could not. The paper was tangled up.

A little girl came running. "Help! Something is stuck!" she said. She grabbed a brush and cleaned out the paper bits from the machine.

She pulled the paper out. Now the printer could work again. It printed a bright yellow sun. The sun was happy and went to play outside.

The little girl looked at the picture of the sun. "You look silly," she said with a smile. The sun said, "Thank you!" And they both had a good day.

Once upon a time there was a little cave. The cave was very small. Little girl named May lived in the cave. One day May wanted to print something. She pressed the big green button on the printer. The printer said beep beep. Then it pulled out a wet sheet of paper. It made a big wet spot on the paper. May shout hooray! She wiped the paper dry with her cloth. Then she printed her drawing of a bear. The bear looked happy on the paper. May hug the paper tight. She loved printing her own things.

Once upon a time there was an empty paper tray. The tray was for paper but there was no paper in it. A frog sat next to the tray. The frog felt lonely. He wanted to print a picture for his mom. But the tray had no paper. The frog wait and wait. He did not know what to do. Then his friend came with paper. The frog put the paper in the tray. He pressed the button. The printer hummed and printed a frog picture. The frog was not lonely anymore. His picture was round and green. He jumped with joy.

Once upon a time there was a duck named Daffy. Daffy wanted to print a treasure map. The map would show where the gold was hidden. Daffy found old paper in the drawer. He put it in the tray and pressed the button. The printer hummed loud. Then it printed the map on yellow paper. Daffy read the map. He wave at the treasure spots. He saw a big X mark. Daffy was happy because he knew where to look. He took the map out and ran to the tree. Gold was there! Daffy smiled big. Printing a map helped him find gold.

Lucy loved to print cards. One day Lucy tried to print a card. The printer broke down. It did not hum or beep. Paper did not come out. Lucy was sad. She sat and cried. Then she saw a ball near the printer. A boy brought the ball to help. He pushed the ball into the paper slot. The ball push the stuck paper out. The printer hummed again. Paper came out smooth. Lucy printed her best card. She gave the card to her friend. Her friend was happy too. A ball helped fix the broken printer.

Once upon a time the printer stayed awake all night. At night the printer hummed softly. It liked the quiet sounds. One night the printer glue itself shut. It could not print anymore. The little machine felt sad inside. A small bird came to visit. The bird thought the printer was lonely. The bird sang a sweet song. The printer heard the song. The bird patted the machine gently. The printer felt warm and safe. It woke up slowly. It printed a tiny star picture. The star was small and bright. The bird was happy too. The printer had a good night sleep.

Rosa the teacher had a big need. She needed lots of paper for her class. But the paper ran out fast. Rosa felt sad. Then she heard the printer whisper. The printer wanted to help. Rosa fed the printer more paper. The printer hummed hard. It printed many books for the children. Each child got a book. Rosa smiled big. The children were happy. They follow the books and learn new words. Rosa hugged the printer. She said thank you. The printer was a good helper after all. Printing helped every child learn today.

Once upon a time, a cat sat on the table by the printer. The printer was loud and wet. Rain came down from the sky. Water got on the paper. "Oops!" said the cat. The paper got heavy and droopy. The paper wanted to fly away. But the rain was hard. It pushed the paper down. The cat licked the wet paper. Then the printer took a fresh sheet. It printed a picture of a cat. "Good boy, printer," said the cat. Now the paper was dry and happy. The cat purred.

Ray had a piece of paper. It had a picture of a teddy bear on it. Ray folded the paper into a boat. "Look," said Ray. The paper boat floated on the water. A duck swam by. "That looks like me," said the duck. The duck wanted to play. Ray let the duck ride in the paper boat. They rowed to an island. There were orange trees and sour lemons. Ray and the duck ate lemons. They laughed and splashed. "This is the best day," said Ray.

Mia wanted a lemonade stand. She needed signs. She put a sign on the table. "Lemonade, five cents," the sign said. But the sign did not print right. The ink ran all over the table. "Oh no," said Mia. A bug came and sat on the ink. Mia tried again. The printer hummed. But the paper jammed. "Help me," said Mia. Her mom came with a fresh paper. The printer printed new signs. All the words were neat now. "Look," said Mia. Her stand was ready for the race.

A sun shone bright outside. A horse stood near the printer. The printer was quiet for a long time. "I am sorry I am too loud," said the printer. "I should wait," the printer said. "But I want to help you," the printer said. The horse nodded. "That is cool," said the horse. The printer took a fresh sheet. It printed a picture of a horse in the sun. The horse smiled. The horse gave the picture a pat. "Thank you," said the horse. The printer was happy now.

A white stack of paper sat on the table. It was tall and round. The frog hopped over. "What is that big pile?" said the frog. "It is paper," said Mom. The frog looked at the paper. The paper looked at the frog. The paper leaned to one side. Then the paper fell over. "Whoa!" said Mom. The paper landed on the floor. The frog helped pick up the pieces. "Let us put them back," said Mom. The frog jumped into the pile. The pile was not so tall anymore. "We should put the paper away," said Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little red cup on the table. The cup was very sleepy. The cup wanted to see pictures of animals. The printer said, "I will print for you." The printer took paper and made a picture. But the picture showed a big yellow shoe, not an animal. The cup said, "That is not right!" The printer was very sad. The printer tried again and again. Finally, it printed a nice cat. The cup smiled. The cup said, "Thank you!" The printer beeped happily.

Emma wanted to print a birthday card for her friend. She wrote the words on the computer screen. Then she told the printer to print. The printer hummed and took a sheet of paper. Emma waited. The printer printed a big round cake in a picture. A soccer ball sat next to the cake in the picture. But the printer did not stop there. It kept printing more cards. The paper came out so fast that Emma could not catch all of them. Some cards fell on the floor. Emma picked up the cards. One card had a soccer ball on it. She laughed. Then she put all the cards in a box for her friend.

At school, the children drew pictures of a tree. They wanted the printer to print their pictures. The printer started to work. It took paper and began to spin. The printer was slow today. The children waited. First it printed one picture. Then it printed another. The light bulb above the printer turned on. This meant the printer was thinking hard. The printer printed the third picture. All the children clapped. They loved the tree pictures. But then the printer started to spin again. It tried to print one more picture. The printer made a funny sound. No paper came out. The printer was stuck! The teacher helped the printer. The children learned they should stop when the printer is slow.

It was a cold morning. The window was icy. Outside, snow fell softly. Inside the house, it was very cold too. Nobody wanted to turn on the heater. Then the printer woke up. It said, "I am ready." Paper slid out of the printer. But the paper was warm, like a plate of hot food. The warm paper moved on the table. The baby looked at it. "What is that?" the baby said. The mother said, "A warm piece of paper came out of the printer." The warm paper kept moving. It rolled toward the baby's hands. The baby touched it gently. The baby giggled. Then the warm paper fell on the floor. The mother picked it up. She put it on the chair. Later, she used the warm paper to wipe the table. The table was clean. Everyone was happy.

Every morning, the old man brought his clock to the printer room. He set the clock on the printer table. The clock ticked and ticked. Then he told the printer to print. The printer took paper and started to print. But the printer did not print well. The ink made the paper sticky. The sticky paper stuck to the next page. The printer could not pull the pages apart. The old man tried to help. He pulled the pages gently. But they tore. The printer stopped. The clock kept ticking though. The old man was sad. Then his helper came. The helper gave the printer some new toner. The printer took the toner and printed again. The pages were clean now. The old man smiled. The printer worked well again. From that day, the old man always checked the toner first.

Once upon a time, there was a flat piece of paper sitting on a table. It was very blank and very quiet. A light bulb glowed above it and said, "Hello, little paper! Would you like to become a picture?" The paper did not say yes yet. It wanted to know what the picture would be. "I could be a bus," said the paper, "a yellow bus with black wheels." The light bulb smiled. "That sounds nice. Let us try." But when the printer took the paper, it printed only grey lines. The paper felt sad. Then the printer tried again. This time it printed a yellow bus! The bus had black wheels and big windows. The paper felt happy and proud. Now it is a picture on the wall. Every day, the picture makes someone smile. The end.

Lily wanted to print snowflakes for her class. She put clean paper into the tray. She pressed the key and pulled a sheet out. She folded the paper in half, then in half again. She used scissors to cut tiny shapes. Out came beautiful paper snowflakes! She hung them on the window. But then her shoe fell on one snowflake. It broke into pieces. Lily felt sad. She picked up the pieces. She glued them back together with tape. Slowly, the snowflake became whole again. She put it back on the window. Everyone clapped. The end.

Joe found an old box of paper in the recycling bin. The paper was torn and dirty. But Joe was not sad. He took all the old paper home. He washed it well. He put it on a warm plate so it could dry. Then he put it back into the printer tray. The printer hummed and made fresh paper. Joe printed drawings for his little sister. His sister drew a moon with stars. Joe was happy. The old paper did not go away. It came back new. The end.

A small drop of ink lived inside a bottle. It could not run far because it stayed in one place. "I wish I could see the world," said the ink drop. So it found a stick. The stick held the ink drop. The ink drop climbed onto the stick. Now it could run! It ran down the table, across the floor, and outside the house. It saw green trees and blue sky. It saw a bird flying. The ink drop felt lucky. But then it saw a puddle on the ground. It fell into the puddle and got mixed with the water. It could no longer be its own color. It stayed small in the water. The lesson: even a small thing can have a big trip, but sometimes staying safe is best. The end.

A big printer lived on the desk. A small printer also lived on the same desk. The sun shone on both printers. The sun said, "Good morning!" The big printer said, "Good morning. I am ready to work." The small printer said, "I am ready too, but I am tired." The big printer helped the small printer. First, the big printer printed a big card for the front door. Then the small printer printed a tiny note for the fridge. The small printer rested its arms. The sun warmed both machines. They worked together and were happy. The end.

Inky was the last sheet of paper in the tray. Inky wanted to print something. But the tray was empty now. Inky sat quietly. "Please call another sheet," Inky said softly. The machine did not hear. It kept humming and did not print. Inky felt lazy and alone. Then a boy named Marco came with a new stack of paper. He slid the new paper into the tray. The machine heard Inky and started to print. A colorful card came out with a drawing of a cat. Marco smiled. Inky was not lazy after all. Being helpful makes you useful. The end.

There was a small printer on a table. Its name was Bo. Bo was shy. Bo had a bucket of ink inside. But Bo did not like to print. "What if I make a mistake?" whispered Bo. One morning, the sun came up. The sun was warm and bright. Bo saw the sun through the window. "The sun is so happy to see me," said Bo softly. Bo took a deep breath. Then Bo printed a bright yellow circle. It looked just like the sun! Bo smiled and waved. Now Bo was not shy at all.

Pip the frog wanted a big picture. Pip sat near the printer. "This printer is too slow," said Pip. "The wheel moves very slowly." Pip waited and waited. The printer finally printed a tiny picture of a frog. Pip was sad. "It is too small," sighed Pip. The printer tried again, but the wheel kept moving slowly. Pip hopped away sadly. Later, Pip found another printer that worked fast. "Thank you!" said Pip. Pip hopped happily with the big picture.

Jen printed a word. The word was "balloon". Jen printed it again and again. The same word went up and down. "Balloon balloon balloon balloon," repeated the printer. Jen felt bored. A cool fish swam near the paper. "Why do you keep printing that word?" asked the fish. "I cannot think of anything else," said Jen. Jen tried to find a new word. But the printer kept printing "balloon" over and over. Jen felt tired. The fish gently touched Jen's hand. "It is okay," said the fish quietly. Jen closed her eyes and took a rest.

Two printers lived on a long table. One was tall. One was short. They were friends. One day, the tall printer wanted to print a big picture. The short printer wanted to help. The tall printer took a big sheet of paper. It was heavy. The short printer helped hold it. "We can do this together," said the short printer. They both leaned down. The paper was heavy but they moved it together. They printed a beautiful picture. Both printers were proud. They printed many pictures after that. They were the best of friends.

Beep was a friendly printer. A teacher named Ms. Dot came to get some paper. "I need a copy of my word list," said Ms. Dot. Beep took the paper and started to print. Beep beeped softly while he worked. He printed the words perfectly. Ms. Dot read the words and smiled. "Thank you, Beep," she said. Then the teacher found a lost bubble near the floor. She picked it up and gave it back to a little kid. Everyone felt warm inside. That is how printing helps teachers every day.

A mean baker needed a menu for his pretend restaurant. He told the printer to print the menu. But the printer did not work. It made one sad bite of paper instead. The baker felt very angry. He stomped away from the table. Soon a hungry kid named Tim came to eat. Tim looked at the tiny paper and laughed. "This is not enough food," said Tim. The baker felt sad too. Then the printer tried again. It printed a long list of treats. Tim ate all the cake and drank juice happily. The baker was happy once more.

A little frog named Fred wanted to build a tower. He asked the printer to print a tall paper stack. The printer beeped too loudly. The loud beeps scared the birds away. Fred sat down on the floor. He felt so tired. His tower paper fell down. Fred cried a little. Then his friend came with a cup of water. "It is okay, Fred," said his friend. Fred took a sip of water. He felt better. He looked at the fallen tower. He tried again slowly. This time the beeps were quiet. The tower stood tall. Fred felt proud again.

An ant named Andy wanted a picture to print. He found a friendly printer on the table. "Can you print for me?" asked Andy. The printer took a piece of paper. It printed a fun drawing. Andy saw a big ant in the picture. Andy picked up some crayons. He colored the picture brown and black. Now Andy had a cozy picture to take home. But then it rained outside. Andy could not go outside to play. He felt sad for a moment. Then his friend brought an umbrella. Andy looked at his colored picture under the umbrella. He felt happy again.

One rainy day, a girl named Lily wanted to print a sunny picture. She put a blank paper into the printer. "Please print a sunny sky," said Lily. The printer hummed a calm song. It printed bright yellow sun and blue sky. But it was still raining outside. Lily did not feel like smiling. She looked at the paper. Then she looked out the window. Raindrops made silver lines on the ground. The paper had rain too. Lily thought about it. She said, "The sun is hiding, but I can see the rain." The paper showed both. She put the paper on the wall. Her room felt calm and bright. The picture answered how she felt inside.

Once upon a time there was a duck who sat on top of the printer. The duck was cozy and warm on the warm table. The printer was hungry to print. It printed and printed and printed. Every page had a picture of a bird flying in the sky. The printer did not stop. Pages piled up on the floor like stacks of green leaves. The duck looked down and saw lots and lots of pages. "Oh no," said the duck. "The printer will run out of paper." The duck hopped off the table and found a big stack of paper under the desk. "We can use this," said the duck. The duck pulled some pages from the stack and put them into the printer. The printer hummed and printed one more page. Then it was quiet again. The duck smiled because everything was okay. The printer stayed on its table and kept being a good printer for the duck and the bird pictures.

Once upon a time a rabbit named Rosie wanted to throw a party. She needed invitations for all her friends. "I must find my brave rabbit friend," said Rosie. Rosie went to the printer and asked it to print invitations. "Please print twenty cards," said Rosie. The printer hummed and took a sheet of paper. It printed the first card with a rabbit on it. Then it printed another card. Rosie put all the cards into an empty jar. She opened the jar and counted the cards. There were plenty of cards inside. Rosie put the jar on the table so her friends could find the invitations. When her friend Henry arrived, he opened the jar, took out a card and read the words. "This is wonderful," said Henry. Everyone at the party had a card with a rabbit on it. The party was a great success because the printer made nice invitations and the brave rabbit helped all day long.

Once upon a time it was a cold morning. Snow fell outside the window. A duck sat on the table and shivered because it was very cold. "I wish someone would warm me," said the duck softly. The printer heard the duck and wanted to help. "I can print warm paper!" said the printer. The printer took a sheet of paper and printed it again and again. Out came warm paper from the printer. The duck saw the warm paper coming out and ran toward it. The duck wrapped itself around the warm paper. The paper was soft and warm, just right for the duck. The duck stopped shivering. "Thank you," said the duck. The duck stayed on the warm paper all morning. The printer hummed happily and gave the duck more warm paper each time it was needed. Outside the window the snow kept falling but inside everything was warm and safe. The duck was happy to sit by the printer.

Once upon a time a new printer was delivered to a house. The house was full of surprises. A curious little girl named Lily opened the box and saw the shiny new printer. "Can you print my first page?" asked Lily. The printer beeped and took a sheet of paper. It printed the first page ever from this new machine. On the page was a house drawn in bright colors. A little sun was smiling above the roof. "Wow," said Lily. "This is my house!" The printer printed a second page. This time it drew flowers and trees around the house. "This is my garden," said Lily. She put the papers on the kitchen table. The printer was happy to help and made many pages for Lily. The first page was special because it was the very first thing the new printer ever printed. Lily smiled every time she looked at those bright pages. The house and the garden were now in print and would never disappear.

Once upon a time it was Saturday morning and the printer was lonely. No one had used it all day. The printer sat on its table and looked very sad. "I want someone to print for me," said the lonely printer. Dan walked into the kitchen carrying his dog, Biscuit, on his lap. Biscuit barked at the printer. "Hello," said Dan. "Are you okay? You look lonely." The printer beeped softly. "Yes, I am lonely. No one prints for me today." Dan smiled. "Let me print you something nice," said Dan. Dan fed a sheet of paper into the printer. It printed a picture of a dog. Dan placed the picture on the table near the printer. Biscuit sniffed the picture and wagged his tail. "You are lucky," said Dan. "Now you have something fun to look at." The printer was not fully happy yet but it felt better knowing someone cared. Dan sat with Biscuit and looked at the picture of the dog. Later in the day Dan printed a card for his mom. That made the printer smile too.

Once upon a time there was a small robot who carried paper to the printer. The robot lived in a big room near the machine. One day the robot found a rabbit sitting on the floor. The rabbit said, "I lost my picture." The robot said, "I can carry paper to the printer and print your picture for you." The rabbit smiled. The robot picked up a stack of paper and walked into the room. He brought the paper right to the printer. The printer hummed and beeped and printed the picture. Now the rabbit had its picture back! The rabbit said, "Thank you, robot." The robot said, "You are welcome." The rabbit hopped away happy and sparkly in the light.

A tall printer lived in an office. It was afraid of the dark. At night the dark came and covered all the desks. The printer would shake and say, "I am scared." A little calculator walked over. The calculator said, "Do not worry. I will hold the light for you." So the calculator stood up and turned on its screen. The light was bright. The printer felt safe again. Then someone called a party at the office. Everyone came with cups of juice. The printer was asked to print all the fun cards for the party. The printer hummed and printed every card. It was not scared at all. Everyone clapped for the happy printer.

Nick wanted to find his lost pet mouse. Nick said, "Where did my mouse go?" His mom said, "Let us print a poster." So they went to the printer. They put big paper into the printer. The printer hummed and printed a big poster. The poster said, "Find my pink mouse!" They hung the poster on the wall. Soon after that, a girl walked by and saw the poster. She said, "That is a pink mouse!" Nick ran outside and found his mouse hiding under a flower. Nick said, "You answered!" The mouse licked his hand. Nick was so happy. The flower helped because it was big and green. They all played together.

Nick had a new car he wanted to look at. But Nick was shy. He did not want anyone to see his car. Nick said to the printer, "Can you print a picture of my car?" The printer said, "Yes, I can do that." So Nick put paper into the printer. The printer hummed and printed a big picture of a red car. Nick looked at his picture. It was perfect! Nick took the picture out and showed everyone. His friend said, "Wow, that is a great car!" Nick smiled big. He was not shy anymore. The printer made a happy job. Nick gave the printer a high five. Everyone cheered. Nick loved his new picture.

Jack found a shiny treasure map under his bed. Jack said, "I will print this map!" Jack went to the printer. He put the map paper inside. The printer started to work. But the ink was wet. The map would not dry. Jack said, "The map is mad. It cannot wait." Jack's mom said, "Let me turn on the light. Light helps things dry." Jack turned on the bright light. Soon the map dried up. Now the lines on the map were clear. Jack could read where the gold was. Jack said, "I know the way now!" Jack put on his shoes and went on an adventure. The small hint at the start was that the map was wet, and now it was ready. Jack found a hill and climbed up. He looked behind a tree. Yes, there was gold! Jack was so lucky.

One morning Jack woke up and opened the drawer of the printer. The printer said, "I have no toner left." Jack said, "What is toner?" His mom said, "Toner is what makes the words show on paper." Jack felt sad. Then a hungry robot came by. The robot said, "I can help print your letters." The robot ate some bread and got energy. Then the robot put paper into the printer. The printer hummed and printed a letter. Now Jack had letters to send. Jack said, "Thank you, robot." The robot said, "You are welcome." Jack put the letter in the mailbox. He walked to the bus stop with his paper. Everything worked out fine. Jack learned that when you help others, they help you back. And a printer without toner is not so bad if a friend shows up with bread.

Once upon a time there was a big printer named Pip. Pip was very tired. He printed so much that his arms hurt. A tree was sitting on the table. The tree was very pretty. Pip tried to print the tree but he could not move. His head was too heavy. He fell down. Now Pip had to rest. He lay still and looked up at the tree. It was warm above him. Even though Pip could not print the picture, the tree was still beautiful. Sometimes you have to be calm and rest when your body is tired. The end.

One day a printer in the library wanted to print an apple. The apple was red and round. But the paper went wrong. The paper flew off the table and hit a car. Then the car started to fly! The car zoomed out the library door. Nobody was sad. A little boy ran after the car. The car stopped at a tree. The printer beeped softly behind the door. The little boy found a new paper and put it back. Now the printer was calm again. Everyone was happy to see the apple still on the table. The end.

A tiny drop of ink lived inside a big printer. The drop was small but it wanted to see the world. It looked through the door at all the colors outside. The drop did not want to stay inside one color forever. It rolled down a tube and fell on fresh paper. Then the drop saw the world! It felt colorful and bright. When the paper came out, the drop was happy to paint with the sun. It saw blue sky and green grass. Later the drop sat on the warm floor and smiled. Thank you for letting me see the colorful world. The end.

There was a house by a lake. The lake was full of water. Inside the printer tray, there was only one sheet left. That was the last sheet of paper for the house. The printer tried to fit the house on that one paper but it would not work. The paper was too thin. Suddenly the paper grew big like a lake! The water spilled everywhere. The printer could not stop the water. It was too loud and too messy. Now the house could not be printed. The paper was gone. The printer sat quietly and let the water dry. The end.

One night the printer woke up. It heard the wind outside and wanted to make something. The printer got a brush and began to build a paper fort. It made walls and a roof. Then it put down some paper grass. The printer was so busy building that it forgot the light. It stayed up until morning. By then it was tired again. The wind blew and the fort blew away. Now the printer was quiet once more. If you stay up too long doing one thing, you get tired. Better to sleep at night and rest. The end.

An old frog hopped into the printer room. The frog liked to sit on the warm table. One day the old printer tried to print a funny picture. But the printer was very slow. Every time it printed one line, the ink made a bubble. The bubble popped and the frog giggled. The printer skipped a turn because it was too slow. The frog did not get angry. The printer tried again and again. Finally the picture was done, silly and slow. The frog gave the printer a little wave. Thank you for printing my picture. The end.

Once upon a time, Tim had a big car in his driveway. He wanted to print a picture of the car so he could show it to his friend. But the printer was sad. It needed a drink of juice. Tim gave it some juice. Then the printer went to sleep for a while. When it woke up, it felt happy again. It took a sheet of paper and printed Tim's car picture. The printer was shy but it did not mind. Tim smiled and said thank you. The printer hummed a happy tune. Everything was fine. The car picture was saved on the paper forever.

Molly waited for a new printer at home. She wanted it to help with her drawings. A bus came along the road. It stopped and the new printer got out. Molly walked up to get her new printer. But the printer was very dry. No ink inside. Molly felt sad because she could not use it yet. Her mom came outside and told her not to worry. Molly sat on the floor and looked out the window. A man helped carry the printer into the house. Then someone filled it with ink. Molly hugged the printer. It worked! She drew a nice picture of a girl and her dog.

Rex worked late in the office at night. All his friends had gone home. The lights were on but the office was quiet. Rex wanted to print a special card for tomorrow. He fed a piece of paper into the printer. It started to hum. Then he heard a dog barking. A dog walked right into the office. The dog did not mean any harm. It just wanted to play. Rex laughed and let the dog play under his desk. The dog found a ball and rolled it back. Rex printed his card. The printer made a beautiful print. They both were happy. The dog barked once more and then went to sleep next to the warm machine.

"Good night," Rex said quietly.

The dog wiggled its tail once.

Frog lived near a little bridge by the river. Frog wanted to print a book about jumping over the water. But the printer only knew how to print in one color, green. That was all it could do. Frog felt sad. "I want more colors," said the shy frog. The printer tried to help but it could only print green. Frog sat under the bridge and thought. Then Frog saw a ladybug walking across the bridge. "I will draw the other colors myself," said Frog. Together they made a big, colorful book. The printer printed the whole book in green and the frog added red, blue, yellow and pink. The book was the best book anyone had ever seen.

Mia wanted to print a thank-you note for her teacher. She picked up a special pen. She carried the note to the printer. The printer was slow today. Mia waited. She waited. The note was almost done when something unexpected happened. The sun came out from behind a cloud and shone directly onto the paper. The ink ran and made a bright streak across the page. Mia laughed. She printed the note again. This time she moved the paper away from the sun. The thank-you note came out perfect. Mia gave it to her teacher. The teacher smiled and said "thank you." Everyone clapped.

Will had a big printer and a small printer on his desk. Both printers liked to work. Will wanted to print two pictures at once. The big printer said, "I can handle that." But the small printer was hungry for paper. "I need more paper to work well," said the small printer. The big printer clapped its hands. "Let us both try!" The big printer fed three sheets at once. It printed the first picture. Then it clapped again and printed the second. The small printer was happy. It had enough paper. They printed two pictures together. Will smiled. "You are both good helpers," he said. And they were.

Once upon a time, a friendly little printer sat on a table. It had a light bulb on top that glowed bright yellow when it was ready to print. A boy named Tim came home and asked the printer to print his joke book. The printer said, "I will print your jokes for you!" First it printed a picture of a park. Then it printed a joke about a dog who wanted to catch a ball but missed. The printer printed it again and again because Tim laughed so hard. The light bulb stayed yellow the whole time, glowing and glowing. Then the printer printed one more joke about a cat who wanted to catch a fish but could not swim. Tim smiled and patted the printer on the side. The printer hummed happily and went to sleep. The end.

Nick had a tree in his backyard. Nick loved his tree very much. One day, Nick put paper into the printer and pressed the button to print a sign. But something went wrong. The printer kept printing the same word again and again. It printed the word "wash" over and over. Nick looked at the papers and felt sad. Nick wanted a nice sign, not dirty words. Then the bell rang. Nick's mom came to the door. She looked at the stack of papers. "What is this?" she asked. Nick said, "The printer keeps printing the same word." Mom took the papers away and told Nick that sometimes machines make mistakes. Nick felt sad for a minute, but then he cleaned the machine with warm water and soap. When he turned the printer on again, it printed a beautiful sign that said "Welcome Nick." Nick smiled and hugged his tree. The end.

A new printer lived in a house. Dad loved this printer a lot. One morning, Dad said, "Printer, print my story!" The printer started to hum a happy song while it printed the words. The sound was nice and warm. Dad read the story and enjoyed every page. Then one day, the old paper tray broke. Dad could not print anymore. He felt very sad. Dad said, "I do not want to read without my printer." Then Dad found an old box of paper near the window. He put new paper inside and printed his favorite story again. The printer hummed its song once more. Dad smiled. Even without the old printer, printing was still fun. The story had a sad beginning and a happy ending. The end.

A rabbit named Ruby lived near a big tree. Ruby liked to read books by the tree. One day, Ruby saw a printer on the table. She said, "What are you doing?" The printer answered, "I am printing a story!" Ruby walked closer and watched the printer work. The printer took a piece of paper and printed a picture of a rabbit. Then the printer blinked its light once. Ruby thought that was funny. Then the printer blinked its light twice. Ruby jumped back. Then the printer blinked its light three times. Ruby ran away and hid behind the tree. The printer kept blinking. "I do not like you," Ruby said. She went home and did not come back to play with the printer that day. Later, Ruby found the paper the printer had dropped and read the story. Ruby liked the book. She thought the printer was still kind, even if it blinked too much. The end.

A scanner and a printer were best friends. They sat next to each other on the table. One afternoon, a sock fell on the floor. The sock was fuzzy and soft. The scanner said, "That sock is smooth. I would love to see it." The printer said, "Let us watch it move." So they stood together and watched the sock roll under the table. The sock bounced and rolled back and forth. The scanner tried to take a picture of the sock, but the sock kept moving. The printer tried to print the sock, but it would not stop rolling. Finally the sock stopped. The scanner said, "I cannot copy a sock because it moves too much." The printer said, "We can print a drawing of the sock instead." They drew a smooth sock and printed it on paper. Both friends smiled. They had a good laugh together. The end.

It was a busy day at the office. A big teddy bear worked there. Many people came to the printer with their papers. The printer had a wheel on the side that helped it turn smoothly. At first, the printer printed quickly. But then the paper ran out. Everyone waited. The teddy bear brought more paper, but the paper was wet from a leaky pipe. The wet paper jammed inside the printer. The printer beeped loudly. People looked at each other and worried. The teddy bear tried to fix it. Then the teddy bear had an idea. He gave all the wet papers out to everyone to dry. He said, "Wait here. We will dry the papers and try again." While everyone waited, the teddy bear watched the printer carefully. Soon the papers were dry. The printer took fresh paper and printed everything again. Everyone got their papers. The teddy bear smiled and said, "Sometimes a busy day is hard, but we can help each other." Everyone agreed. Everyone was happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to make a birthday card for her friend Amy. Amy was getting one year older. Lily sat at the desk and took out a big piece of paper. She opened the calculator and pressed the buttons. The numbers made a round shape on the paper. She wrote her own words on it too. "Happy Birthday Amy!" she said. But then the machine made a funny sound. The paper came out wrong. It was all crumpled. Lily was sad. She wanted to give the nice round card to Amy. But she had no nice round card now. Then Amy came into the room. Amy looked at the sad crumpled paper. "Don't cry, Lily," Amy said gently. "I will make you another card." Amy went to the desk again. The machine hummed. A new round card came out. Lily smiled. "Thank you, Amy." They both gave each other hugs. It was a happy birthday for Amy after all.

Pam had a car picture on her desk. She printed it yesterday for fun. Now the page was still in the printer. Pam wanted to play with the paper. She picked it up and shook it hard. The car shape fell on the floor. "The car flew away!" Pam said. She tried to catch it but it rolled off the table. Then Pam saw the old paper airplane on the desk. She picked it up and shook it again. The airplane went far across the room. Pam thought about it. "I can fold the paper into a new airplane." She found a pen and folded the page. The new airplane went very far. Pam laughed. She shook the new paper airplane and threw it in the air. It flew straight and landed in the toy box. Pam smiled. The car and the airplane were both gone now, but Pam had fun with them.

There was a printer at school. The children called it Mr. Dot. Mr. Dot was a big box that could print. One morning the teacher said, "We need more paper." Mr. Dot took a piece of paper and made some cards. The children loved the cards. Soon they all said, "Mr. Dot is our friend." One day the teacher ran out of paper. Mr. Dot sat on the table and felt quiet. The paper tray was empty. He could not print anything. The children were sad too. "Oh no," they said. Then the principal brought more paper. Mr. Dot took the paper and started printing again. The children cheered. From that day, every child called him Mr. Dot. He did not mind. Being called by a friendly name made him happy. Always wait until there is paper before you are sad, that is the lesson.

One sunny day, Tim sat under a big tree. Tim wanted to make a boat out of paper. He found a piece of paper on the desk. He put it in the printer and waited. The machine hummed. Out came a long flat page. Tim took the page and found a pen. He folded the corners to make a boat shape. But the boat would not float. It sank right away. Tim was sad. He looked at the tree above him. The tree had a wheel hanging from a branch. That was a big wheel from a wagon. Tim grabbed the wheel. "Maybe I need a bigger wheel." He put the wheel in the boat. Now the boat floated on the water! Tim jumped up and down. "A wheel in my boat makes it float!" Tim rowed the boat around the puddle. The tree was proud of him. Sometimes you find something you did not expect, that is the lesson.

It was a rainy day. Rain fell on the window. Tim was awake late because he could not sleep. The room was quiet except for the rain. There was an old note on the desk. It was a picture of a car. Tim liked looking at the car. He shook the car picture gently like wind. Then the paper got wet from a drop of water. The colors ran and the car looked blurry. Tim shook the wet paper dry. But it was ruined now. "No good," Tim said. His mom came in with a dry towel. "Can I help?" she asked. "Yes please," Tim said. They shook the paper together. It came out mostly dry. Then Tim put the paper in the printer. The machine hummed. Out came a fresh copy of the car. Tim looked at the bright car. He felt better. "Thank you, Mom," he said. The rain stopped and the sun came out. Tim and his mom drank hot cocoa together. Even when things go wrong, you can print them again, that is the lesson.

Sara had a crumpled paper ball on the floor. It was a page that had been dropped and crushed. She picked it up and looked at it. It was all folded and creased. "What should I do with this?" Sara asked her mom. Her mom said, "Let me see if I can fix it." Her mom smoothed the paper flat. It became almost flat again. Sara looked closely. On the paper there was a road drawn with lines. She saw a little house and a car on the road. Sara held the paper up to the window. The light came through and made the colors brighter. She blinked her eyes slowly. The road seemed to come alive. She could almost see the car driving down the road. "It looks like a road," Sara whispered. Her mom smiled. "Looks like it." Sara put the paper back on the desk. It was not crumpled anymore. She learned that even when things fall down, you can make them flat and use them again.

Once upon a time, a girl put a drawing on the table. She wanted to print a cat. But the printer printed something else. It printed a big bear. "No, no, no!" cried the girl. She looked at the table. There stood her paper with a bear on it. "I want a cat!" she said. She took the paper away. She told the machine, "Call your friends and print again." The machine hummed and beeped. Then it printed a new paper. Now there was a cat on the paper! The girl smiled. The bear was strong, but she liked the cat much better.

It was raining outside. Sun did not shine. A girl wanted to print a sunny picture. "I wish I had sun today," she said. The printer started to work. It printed a bright yellow sun. The girl looked at the paper. The sun was tiny and round. She held it up. "Look, it is yellow," she said. Even though it was rainy outside, the sun felt warm in her hand. She put the picture on her wall. The room was not bright, but the little sun made it feel warm. She learned that the sun can come inside too.

A tree grew in the yard. A train went by the tree every day. The tree wanted to share a story with the train. The tree asked the printer to print a story about trains. The printer worked hard. It printed a long paper full of train words. The tree read the story. Then the tree folded the paper. "Here you are," said the tree. The train came closer. The tree gave the paper to the train. "Thank you," said the train. The train read the story aloud. All the trees could hear. They were happy that the tree shared. Now every day, the train would hear a new story from the tree.

A tall stack of paper stood by the gate. The stack was very high. Paper tried to stand up straight. But the wind blew. The stack tipped over! Papers fell everywhere. A flower grew next to the stack. "Oh dear," said the flower. "What happened?" The papers rolled down the hill. They bumped the flower. The flower did not get hurt. A nice lady saw all the papers. She helped pick them up. She stacked them again, just the right way. "Good job," she said to the flower. The flower smiled. From then on, the papers stood up straight. The flower was happy too.

A cat loved warmth. The cat jumped onto the warm printer. The printer hummed softly. The cat closed its eyes. A light bulb hung above the machine. The light bulb glowed green. "Hello, little light," said the cat. "You look so nice today." The light bulb said, "Thank you for letting me shine here." The cat purred and curled up. The printer did not mind. It kept printing. Soon a blue balloon popped on top of the printer. The balloon floated up to the light bulb. "Look what you carry," said the light bulb. The cat opened one eye. "I like this spot," said the cat. The light bulb glowed brighter. Everyone was happy together on the warm table.

Bo sat at the desk with the big printer. Bo wanted a party for his birthday tomorrow. Bo pulled the paper tray out and set a sparkly plate on the paper. The printer hummed. It was a happy sound. Bo looked at the paper. The plate was there! Bo looked at the sparkly plate again. "Look," Bo said. "The printer made it." The printer beeped once more. It printed a big flag too. "Look, look, look!" Bo clapped. The printer hummed a little song while it worked. Bo smiled. The party would be wonderful. A sparkly party with a sparkly plate. Bo did not need to look very hard anymore. Everything looked perfect. The printer was so kind.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to print a picture of a big pink cake for her grandma. Lily sat at the desk and pressed the button. The printer hummed and beeped. But the paper went the wrong way. It rolled off the desk and landed in the floor. Lily looked sad. Then she called her mom. Mom came and picked up the paper. They put it back and tried again. This time it worked! The printer made a beautiful picture of a pink cake with cream on top. Lily gave the paper to her grandma. Grandma smiled and said thank you. It was a happy day.

Sue had a old printer on the second floor. One day Sue moved the printer to a new room down the hall. The printer did not like the new room. It felt lonely. It hummed softly and could not find its favorite chair. Sue made a little house out of paper for the printer. Then Sue drew a duck on a piece of paper and put it by the door. The duck was cute and yellow. The printer felt a little better. Even though the room was small, the printer stayed happy. It printed many pictures for Sue. She hung them on the wall. Every night she called the printer home and it did not feel sad anymore.

A little light bulb lived in a lamp above a desk. The light bulb was very shy. It did not like the bright sun or other bulbs. One night the bulb decided to seek a quiet spot near the printer. The printer was also shy. It hid behind its table. The light bulb peeked out and beeped softly. The printer heard the sound and came forward. Together they found a cozy corner by the window. The light bulb glowed gently and warm. The printer hummed a happy tune. They made a soft room full of light. The bulb learned that being shy does not mean you are not special.

Mia wanted to print a picture of her red car. She put the paper into the tray. Mia pressed the button. The printer made a copy. Mia took the paper and sat down to color it. She gave the picture to her dog, Biscuit. Biscuit was curious. He sniffed the paper and then bit a corner. Ouch! The ink came off on his nose. Mia laughed. Biscuit licked his nose. Mia made another print. This time she held the paper herself so the dog could not reach it. Biscuit watched from a safe distance. Mia colored the car with blue crayons. The car looked bright and fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little house with a red door. Dot lived inside. Dot had a friend named Tab who was a robot. Tab brought paper to the printer every day. One morning, Tab came running to the house. "I cut the wrong sheet!" Tab said. Dot was sad because Tab had cut the paper and it made the house look broken. "Don't worry," said Dot. "I will print again." So Dot took the cut paper and fed it back into the printer. The printer hummed. The printer beeped. Then out came a perfect orange sheet of paper. It fit right on the wall like a new picture. Dot smiled. The house looked happy again.

Ted was a teddy bear. Ted had one blank piece of paper in his tummy. Ted wanted so much to be a picture. He wanted to be a bear like him. But the blank paper did not know what to draw. "I am too empty," the paper whispered. "I want to see colors." Ted tried to help. He sat on the blank paper and told it what to draw. But nothing came out. Ted felt very sad. Then the light from the window hit the blank paper. The paper saw its first brown color. It grew warm. Now Ted could draw brown fur. Ted drew himself! The blank paper became a wonderful picture of Ted. Ted felt very happy now.

Dan was a duck. Dan lived by a quiet pond. Dan wanted to print a picture of the whole family. But the printer was tired. "I am too tired," the printer said. Dan felt sad. He wanted everyone to see the picture. His friend Nat the mouse heard Dan's sad noise. Nat came close. "Let me help," Nat said. Nat pushed the tired printer button. The printer hummed and beeped. Slowly, a picture came out. It showed Dan, Nat, and all the family around the pond. Dan was so glad. He shared the picture with everyone. They all clapped and smiled. Even the tired printer rested a little more.

Behind the office printer lived a tiny mouse named Pip. Pip loved the quiet behind the machine. It was his home. One day, a loud truck rolled past. The printer made a loud sound. Pip ran into his little hole. He was scared. He did not like loud noises. Then a calculator rolled by. It stopped near the printer. The calculator had a friendly face. "Hello, Pip," the calculator said softly. "Are you okay?" Pip peeked out. He felt a little better. The calculator asked Pip to share some candy it carried. Pip shared his candy with the calculator. The calculator gave Pip a sweet treat. Pip ate and felt full. The quiet behind the printer was still his home, but he was not sad anymore.

Pip was a little boy. Pip wanted to say thank you to someone special. His friend Lila brought him a very ugly tree for his desk. "Thank you, Lila," Pip said. "But I want to write a note." Pip found a blank piece of paper. He put it in the printer. The printer hummed and beeped. Out came a beautiful thank-you note. Pip wrote kind words on it. Pip taped the note to the ugly tree. The ugly tree now looked pretty. Lila came to Pip's room. She read the note. She smiled. She gave Pip a big hug. Pip felt so happy. The ugly tree was gone, and a beautiful memory stayed.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily had a lemonade stand in her yard. She wanted to print signs so people could see the names of her drinks. She found a printer and put a sheet of paper inside. A light bulb lit up above her head. "I can do it!" she said. She typed the letters and pressed the button. The printer hummed and beeped, then printed two flat signs. They were perfect! Lily hung them near the stand. Soon, kids walked by and read the signs. They loved her lemonade! Everyone had a good time. Lily smiled and poured cold sweet juice into little cups. Her signs helped a lot. It was a happy day for everyone.

Once upon a time, a fish named Bubbles sat alone in a paper tray. The tray was empty and neat. No fish food was inside. Wind blew through the room.
