The wind picked up the tray and carried it far away from the table. Bubbles was sad. "I want to swim," said Bubbles. The wind carried the tray to a big puddle. Bubbles splashed around happily. But there was no water for him to eat. He felt very sad. Then a kind person came back with paper. The person printed fish food on the paper. Bubbles ate the food and swam again. He was happy once more. The empty tray was gone, but the wind still blew. Everything turned out okay in the end.

Once upon a time, a boy named Tim drew a picture of a moon. He wanted to give it to his mom. He put his drawing into the printer. "Please print my moon," he said. The printer took the paper and printed the drawing. Tim opened the door and looked at the picture. It was beautiful! But there was one problem. A rabbit kept chasing the moon on the paper. The rabbit did not stop. Tim tried to hold the paper, but the rabbit kept running across it. Finally, Tim printed another page. This time he drew a fence. The rabbit ran behind the fence and stopped. Tim gave the moon picture to his mom. His mom was so happy. Tim learned that nice drawings are the best gifts of all.

Once upon a time, a robot printer felt sad. Its drawing tools were dull and slow. It could not draw like a crayon. A teddy bear saw the robot looking at its paper. "You can be fast," said the teddy bear. "Let me show you." The teddy bear skipped ahead and left bright marks on a new paper. The robot watched and felt inspired. Then the robot picked up the paper and started drawing, too. It was fast and bold. The drawings were wonderful. The robot felt better than before. It printed many pictures for the teddy bear. They played together on the table. The robot was happy now. Being fast made all the difference.

Once upon a time, a frog named Freddie lived near a plant. The plant lost its leaves and became gray. Freddie missed the green leaves. One day, Freddie found a crumpled piece of paper on the ground. He smoothed it out with his hands. Paper was flat again. Freddie walked to the plant. He stood under the gray plant. Then he pressed the paper onto the plant leaves. Magic happened! The plant grew green again. Freddie jumped on a leaf and laughed. The plant was happy. The paper helped the plant come back to life. Freddie hopped away and told all the frogs about it. They cheered together. The gray plant was green once more because of a flat piece of paper. Nothing was ever lost completely.

Once upon a time, two printers sat on a table side by side. One was old and tired. The other was young and bright. The old printer could not keep up with the busy world. The young printer felt sad too. "We need friends," said the young printer. The old printer nodded. Kate came to the table carrying more paper. "I need help printing," said Kate. The old printer and the young printer worked together. They built a long line of pictures for Kate. The old printer hummed softly while the young printer printed quickly. Kate was so happy. She looked at all the pictures and gave them a big wave of thanks. From that day on, the two printers worked as a team every single day. They were never lonely again.

Once upon a time there was a little white puppy named Ruby. Ruby sat in the sun and the sun made her warm and happy. Ruby had a picture on the table that was almost done printing. The paper was still wet. Ruby opened the window. A big wind blew! The paper flew right out the open window. Ruby ran to the window. "Oh no!" said Ruby. She looked down. The paper was gone. It flew over the house and out of sight. Ruby felt sad. Then she saw the puppy on the ground. The puppy looked up at Ruby and wagged its tail. "Good news!" said Ruby. She jumped and caught the paper before it went far away. The puppy was so happy to see its friend. Ruby smiled. The lesson is: don't let things fly away when they are still wet.

There was a boy named Bob who loved to print pictures of his fish. Bob put the paper in the machine and pressed the button. The printer hummed and beeped and printed a picture of a big green fish swimming in water. Then Bob put the paper on the table. Bob turned around, but the paper was missing! Bob looked under the chair. He looked beside the bed. He looked on the floor. The paper was not there. Suddenly, the little puppy came bounding across the room. The puppy saw the paper and grabbed it with its mouth and ran off into the yard. "Hey!" called Bob. "That is mine!" But the puppy did not come back. Bob felt sad and worried. Then he heard a giggle. The puppy came back with the paper in its mouth. The puppy gave the paper to Bob and licked his hand. Bob laughed and hugged the puppy tight. The lesson is: someone who loves you will always come back for you.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia who lived in a house. One day Mia's mom brought home some old paper from a pie. There were papers from birthday cards and old drawings. They were all crinkly and tired. "What can we do with these?" asked Mia. "We can play," said Mom. "But they are too old to print new things." Mia took the old papers and put them in a box. Later, the baby spilled juice on the box. Juice went everywhere. The box got messy. "Oh no," said Mia. "The papers are all wet!" Mia looked around. She found an old towel. She wiped the juice off the papers. Then she dried each paper one by one. Finally the papers were clean again. Mia put them back in the box. Next week she used them to print new birthday cards for her friends. The lesson is: old things can be saved if you are patient and kind.

Jen loved to print pictures of her egg and her calculator. One morning Jen sat down to print a picture of a pink egg and a calculator. The printer started to hum. Then it stopped. The screen showed nothing. "Hmm," said Jen. "The ink is dry." Jen pulled the paper tray out and took out the empty ink cartridge. The cartridge was completely dry. Jen tried to find another cartridge, but the only other one was also dry. The printer would not work. "I need help," said Jen. She ran to ask her dad. Dad found a bottle of special ink at the store. He helped Jen put the new ink into the printer. Soon the printer hummed again and printed the picture perfectly. Jen smiled and held up the pink egg and the calculator to show her dad. Dad clapped his hands. The lesson is: even when something breaks, asking for help can make it better again.

There was a tiny robot named Pip who lived next to a big hill. Pip woke up one morning. "My batteries are dead," said Pip. "I cannot print anything." Pip wanted to fix the printers but did not have any ink. Then Pip heard a whistle. Up the hill came a friendly printer who could talk! "Hello, little Pip," said the printer. "I can help you print." Pip was so happy. They went together down the hill to the house where the printers lived. The friendly printer showed Pip how to add fresh ink. Pip learned how to fill cartridges and press buttons. From that day, whenever a printer needed help, Pip was the first one to run and fix it. The lesson is: working together and waking up early helps you do good things.

One day a boy named Tim asked the printer to print a joke. "Please print a funny joke for me," said Tim. The printer sat quietly on its table. Tim waited and waited. The printer did not say anything. Tim tried pressing the button again. Still nothing. Tim looked at the machine. The machine looked back at Tim. "I do not know what joke to print," the printer said shyly. "I am not very smart about jokes." Tim frowned. Then Tim thought of a joke. "Why did the wheel go to school?" Tim asked. "To get smarter!" Tim told the printer the joke. The printer thought hard. Then it printed the joke on a big piece of paper. Everyone who read it laughed. Even the printer smiled behind its screen. Tim learned that sometimes you have to try your best and tell a joke yourself before the printer can print one. The lesson is: if you want something printed, try doing it yourself first.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Dot. Dot sat on the table all day. Dot printed drawings for Finn. Finn drew pictures of animals and trees. One day Finn forgot to give Dot ink. Dot felt sad and did not want to print. Finn heard Dot humming but Dot would not say sorry. The light bulb above the table glowed orange. Finn asked Dot why Dot was sad. Dot said it was Dot's fault. Finn helped Dot clean the ink tray. Then Dot said sorry softly. Dot printed more pictures for Finn. Finn smiled at Dot. Now they are good friends. The end.

Once upon a time there was a library and a printer named Rob. Rob sat next to the big book shelves. A girl named Mabel brought Rob some paper. Rob printed a picture of a purple ball. She put it on the library table for children to see. Children came and sat around. They looked at the purple ball. Then a little flower grew on the paper too. A child picked up the flower and smelled it. Everyone sang a happy song together. Rob hummed along while singing. The flower smelled sweet like honey. Children laughed and clapped their hands. Rob was glad to help the library feel warm. The end.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Leo. Leo sat on the table ready to print. A family came with paper and ink. The family wanted to print photos. But something went wrong. A paper got stuck inside Leo. It caught the paper path. The printer made a beeping sound. The paper was bumpy with jammed pieces. Finn reached into the printer opening. Finn pulled out a little teddy bear that had gotten stuck. It was not a real bear but paper stuck together. Finn freed the paper. Then the family printed their photos. The photos came out perfectly smooth. Everyone laughed and hugged Leo. The end.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Sam. Sam waited on the table for someone to press the button. A child named Leo came and stood close. But nobody pressed the button. Sam felt lonely sitting there. Finn said Sam could wait for now. Leo went home without printing anything. Sam did not understand why no one used Sam. Sam sat alone all day. Finn came back later and pressed the red button. Sam printed a nice picture of a park. Leo saw the picture and smiled. Now Leo knows Sam is useful. A lesson learned: always use your helpers. The end.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Max. Max printed a page for a paper airplane. Finn cut the page into a round shape. He folded it like wings. Max watched Finn fly the airplane. The airplane zoomed across the room. A duck ran under the table. The duck gobbled the paper airplane. Finn tried to catch the airplane but he missed. The duck flew away with the airplane. Finn heard the duck say quack. He chased the duck around the room. The duck dropped the airplane near a window. Finn caught it just before it fell. Finn printed another airplane. Then Finn flew it and the duck laughed. They all had fun together. The end.

Once upon a time, a little restaurant sat in town. A girl named Lily wanted to print a menu for her pretend food. She found a light bulb on the wall and flipped it. The light was bright and warm. She took paper and fed it into the printer. The machine made a sound like a hummingbird. It printed the menu, but something was wrong. The paper came out with a wobbly line. Lily looked at the menu and felt sad for a moment. Then she opened the drawer and found a soft cloud of ink. She wiped it gently and the words became clear again. The menu now looked perfect and shiny. Lily put it on the table for her friends to see. Everyone said the food would be great.

Noah had a old printer at home. He wanted to print a picture of his dog, Biscuit. He pushed the button. The machine hummed and beeped. But the word BISCUIT kept printing over and over. Noah tried again. Still the same word appeared. "Stop that," he told the printer. The machine did not listen. It just kept making the same word again. Noah looked into its drawer. Inside, he saw a small mirror. It showed him a funny face. He laughed out loud. Then he wiped the inside of the machine with a wet cloth. He pushed the button one last time. This time the word BISCUIT appeared once, very clearly. Noah smiled and hung the picture up on the wall. His dog Biscuit looked silly, like a funny ghost.

One day, a car named Sam pulled into a driveway. Sam wanted to print a map for a trip. Sam rolled up his window. Sam fed paper into the printer. The machine started to print. But something was wrong. The paper kept coming out, and the next paper went in too. Printing never stopped. Sam watched from the driver seat as pages piled high and tall. "Please stop," Sam said quietly. The printer did not stop. Pages stacked up like a paper river flowing down the steps. Sam was scared. He could not reach the papers before they fell. At the bottom of the pile, a tiny bird landed. Sam reached down and picked up one paper. It had a drawing on it. The bird looked at Sam and chirped. Sam laughed softly and stacked the papers in a box.

Tim loved treasure maps. He wanted to print one so he could find gold in a cave. He asked his friend Mia to help. "Let us print it together," Tim said. They fed paper into the machine. The machine hummed. Tim pushed the button and waited. But the paper came out wrong. One side had a big tear on it. "That is bad," Tim said. He tried again. Same thing happened. A silly tear split across the whole page. Tim was sad. The map was ruined. Mia reached for the torn page but could not fix it. Then Mia had an idea. "What if we print a new map?" she said. Tim smiled. They printed another map, clean and whole. Tim took the map and ran outside to play. The second map was perfect.

There was a big tree next to a printer. The tree was sad because nobody played with it anymore. The printer was also sad. Its ink was low and its buttons were stuck. The two friends felt lonely on their hill. One day, a boy named Oliver found them both. Oliver cleaned the printer's buttons. He refilled the ink. "Good news," he said to the tree. "Your friend is awake again." The tree felt warm inside. The printer hummed happily and started printing colorful pictures. The pictures made Oliver smile. Oliver and the tree played together on the hill. The printer made a picture of the hill for the tree to hold. They all felt happy. And every day after that, they played together in the sun.

Once upon a time there was a little printer named Pip. Pip could only print in red. All the colors were gone! Blue, green, yellow - all gone. Pip tried very hard but he could only print red. A little dog came to the table. The dog was scared because he wanted a blue ball. He looked at all the red pages and ran away fast. Pip felt sad. Then Pip found one blue ink drop under his table. Pip took that drop and printed a blue ball! The little dog came back. He was so happy. He played with his blue ball. Pip was happy too because he could now print blue.

Once upon a time a girl named Lily needed to print a note for her mother. She put a piece of paper into the printer. She pressed the button. The printer began to hum. But then it stopped. The printer said, "I do not have any toner left." Lily felt scared. Everything would not work now. She looked inside the printer box. There was no toner at all. Lily thought for a long time. Then she found a small bottle of toner near the door. She put it back inside the printer. She pressed the button again. The printer hummed and printed the note. Her mother was so happy to get the note. Lily learned that you must always save your toner.

Once upon a time Emma had a big flower drawn on her wall. She wanted to print another picture but the machine chose the wrong thing. It printed an ugly cow instead of a flower. The ugly cow stood on her desk. It did not look nice at all. Emma was sad. She looked at the ugly cow and felt silly. Then Emma pushed the ugly cow gently. "Come here," said Emma. The ugly cow walked over to the flower on the wall. Emma looked at both pictures. The cow had brown spots and looked almost like the flower. She laughed and printed the flower again. Now there were two pretty flowers on her wall. Emma smiled.

Once upon a time a sun was shining bright outside. Inside a house a little boy wanted a letter from his grandpa. Grandpa was far away in another town. The printer could print a letter for him. The printer hummed and printed the letter. The boy read the letter and loved it. Then the boy found something wrong. The letter had smudges on it. The printer did not say sorry. The boy was sad. He wanted the printer to say sorry. He told the printer, "You should say sorry." The printer heard him. The printer took a deep breath and said, "I am sorry. I made a mistake." The boy felt better. The next day the printer printed a nice clean letter. Everyone was happy.

Two printers sat on the same table. Their names were Printy and Paper. They were friends. One day a fish swam up to their table. Printy saw the fish. "Hello," said Printy. "What are you?" asked Paper. "I am a fish," said the fish. "Can you print me?" asked the fish. Paper answered, "We can try." Printy pushed some paper into his body. He hummed and printed a picture of a fish. The fish looked at the paper. "That is just like me!" said the fish. Printy and Paper both beeped happily. Then a bird came flying down. "Can you print my picture too?" asked the bird. Printy said, "Yes we can answer your question." They printed the bird together. They worked as a team and made many pictures. They were the best printers at the table.

Once upon a time a boy named Tim wanted to make snowflakes. He cut paper into small pieces. Each piece had six points. Tim drew lines on each piece to make the snowflake shape. Then he put the pieces into the printer. He wanted to print snowflakes. The printer took the paper and printed on it. But the paper was too thick. The printer could not print through it. Tim felt stuck. He pulled out the paper. He looked at the paper car beside him. "I need help," said Tim. Then he remembered. He folded the paper thin and printed on it again. The printer printed the snowflake perfectly. Now the paper was thin enough. Tim cut the snowflakes out and hung them on the window. The snowflakes fit nicely. He looked cool as he stood by his car holding the pretty snowflakes.

Molly wanted to print a birthday card for her friend. She sat down at the printer. Molly picked up a blue card and put it in the tray. Then she pulled the handle and pushed it in. The printer hummed and beeped. It took the paper and started to print. Molly had to wait. The printer stopped once. Molly was sad. She waited some more. Then she heard a duck quacking. A duck ran up to the printer. The duck tapped the side of the machine. The printer started again. It printed the card. On the card, there was a picture of a boat on water. Molly smiled. The duck was printed too! Molly gave the card to her friend. Her friend laughed and said thank you.

The old printer sat on the table all day long. It made many copies. But now the printer was tired. Its ink was running out. It could not print well. The buttons did not work right. A train rumbled by outside. The train looked heavy and tired too. The printer whispered, "I want a rest." Nobody heard it. A clean cloth came to the table. Someone wiped the printer. The printer felt better. Now it could print one more time. Molly sat down and asked the printer to print a picture. The printer hummed and printed the picture. The printer was happy again.

A tall stack of paper stood on the table. It was very hard and tall. The bottom paper did not feel safe. It wanted the stack to fall down. The calculator sat next to the stack. The calculator looked worried. "Please fall," the calculator said softly. The stack did not move. The stack grew even taller. Molly came into the room. She saw the tall stack. She reached for a top paper. The paper shook. The stack began to lean. The whole stack fell over. Papers rolled everywhere. The calculator rolled too. It tumbled to the floor. Molly picked up the papers. She put them back in order. "It is okay," Molly said softly. The calculator looked up and nodded.

A mouse lived behind the office printer. The mouse loved the warm hum of the printer. The mouse liked to write notes on small scraps of paper. One day, the mouse saw a kite fly outside. The kite had a long tail. The mouse wanted to write about the kite. But the printer would not start. The mouse tried many times. The printer beeped and stopped. The mouse felt so mad. "Why will you not print?" the mouse cried. The mouse wrote the words by hand. Then the mouse fed a scrap of paper to the printer. The printer hummed and printed a picture of a kite. The mouse read the paper and smiled. The kite flew far away. The mouse knew it would come back again.

Jill wanted to see outside the window. Jill sat at the printer. The printer could not open the window. The printer just printed things. Jill felt so mad. She wanted to look at the sky. She wanted to see birds fly. The printer hummed and made copies. Jill did not care. "I wish I could go outside," Jill said. A bird flew past the window. Jill watched the bird. The bird dropped a feather on the table. Jill picked up the feather. It was white like milk. Jill dipped the white feather in ink and made a mark. Then Jill turned the printer around. The printer looked out the window. Jill patted the side of the printer. "Good idea," Jill said softly. The printer printed a picture of the sky with a white feather like milk. Jill smiled and leaned against the warm machine.

Once upon a time, a little printer wanted to draw like a crayon. The printer was blue. The printer had no colors yet. "I want to write in brown," said the printer. A bird sat on the table next to the printer. "You can write in brown too," said the bird. The printer was happy for a moment. But then the printer tried to write on every paper it found. The paper was too thin. The printer could not write well. The printer stopped. "I need soft paper," said the printer. Then the printer found the softest paper in the whole house. Now the printer could write in brown and draw like a crayon. The bird smiled.

There was a tall tower of paper near a window. The window looked out to the garden. A tired printer sat inside the tower. "I wish I could see outside," said the printer. No one heard the printer. The printer sat very quiet for a long time. Then a boy came to the window and pulled the curtain back. He saw the green trees and the red flower bed. He looked at the printer. "Can you bring me outside?" he asked. The printer rolled its paper toward the window. It printed a picture of the garden on fresh paper. The boy smiled and hung the picture on his wall. The printer felt proud. It did not need to go outside after all.

A coat fell on the floor near the empty paper tray. The coat was light. "I have no paper!" shouted the printer. The printer was sad. There was no paper for the printer to print on. Outside the door, a flower stood up. "Do not shout," said the flower. "I will help you." The flower bent down. The flower dropped its petals onto the tray. Those petals were like paper. The printer picked them up. The printer printed a picture of the flower. It printed the picture twice. One copy went in the folder. The other copy the child put in a book. The printer was happy again. Paper was never missing again.

A child drew a picture at school. The child drew a cat and a fish and a house. "I want you to print this," said the child to the printer. The printer was slow that day. The printer took so long that the child began to cry. "Give me the picture now," said the child. The printer finally printed the picture. The printer was quiet while it worked. When the picture came out, the child ran to get it. The child looked at the drawing. The cat looked happy. The fish swam in the water. The child smiled. The lesson was simple: the printer did its best, and it was worth waiting for.

It was a busy day at school. Little cups of juice sat on the desk. A teacher told the children to write stories about their families. Each child gave one story to the printer. First came a story about a dog. Then came a story about a bird. The printer hummed and beeped. The printer was little but it worked hard. "I cannot stop now," said the printer. "I must print all the stories." The printer printed each story carefully. At the end, the printer printed a picture of a fish swimming in blue water. Every child got a copy. Everyone clapped. The printer was tired but it was happy.

The sun went down. The room got dark. A dull printer woke up from sleep. "What is that sound?" said the printer. A frog hopped onto the table. The frog had a big green eye. "Who are you?" asked the frog. "I am a printer," said the printer. "You can chase me if you want." The frog blinked. "Why would I chase you?" The printer printed a picture of the frog. That made the frog jump off the table. Then the printer printed another picture. The frog did not want to chase the printer again. The printer turned off. The frog hopped away to sleep. The printer was glad. It had something nice to print, and it did not have to run anywhere.

Once upon a time, a teddy bear sat on a chair. The teddy bear was very happy. He had a big job. He had to bring paper to the printer. The printer sat on the table, waiting for paper. "I will bring the paper now," said the teddy bear. He picked up the first sheet of paper. "Here is one," he called to the printer. The printer hummed and said, "Thank you." Then the teddy bear brought another sheet. But the teddy bear chased a tiny bug that ran across the floor. The bug went into the printer's paper tray. The printer could not get the paper out. It made a sad beep. The teddy bear chased the bug again but could not find it. So the teddy bear sat down and patted the printer gently. "Do not worry," he said. "I will help you soon." The printer felt better after the teddy bear was kind. A new sheet of paper slid out from the tray. Everything worked fine again.

Sue wanted to print pictures for her class. She put her drawings on the paper tray. Then she pressed the green button. The printer started to hum. The pictures came out one by one. Everyone clapped. Sue's teacher said, "These are wonderful!" Then the printer made a strange noise. It stopped. The pictures were all blank. A bike rolled into the room. The bike did not mean to do this. It left its tire on the paper tray. The tire blocked the paper so the printer could not feed it right. Now no pictures would come out. Sue said, "Oh no." Her teacher tried too but it still did not work. Then the bike rolled away. The printer hummed again and printed all the pictures. Sue showed her class the beautiful pictures. Everyone learned that things can go wrong but we can try again.

A cat named Mia liked to sleep on the warm printer. The printer was warm because it just printed something. Mia curled up on top of the paper tray. "This is the best spot," she purred. A bird landed on the table near the printer. "Hello, friend," said the bird. Mia opened one eye. "Go away, bird," she said. The bird flew to the window and sang a song. Mia closed her eyes again. Then the printer started to beep. It wanted more paper. Mia woke up. She saw the paper tray was empty. "Huh?" she said. The bird swooped down and dropped a small fish onto the tray. "That is not paper," Mia said. "It is food," said the bird. The printer ate the fish instead of paper. It got a little confused. "I cannot print with fish," said the printer. Mia licked the bird. "You gave me a good surprise," she said. Then Mia jumped off the printer. The bird sang happily the whole way home.

Leo was allowed to press the print button. He loved his car. Leo put a picture of his car on the paper tray. "Let us print my car," he said. He pressed the green button. The printer hummed and took the paper. But the paper was wet. It stuck to the tray. The printer could not pull it out. "Oops," said Leo. He looked at the tray. The wet paper made a sound like a little boat. A shell fell from somewhere. The shell was smooth and round. "What is that?" said Leo. He picked up the shell. It was soft and fluffy inside. "I can eat this!" said Leo. He bit into the shell. It tasted sweet. Then he looked at the stuck paper. He patted the tray gently. The paper slid out. His car picture was perfect! "Nice," said Leo. He kept the shell to eat later.

A new printer came to a family's home. Everyone was excited. The family unpacked the box. The printer was shiny and new. "Look at you," said the papa. "You are going to be great," said the mama. The little girl held the paper tray. She wished the printer would work well. Papa plugged the printer in. The printer hummed and waited. The little girl put a drawing on the tray. It was of a leaf. "Print my leaf," she said. She pressed the button. But nothing happened. The printer sat there and did not move. The little girl pushed the button again. Still nothing. The printer felt sad. The family sat together. "Maybe we need paper first," said the mama. They took out fresh paper from a box. The little girl added her drawing. This time the printer printed the leaf. Everyone smiled. That was the happy part. Later, the little girl found a dead leaf on the floor. It was very old and dry. She put it in the box with the printer papers. The old leaf did not fit in the tray. The printer made a sad beep. Then the little girl gently put the old leaf outside. She patted the printer. "Don't cry," she said. "We have your new paper now."

A neat rock sat on the table next to the printer. The printer blinked its light on and off. The rock watched the light blink. "Are you ready?" asked the rock. "I am getting ready," said the printer. Then the printer sent a message on the paper. It printed a tiny note. The rock read the note. "Please send me to school," it said. The rock did not want to go. But the printer folded the paper carefully. It put the paper inside a small envelope. "I will send you," said the printer. The envelope was sent down a long road. A big truck picked up the envelope. The truck carried it far away. The rock was surprised. It did not know it would travel so far. Soon the truck brought the envelope back. The printer opened the envelope. Inside was a new rock, also neat and tidy. The rock was happy. "Thank you," said the neat rock. The printer blinked its light once more. "You are welcome," it said. The two rocks sat together on the table, friends forever.

Sue sat at her table in the house. It was a cold morning outside. She wanted to print something warm. She put a friendly sheet of paper into the printer. The machine hummed a soft sound. Then it printed. Warm paper came out of the printer. Sue held it close to her face. It felt nice and warm on her hands. She put the warm paper over her blanket. It made her feel cozy inside the house. On cold days, you can print a warm paper and hold it to your chest.

Noah had a big printer and a small printer. They were both in the room. Noah loved both of them. One day, the small printer got a piece of paper stuck inside it. It made a loud sound. "Ugly!" said the big printer. The small printer was sad. Noah took a pencil and carefully poked the stuck paper. Then he pulled it free. The small printer cheered. "Thank you, Noah!" it said. The big printer clapped too. You can help your friends when they look ugly or stuck. Just be kind.

Once upon a time, a little bear found an old key lying on the ground. It was a tiny key, so small it barely fit in his paws. The bear wanted to open a box, but he did not know where to put the key once he found it. He sat on the grass and looked at the key. Then he thought of his friend, the printer. The printer could make new paper. The bear walked to the printer and said, "Can you help me? I want to print something for my friend." The printer hummed softly and said yes. The printer took the tiny key and printed a picture of it on a piece of paper. Now the bear had his picture of the key, and his friend could see what the key looked like. The bear smiled and went home with his paper. His friend was happy to receive the picture.

Tess wanted to throw a party for her friend Ana. She asked her mom to help her print the invitations. Mom put paper into the printer and pressed the button. The printer made a pretty card with hearts on it. But the next day, the invitations did not come out right. The cards were blank. Tess felt sad. "What happened?" she asked. Mom said, "The printer needs more ink." They tried again, but the printer still made blank cards. Now no one would come to the party. Tess sat on the chair and cried. She looked at the blank cards and felt very sad. Then she saw a stack of old papers near the printer. She pulled them out gently. One of them had a faint heart on it. She held it up and smiled. "I can use this," she said. She printed new invitations using that old paper. That evening, many friends came to the party, and they all sang happy songs.

A lake was calm and quiet one morning. A little duck swam across the water. On the shore stood the printer. It was humming a soft song while it printed a drawing of the lake. The duck heard the printer humming and thought it sounded nice. "I like your song," the duck said. The printer beeped happily and kept printing. Soon, a bird landed on the printer's table. "Do you want me to sing too?" the bird asked. "Yes please!" said the duck. So the bird began to sing, and the duck joined in. The printer hummed along. The song was bright and happy. All around them, flowers opened their petals. A frog sat on a rock nearby and listened. "This is a lovely place," the frog said quietly. Then, as if it knew its part was almost done, the bird sang louder. The printer started to shut down its power. The duck and the bird waved goodbye. The frog hopped away toward the shore. The sun rose higher, and everything felt warm.

Dot wanted to print a picture of a frog sitting on a lily pad. She put the paper in the printer and pressed the button. The printer hummed and began to print. Dot watched carefully. First, the green lily pads appeared. Then the brown frog appeared too. But then the printer stopped. It made a sad beep. The ink ran out in the middle of the picture. Dot frowned. "Oh no," she said. The picture was half done. The frog was missing. Dot looked at the dry ink cartridge on the side of the printer. It was empty. She could not print the frog now. The frog in the real world was sitting on a big leaf in the garden, waiting to play. Dot picked up the half-printed picture. "I will draw the frog myself," she said with a laugh. She grabbed a pencil and drew the frog on the blank paper. It was not as good as a real picture, but it had the same smile. Dot hung the picture on the wall. The frog in the garden saw the picture and jumped happily.

Ella needed to print a letter for her teacher. She put the paper in the printer and pressed the button. The printer hummed, then made a loud noise. It stopped. Paper came out, but it was all folded wrong. Parts of the paper were torn. Ella gasped. "My printer broke," she said. Her brother Bear heard her cry. He came running and looked at the broken printer. He reached into the side of the machine and felt around. "I think I caught a small bit of paper stuck inside," he said. He pulled it out carefully. Then he pressed the button again. The printer hummed and printed the letter perfectly. Ella clapped her hands. "Thank you, Bear!" she said. Bear smiled. "You are welcome," he said. Ella printed her letter, and it came out clean and straight. The teacher read the letter with a big smile. Ella gave a hug to her brother. They both laughed.

Ivy's brother was flying a kite outside their window. Ivy held a stack of papers ready to print something special. As she turned to place the paper in the printer, one page slipped out of her hands. It fell out the window. Down it floated, past the kite string, and landed on the roof. Ivy's brother saw the paper and laughed. "Look! A paper flew away!" he said. He reached for it, but it was too far. Ivy climbed the ladder and got the paper back. She brought it inside and placed it in the printer. The printer printed the page perfectly. Then Ivy pulled out another page, and another. Each time one fell out the window, she printed another one. When the last page came back, Ivy had six pages. She tied them together with a long string. Then she took the kite out the window again. Her brother used the string to fly the papers in the wind. The papers fluttered around like little birds. Everyone who saw it laughed and clapped.

Amy wanted to make a thank-you note for her friend. She picked up a crayon and drew a big smiley face. Then she hid the crayon inside the paper so nobody could see it. The paper was a little too thick, so when the printer pulled it in, it got stuck. The printer was angry. It beeped loudly and did not want to print. Amy had to help by pulling the paper out slowly. Then she pressed the button again. The printer hummed and printed a bright yellow card. She wrote thank you on it with a pencil. Her friend loved the card. Amy smiled and gave the card away.

Lily sat at the table with her dog next to her. The dog was curious about the printer. Lily reached into the tray and pulled out one sheet of paper. The dog sniffed the paper and put his nose right on it. He tried to build something with the flat paper but it just fell over. "That is not how to use paper," Lily said gently. She put the last sheet back into the tray. The printer beeped. It wanted another piece of paper to do its work. Lily pulled out two sheets this time. The printer hummed happy sounds and printed a picture for her. She gave one sheet to her dog. The dog licked her hand and wagged his tail.

It was snowing outside. Anna wanted to print snowflakes to hang on the window. She held some white paper up to the light. The printer took a blank sheet and started to print six little shapes. But the shapes were not perfect. They were wobbly and looked like circles instead of stars. Anna felt sad. The printer felt sad too because it did its best but could not make good snowflakes. Then Anna heard a soft song coming from outside. A bird landed on the windowsill. The bird sang a fluffy song. Anna laughed and sang along. She folded each wobbly shape into a new pattern. Now every snowflake looked like a tiny star. She hung them all up. The printer hummed proudly and gave her more paper to make even more stars.

The printer always made loud sounds. One day Amy sat next to it and whispered, "You are quiet and kind." The printer listened. After that, Amy always talked gently to the printer. Soon the printer began to hum softly when she was near. Amy named it Sunny. When Amy left the room, the printer felt sad. It missed her voice. Sunny stayed on the table and waited quietly. Every night Amy came home and sat close to the printer. Sunny hummed a warm song and Amy patted its side. They were friends now. Amy never ignored the printer again. She always said please and thank you. The printer was happy to have a kind friend nearby.

Tommy dropped his soccer ball on the floor. Next to the ball was a crumpled paper. Tommy kicked the ball hard and it rolled into a corner. The crumpled paper was under the ball. Tommy wanted to play again but first he picked up the ball. He stepped on the crumpled paper and it bounced away. Tommy saw it on the floor. He picked it up and looked at it. It was torn and twisted. His mom said, "Let me flatten this paper." She smoothed it out on the table. Tommy watched as the paper became flat and wide again. He put it in the printer and pressed a button. The printer hummed and printed a green picture of a banana. Tommy smiled. He rolled the soccer ball back toward the table and kicked it. It flew across the room and hit the wall.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to print a picture of an apple for her grandma. The printer sat on the table. Lily put paper in the printer. She pressed a button. A green apple came out of the printer! Then she printed a tree too. She gave the picture to her grandma. But the glue was not on the right spot. The glue was short and went in the air. Grandma laughed. "The glue is funny, Lily!" she said. Lily smiled. She printed one more apple for the tree picture. Now the picture was perfect. The apple sat on the tree. Grandma was happy.

Once upon a time, the office was quiet at night. Everyone had gone home. The lights were off. A seed fell on the floor. It rolled under the printer. The printer stayed on. The seed started to grow. It grew roots into the paper tray. A tiny sprout came up. It looked like a little green plant. The printer could not close the tray. The sprout grew taller every night. One morning, the sprout was as tall as the printer. The plant pushed the tray door open. A new flower came out of the paper. The office smelled sweet. Everyone came back for coffee and flowers.

Jack wanted to print a picture of a horse. "I want to color it," Jack said. His mother put paper in the printer. Jack pressed the button. A white horse came out. Now he needed colors. Jack picked red. He picked blue. He picked green. He colored the tree brown. He colored the sky blue. The horse was cool and bright. Jack was happy. Then he saw the sun in the picture. He colored it yellow. "That looks nice," his sister said. Jack gave the picture to his mom. She hung it on the wall. Jack clapped his hands. "Great job!" his mom said. The picture stayed on the wall all week.

Inky the cat loved warm things. She liked to sleep on the printer. One day, Inky curled up on the warm paper tray. She purred softly. The printer hummed and clicked. Then a loud sound beeped. A motor started spinning. Inky jumped up. The printer tried to print something. It did not work. The paper jammed. Inky licked her paw. "Hello?" she called out. The printer heard her. "Sorry," the printer said. Inky walked into the kitchen. She found bread on the counter. She ate the bread. Then she walked back. "Good night, Inky," the printer said. Inky purred and went to sleep again.

Anna was afraid of the dark office. "No printer!" Anna said. "I do not like it dark." Anna turned on the lamp. The lamp made the room bright. But the printer still looked scary. "I will fix that," Anna said. She turned on the printer. It hummed. Paper went in. A fish came out of the printer! Anna laughed. "A fish is not scary." She printed another fish. She printed a seaweed. She printed a starfish. The office looked fun now. Anna ate a cookie. She sat next to the printer. "Good morning, Anna," the printer said. Anna smiled. She took the pictures home with her.

Nick wanted a bedtime story. He asked the printer to print one. Nick lay down on his bed. The printer hummed quietly. Pages came out one by one. Nick read about a dog walking in the forest. The dog found a stick. The dog used the stick to dig a hole. Nick learned a lesson. "You should not throw rocks," Nick said. The dog was careful. Nick closed his eyes. The story helped him sleep. He dreamed of the dog and the stick. He slept all night. The next morning, Nick woke up. "Thank you, printer," he said. He smiled and drank his milk.

Once upon a time, there was a little drop of ink named Fred. Fred lived inside a calculator. It sat on a warm table next to a big paper. Fred wanted to see the world outside. One day, Fred heard a sound. "Print!" said the calculator. Fred jumped out and fell on the paper. Then the calculator said, "Throw me onto a flower!" So Fred threw himself onto the paper. He rolled like a tiny ball across the white sheet. A picture of a red flower appeared. Fred saw the flower and felt so happy. He had traveled far to meet it. The end.

Little Printer lived on a small table in a quiet house. On the weekend, Little Printer was alone. No one came to use him. A sad feeling filled his body. His friends went away. Little Printer looked at an apple that lay nearby. He wanted someone to print it for him. He tried to push paper into his mouth, but he could not eat. His gears were too small and hard. He sat and waited all day. Then at last, someone picked up the apple. They put it under the machine. Green and red colors printed on the apple. Little Printer felt a little less sad. The end.

A little monkey named Mimi wanted to draw a sunny day. But it was rainy outside. Mimi was lonely. She looked at her paper. "I cannot draw sun," she said. Her friend peeked over her shoulder. "Can I help?" asked her friend. "Yes," said Mimi. "Draw a blue sky first." They sat together. The friend drew a bright yellow circle in the sky. Mimi added clouds and rain drops. The picture was beautiful. They printed it on thick paper. Now every one could see the sunny picture. Mimi smiled. The end.

Old Printer lived in a small room. A kitten named Kit sat near him. Kit was shy. She watched Old Printer pull paper in and push it out. "Do you have a new room?" Kit whispered. "Not yet," said Old Printer. "Maybe soon." Kit climbed onto the printer table. She stepped carefully on each foot. Old Printer looked down at her. "Will you play with me?" he asked gently. Kit nodded shyly. She batted at the paper tray. Paper flew everywhere. Kit laughed and played. Now Old Printer had a friend. The end.

At school, the big printer helped everyone. Pam stood waiting. She wanted pretty pictures for the class. "Please print my drawing," said Pam. The printer hummed and pulled in fresh paper. It printed many colorful pictures. Pam held them up. Everyone clapped. But then some kids wanted to print pictures too. Pam felt blue. "My turn next," she said quietly. The printer kept working. Soon it had printed many good pictures. Pam got her turn again. She showed everyone her favorite picture. The printer helped make the best day ever. The end.

Ivy sat with a game of cards. She wanted to print her winning card. Ivy fed the paper into the printer. But something was wrong. A paper jam! The printer made a loud beep. The paper got stuck inside. Ivy frowned. She reached in with both hands. Her fingers touched warm brown paper. She pulled it out slowly. "Easy now," she said softly. She fed the paper back in gently. The printer hummed and worked again. The card printed perfectly. Ivy smiled. She learned to be gentle with machines. The end.

Will sat in a chair and looked at the little printer. The printer had a light that blinked on and off, on and off. Will watched it blink. He felt sad. The light blinked fast. Then it blinked slow. The printer was tired. It did not want to print now. So Will took a black piece of paper and held it up to the light. He wanted to know why it blinked. Will said, "I am sorry, little machine." The printer hummed soft and quiet. Will put his hand near its side. He gave the printer a big hug. The printer was warm now. The light stopped blinking. Everything was okay again.

It was raining. A soccer ball sat under a gate. Will wanted to print a picture of the soccer ball for his friend. He fed a paper into the machine. But the paper was wet! The paper got all red and curly. The printer made a sad beep. The wet paper would not go in the tray. Will took the wet paper out. He tried again. Still wet. The paper stuck. Will went inside to find dry paper. While he was gone, the printer used the last dry paper. It was too late. The soccer ball picture could not be made. Will came back. The printer was quiet. It just sat there looking at the empty tray. Will said, "I am sorry." He bought new dry paper. He printed the soccer ball picture all over again. Now it is perfect.

A teddy bear named Gus was very busy. He wanted to paint the floor red. But he only had yellow paint. Gus looked at his teddy bear friend. "I cannot paint today," he said. "The paint is gone." The teddy bear looked at a blank page. "What if I make a paper boat instead?" he said. Will helped. Will printed a flat piece of paper. Gus folded the paper into a boat shape. Now Gus had a boat. They sat by the water together. Gus blew on the paper boat. The paper boat floated away. Gus felt happy. Then Will printed another page. Gus painted the boat green. The paper boat was beautiful. Everyone clapped for Gus. The teddy bear had a wonderful time. But then the paper boat got caught in a drain. Gus cried softly. He sat alone on the shore. He missed his friend.

Leo loved the sky. It was blue and bright. One day Leo brought his old printer outside. The old printer was slow. It took forever. "I wish you could bring me something nice," Leo told the printer. The old printer hummed but did not move. Leo waited a long time. At last the old printer printed one small square. It was a tiny blue square. That was the best thing it could do. Leo smiled. He knew this old machine was helpful in its own way. The small blue square was bright against the green grass. Leo put it in his pocket. It was a good day after all.

A little girl named Mia visited the library. She found a friendly printer on a table. The printer was quiet and kind. Mia asked, "Can you help me find a book?" The printer said, "I can try. Just tell me what you need." Mia said, "I want a story about a frog who finds a lily pad." The printer hummed and took a piece of paper. It began to print. Suddenly the printer did something strange. It stopped. It did not answer. The paper came out all crumpled. It was a mess. Mia was confused. Then the printer said, "I do not know what to do. I am stuck." A boy walked by. He picked up the crumpled paper. It was a funny picture of a frog with no lily pad. The boy laughed. The friendly printer heard him laugh. It beeped happily. It printed many copies of the funny frog picture. Everyone was sweet and happy.

Once upon a time, a duck sat on the floor near a door. The door was open. The duck looked out the door and saw a big house. Inside the house, there was a printer on the table. The printer hummed softly. A little boy had left a page on top of the printer. The duck walked to the door and saw the page. The page was sad. It wanted to fly out of the door. The duck helped the page go through the door. The page flew away into the sky. The duck was happy again.

Bo wanted to print a picture of his whole family. Bo put a special card into the printer. The printer started to print. First it printed Mom. Then it printed Dad. Then it printed Bo and his little sister. Then it printed their bird. The bird sat on the chair. The bird was lonely because nobody played with it. Bo printed one more picture. The picture showed the whole family together. Bo hung the picture on the wall. Now the family could all look at the picture every day. They were not lonely anymore. Everyone smiled.

A dog was sitting in the garden. The dog heard a loud beep from a printer. The dog looked up. The printer was on the table next door. The printer beeped again. The dog's ears stood up. "Hello?" said the dog. The dog walked closer. The printer was printing a new card. "Be quiet," said the dog to the printer. The printer stopped beeping. Then it printed the card quickly. The dog wagged its tail. The dog sat back in the garden. The dog was full of joy. The printer worked well after all.

Once upon a time, a teacher had a big box called a printer. The printer lived on the table next to her desk. A small dog named Biscuit sat on the floor and watched her work. One day, Biscuit knocked over some paper, and the teacher needed new pages fast. She put in a sheet and pressed go. The printer hummed and beeped and printed black paper. Biscuit licked the warm page and barked with joy. The teacher smiled and said thank you. Then she printed a picture of Biscuit for the class. Everyone clapped. The printer was happy too. That was a good day for printing.

Once upon a time, a baby flower grew in a garden near a new machine called a printer. This printer had never printed anything before. It was shy and did not know what to do first. A little girl brought the printer to the table and said come on, print something brave. The machine held still and thought. Then it pulled out the very first page it ever made. It was blank at first, then little words appeared. The flower watched from its pot. A butterfly landed on the page and rested there. The printer felt brave for making that first print. Everyone saw the pretty page and smiled. Nothing else happened that day, but the printer learned it could do one thing well.

Once upon a time, a tiny robot lived inside a big machine called a printer. The printer broke down and would not print anything. A little flower outside the window saw the broken machine and felt sad. The robot woke up and looked around. He found a road near the house where the printer lived. He climbed onto the road and began walking back. But the road was bumpy and he fell down once, twice, three times. At last he reached the table and climbed back into the printer. He found a small piece of paper stuck in the gears. He pushed it out gently and the printer started again. The flower cheered and waved goodbye. The printer worked again because the robot walked far but arrived on time.

Once upon a time, a kind girl named Sunny had a friend who was a printer. One day the printer broke. It made a loud noise and nothing came out. Sunny felt sad for her friend. She sat beside the printer and talked softly. She said I will help you. Then Sunny found a bottle of water. She poured a tiny bit of water on the machine's table. The damp table helped the gears move easier. Soon the printer hummed again and printed a pink page. Sunny laughed and hugged the printer. Her friend smiled with a beep. It was not scary at all. The printer was happy again. Sunny knew that even broken things can be fixed with patience and care.

Once upon a time, a small machine named Pam sat alone on a table. Pam was a printer, but she was very shy. She did not like loud noises or big groups. A kind woman asked Pam to print some letters. Pam shook her head and hid behind her paper tray. Pam whispered sorry, I cannot do it today. Pam's friend looked sad. Then Pam heard a tiny voice from the garden. It was the house's cat, Meow. Meow said Hello Pam. Pam peeked out. Meow curled up on the table next to Pam. Pam felt silly and fluffy inside. She decided to try. She took a sheet of paper and printed slow, slow words. The words were plain and simple. Meow purred and rubbed against the warm paper. Pam printed a second page for Meow to play with. Pam felt braver than before. Sharing the table made her happy.

Once upon a time, a calculator sat on a table next to a big machine called a printer. They were friends who spent their days together. One afternoon, the calculator started telling jokes. Ha, ha, said the calculator. The printer wanted to laugh but could only make a quiet beep. The printer tried to tell jokes too, but the jokes were not funny. They printed silly lines all over the paper. One joke read why did the printer break up with the calculator because she was too fast. The calculator did not think that was funny either. Then they both tried to fix their jokes, but the jokes kept going wrong. The printer printed words the calculator did not understand and the calculator printed numbers the printer did not get. Finally they stopped laughing. They looked at each other and said maybe silly jokes are not always right for us. They printed one last quiet sentence together: sometimes less is more. The calculator nodded and the printer went beep quietly to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was an office at night. The door was closed. The lights were off. Dot waited by the big box machine. It was a printer. A bird landed on the desk. The bird looked at the printer and sang, "Tweet, tweet!" The printer hummed quietly. It did not want to print because all the people had gone home. Dot waited. The bird waited. They both waited together. Then the printer beeped. A long piece of paper came out. On the paper was a picture of a lion. "Look," said Dot. "The printer printed a lion." The bird was very happy. The bird flew away to find a friend. And the printer waited for tomorrow, when people would come back and use it again.

Once upon a time, on a Saturday morning, a lonely printer sat on a table in the living room. It wanted someone to print something for it. But nobody came. The printer did not talk to anyone. A teddy bear sat near the table. The teddy bear could walk. The teddy bear walked slowly across the room. "I will print you a picture," the printer said. The teddy bear walked closer and closer. But the paper tray was empty. There was no paper inside. The printer felt sour and sad. It could not print. The teddy bear walked back to its bed. The printer stood alone on the table, waiting and waiting. The teddy bear came back later with a small roll of paper. The printer printed a picture of a teddy bear, and the teddy bear smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little house near a tree. A mouse lived in the house. One day the mouse wanted to fly far away, so she took a piece of paper and drew a picture of herself flying. She put the paper into the printer. "Please print my picture," she said. The printer started to work. But something went wrong. The printer printed a picture of a cat instead! The mouse looked at the paper. She felt sad. "I wanted to fly," she said softly. "But I got a cat." The cat picture sat on the floor. The mouse picked it up and took it back outside. She went to the park and flew in real life! She learned that if you ask nicely, the printer can listen. And next time, the mouse drew her own picture before she asked.

Once upon a time, a soccer ball rolled into the garden and bumped a broken printer. The printer made a loud beep. Paper came out, but it was torn and wrong. The printer did not work anymore. A girl named Mia saw the broken printer. She counted ten little flowers growing around it. "I can help you," said Mia. "What do you need?" the printer said. Mia brought a fresh paper roll. She helped the printer open its doors. She fed the paper in the right way. She pressed the button again. The printer hummed and worked! A beautiful picture came out on the paper. The soccer ball played with a ladybug and chased a butterfly. Everyone was happy, and the printer was not broken anymore.

Once upon a time, a child named Sam drew a picture of a fish on a big piece of paper. "I will give this to my grandpa," said Sam. Sam gave the paper to the printer. The printer began to work. But suddenly, a mean wind blew through the window. The wind pushed the paper out of the printer before it was finished. The half-printed picture flew right past the fish and onto the floor. Sam looked down and saw the picture. The fish looked back at Sam, but it was not alive anymore. It was just ink on paper. "Oh no," said Sam. "My fish is dead." Sam cried. Then Sam remembered: the picture was already drawn. The fish on the paper was still beautiful. Sam took the drawing and taped it to the wall. "I will draw you again tomorrow," said Sam. And he did.

Once upon a time, a flower grew in the library. The flower was weak and small. It liked the quiet sounds of the library. A bird landed on a table near the flower and looked around. A little girl named Lily sat nearby with a book. She wanted to print a story for her family. "Excuse me," said Lily to the flower. "May I print something?" The flower nodded weakly. Lily fed a paper into the printer. The printer hummed and printed a beautiful picture of the flower. The flower was happy to see itself on paper. Later, another boy wanted to print too. The flower said, "I am too weak to help you now." The boy laughed gently and used a different paper. When the library closed, many people came to see the flower's picture. Everyone stopped to look. The flower was not weak anymore, because it had been printed in a picture that everyone loved.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Beep. Beep was very loud when it beeped. Tim sat at the table and turned Beep on. Beep went beep beep beep. It was too loud. Tim covered his ears. The sound hurt his head. "Stop," said Tim. Beep did not stop. It kept beeping and beeping. Tim put his hand on the paper tray. Beep went beep beep beep. Then Beep stopped. A small piece of paper fell out. It was wet. Tim looked at the water on the paper. The little page was torn. Beep was sad now. Tim hugged Beep gently. "I am sorry," said Tim. Beep sniffled. It was not angry. It just felt bad. Tim patted Beep's side. That made Beep feel better. They were friends again.

A fish sat inside the machine. A little fish swims in the tray. The fish swam around and around. Paper was going into the tray. "Where are you?" asked the fish. The paper slid over the fish. The paper ate the fish. "Ouch!" said the fish. The paper would not let go. Tim tried to pull the paper out. It got stuck. "Help me," said the fish. "I am stuck too." The paper balled up around the fish. It was a bright ball of paper. Tim took a new sheet of paper. He pulled hard. The stuck paper came out with the fish. The fish was safe. The fish swam away into the dark. The paper stayed in the tray. "Thank you, Tim," whispered the fish. "You are a good helper." Tim smiled and went to play.

Will had an old printer. The printer was slow. It took a long time. First it took a long time. Then it took even longer. Will watched from his chair. The frog sat on the chair next to Will. "I am waiting," Will said. "It is slow today," said the frog. The printer hummed and hummed. Will counted to one hundred. Then the printer started again. It printed one page. Then another page. Will jumped up and down. The printer printed more pages. One by one they came out. Finally, the last page was done. Will clapped his hands. "Good job," said the frog. The frog hopped off the chair. "You are patient," said the frog. Will nodded. He knew that patience was important. Now Will used the slow printer again. It did not need to be fast. It just needed to be done.

Lena found the last sheet of paper in the tray. It was the only sheet left. Lena pulled it out slowly. It was a big sheet of paper. She held it up. "What will I print?" thought Lena. She turned the printer on. The printer took the big sheet. It printed a picture of a duck. The duck was smiling. Lena looked at the picture. She loved it. She put the picture on her wall. The big sheet was gone. Now the tray was empty. But Lena had a happy surprise. Inside the tray was a small bell. The bell rang when Lena pressed a key. "Ding!" said the bell. Lena laughed. The bell and the duck made her smile. She gave the bell a big hug. Everything was okay. There was room for more paper. And a bell to ring for fun.

Rosa turned on the printer. The printer began to print. Page after page after page. The pages flew out fast. Rosa tried to stop it. She hit the button. The printer did not stop. Pages kept coming. Rosa was scared. "Oh no," she said. Pages covered the floor. Rosa jumped on one page. Then she jumped on another. An ant saw all the pages. The ant was scared too. "Jump away!" said the ant. Rosa jumped. The ant jumped. Pages popped up everywhere. Rosa grabbed a big sheet of paper. She wrapped the ant in the paper. "Hold tight," said Rosa. The ant was safe inside the paper. Rosa pushed the paper into the trash bin. Then she pressed the stop button. The printer stopped. Rosa breathed out. She wiped her hands. She picked up the ant gently. The ant was okay. Rosa learned to watch carefully next time.

A mouse lived behind the office printer. The mouse visited every day. The warm paper was soft under the mouse's feet. Lena heard a tiny squeak. "Hello, mouse," said Lena. The mouse looked up. "Hello, Lena," said the mouse. The printer hummed softly. The mouse liked the warm hum. Lena poured some water near the mouse. "Drink this," said Lena. The mouse drank. Lena gave the mouse a piece of bread. The mouse ate. Lena always visited the mouse. She brought food and water. The mouse was her friend. One day Lena brought a picture of a duck. The duck looked so happy. "Can you see the duck?" asked Lena. The mouse shook its head. "No," said the mouse. Lena showed the picture again. "Look at the duck." The mouse sniffled and ate more bread. Lena smiled. She knew the mouse would love the duck too. The mouse visited every day after that.

Sara had a tiny house with a small garden. Sara wanted to print a very big picture of her dog. She put the paper in the printer, but the printer was too small. The paper got stuck. Sara tried again but the printer could not hold the big picture. She kicked the printer gently. The printer pushed out a small piece of paper. Sara printed a smaller picture instead. She hung the small picture above her house. Her dog looked at it and wagged its tail.

Mr. Teacher needed papers for all the children. She put a big block of paper in the printer. But the printer did not work. It made no sound at all. A bird flew into the room and landed on the printer. "Help," said Mr. Teacher. The bird looked at the quiet machine. Then the bird tapped the side of the printer with its beak. The printer hummed and began to print. All the children were happy. They each got their own paper.

It was raining outside, and the sky was gray. Finn wanted to print a sunny picture because it was his favorite day. He put the shell (a kind of paper) in the printer and pressed the button. The printer hummed. It printed a bright yellow sun with warm orange rays. Finn held the colorful paper up to the window. The sun looked gentle through the rain drops. Finn smiled. Even on a rainy day, he could still have a sunny picture.

A blank sheet of paper sat on a long table. It wanted to become something fun. It looked at the printer across the table. "I want to be a picture," whispered the paper. "I want to see the world," said the paper. "Come here," said the printer gently. The paper rolled into the printer. The printer took the paper and made a bright picture of a house and trees. The paper felt tired and happy. "Thank you," said the paper quietly. "You gave me a new look."

Once upon a time, a little girl named Sophie wanted to make signs for her lemonade stand. She had only one crayon left. It was very, very empty. She looked at her big box of crayons and felt sad. "I cannot make the signs," she said.

Then her mom said, "Go ask your brother to print the signs."

Sophie ran to the computer. She opened the printer. She put a piece of paper in. She pushed the green button. The printer hummed and hummed. Then it printed two signs. One said LEMONADE and one said FRESH!

Sophie picked up the signs. She took the empty crayon home. The lemonade stand was very busy that day.

Milo had an old boat. Milo wanted to show his teddy bear the boat outside. But Milo did not have any paper to print a picture of the boat.

Milo went to his friend Printer. "Can you print me a picture of my old boat?" asked Milo.

"Sure," said Printer. "I can do that!" Printer took a piece of paper. Printer put it in the machine. Printer pushed the button. Printer hummed and printed a picture of a small boat.

The picture was not perfect. It looked a bit dark. But Milo still liked it. He showed the picture to his teddy bear.

"Oh, this is wonderful!" said the teddy bear. "My friend Printer is so good!"

Milo smiled. They played together by the little lake all afternoon.

A dog named Buster wanted to read a book about fish. He sat on the floor and opened the cover.

But when he started reading, the words were all dark. Dark letters are hard to see. Buster could not read.

Buster's owner said, "Try to find your Printer. I will print the book in a light color."

Buster walked to the Printer. "Can you print me the book?" he asked.

"I sure can," said Printer. "Put the book here."

Buster put the book on the table. He pushed the button. The printer hummed. It printed a new copy of the book. Now the letters were light and easy to see.

Buster read all day long. He loved the book about fish swimming in a river.

A rabbit named Bella was very tired. Her Printer was also tired. It made a lot of funny sounds but nothing worked right.

"I am too tired," said Printer. "I cannot print today."

Bella felt sad. "Why isPrinter tired?" she asked.

"Because my paper tray is full," said Printer. "All the paper fell out into the grass."

Bella ran outside and picked up all the paper. She brought it back to Printer. She helped Printer push the papers back in.

"Thank you, Bella," said Printer. "Now I am happy again."

Printer hummed a happy song. Bella skipped around the garden with her.

Then the sun came up bright and warm. Bella did not feel sad anymore. She knew Printer would be ready for more printing tomorrow.

A rabbit named Pip wanted to fly paper airplanes. Pip found a piece of paper on the floor. It was a little wet from the rain.

Pip looked at the wet paper. "This paper is so wet," he said. "I cannot make a good airplane."

His friend Milo had a Printer. Milo could print new paper. Milo printed a fresh piece of paper.

Pip dried the wet paper on a warm rock. Then he folded it into a airplane shape. Pip jumped up. The airplane flew across the room.

It flew past a cow standing in a field outside the window!

"Did you see that cow?" said Pip.

"I saw it!" said Milo. "That cow never stops asking questions. You know why? Because cows always answer everyone. That is their job."

Pip laughed. His airplane flew higher and higher. It landed on Milo's nose.

They both smiled.

A car named Sparky lost its favorite red ball at the park. Sparky was very angry. His wheels turned red and black. The car did not want to play.

Sparky's driver found a big piece of poster paper. "Let us print a poster," said the driver. "We will look for the red ball at the park."

They put the poster in the Printer. The Printer hummed. It printed a big poster with WANTED: RED BALL written on it in bright letters.

The driver hung the poster on a tree. Other cars and trucks came by. Everyone looked at the poster.

Suddenly a small bird landed near the tree. The bird saw something shiny under a bench. The bird looked at the poster. "Yes! A red ball!" said the bird.

The driver ran to the bench. The red ball was there! Sparky was so happy. He ran around the park, chasing his red ball.

Sparky gave the red ball back to his driver. Then Sparky skipped and danced all afternoon.

Jill had a new printer at home. It was very noisy and it did not want to work yet. Jill was sad. "Why does it not print?" Jill asked her mom. Her mom said, "Maybe it is looking for its first page. Let me try." Jill put a cup on the paper tray. The printer hummed, then beeped. A picture came out! It showed a big cake with candles. It was so cold in the room that the ink did not move right. The cake looked blurry. Jill cried softly. But then her mom said, "We can print again. It will try again." Jill wiped her eyes. She printed the picture once more. This time the cake looked better. She smiled. The printer hummed happily and printed the next page too.

A frog sat on a button. He wanted to print a picture of his lily pad home. He pressed the button. But nothing came out. He pressed the button again. Still nothing. The light blinked red, then red, then red. It was a dry day. The air was too still. The frog felt tired. "I want to show my friend," he said. "Maybe I need water," his friend the cat said. The cat sat near the machine. After a while, a small drop fell from the top. A tiny sheet came out. It was flat and dry. The frog smiled. He held up the paper. It was his lily pad. He could share it with his friend. The lesson was: wait a moment when things do not print right away.

It was a very cold morning. The wind blew outside. Inside, a girl named Lily set up her printer. She put a blank sheet of paper into the tray. She wanted to print a picture of the sea. She pressed the button. The printer hummed warm. Then warm paper came out, but it stopped halfway. The paper was stuck. Lily pulled, but it did not come. She tried again and again. Finally, she said, "Wait, please stop." She took deep breaths. Then she gently pushed the page with both hands. The paper slid out slowly. It was nice and smooth. The sea looked blue and green. Lily held the paper close. The warmth from the printer made the paper feel soft. She could draw waves on it later. She hugged the warm paper and ate her breakfast. She did not mind the cold morning.

Bella had a little puppy named Pup. Pup loved printed pages. One day, Pup found a sheet on the floor. It was a picture of a moon. Pup danced across the room. He danced under the table. He danced right at the printer. "Oh, what is this?" Pup barked. Bella came running. "Pup, come here!" Pup ran right past her. He grabbed the moon page and ran off the house. Bella chased him. She ran hard. She ran fast. She looked back. Pup was gone. "Help me find my dog!" Bella told her mom. Her mom went to the park. She called Pup's name. At last, they found Pup sitting by a tree. He held the moon page tight. The paper was torn. It was a hard lesson for Pup. He learned to leave pages alone. Bella gave him a bone and they walked home together.

Tom wanted to print a picture of a lake. He put crayons beside the printer. He printed the picture. It was beautiful. But Tom's friend Sam also wanted to print. They both waited. Then Tom saw Sam take the picture away. "That is mine!" Tom said. Sam said, "Look, I am coloring it!" Sam colored over Tom's red fish with blue. Tom was sad. His fish turned purple. "This is not fair," Tom said quietly. His mom heard. She said, "Let us print another one. We can share the colors." Tom and Sam each got a fresh page. Now they could color the lake together. They chose different colors for different fish. They shared the crayons. They made two pretty pictures. Tom was happy again. They hung them both on the wall side by side.

Little Ink was a drop of ink inside the printer. It wanted to see the world. It looked at the dark tray. It did not like being alone. "I want to go out," Ink said softly. The printer did not answer. Ink pushed against the wall of the tray. It pushed hard. Then something happened. A thin line pushed out with Ink. It slid out onto the table. Ink saw a mirror on the desk. It looked at its tiny shape. It was still very small. But now it was outside the printer. It could see the room. It saw the mirror and the shiny table. It was free. A little girl picked it up. She put it on a piece of paper. Then she printed a word with it. Ink went on the paper. It moved across the white page. It made a mark. It was still tiny, but it had seen the mirror and the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little house with a small door and a big yard. In the house lived Milo. Milo had a desk by the window. On the desk sat a printer. The printer was very quiet all day. Milo came home from school and sat down. He looked at the printer. "I wish you had a name," Milo said. He went to his room. He found a tiny paper cow on his desk. Milo took it out of the box. Then he put it into the printer. The printer made a sound. It took paper and printed a picture of a cow. Milo smiled. Now the printer is named Little Cow. It feels happy when Milo talks to it.

Once upon a time, the sun was warm and bright in the sky. Milo wanted to find his cat, Whiskers. Whiskers ran away. Milo felt sad. He knew Whiskers would come back if he could see a poster. Milo opened the drawer and found some blank paper. He put paper into the printer. Milo drew a picture of Whiskers on the paper. It was a light, happy drawing. He put the paper into the printer. But the paper was too light. The printer did not work right. It beeped and made a mess. Milo tried again. Still nothing good happened. He put one more piece of paper in. The printer worked! It printed the poster very well. Milo hung the poster on the wall. Later that night, Milo saw Whiskers under the bed. Milo cried with joy. Whiskers was back.

One day, a fresh sheet of paper sat on the desk. It was blank. It felt empty. "I want to be something," the paper said softly. A teddy bear sat nearby. The teddy bear looked at the paper. "You can be a drawing," the teddy bear said gently. The paper did not believe it. Milo came into the room. He picked up the paper. He put it into the printer. The machine hummed. It took the paper and printed a smiling sun. The paper felt surprised. A sun was not a picture of anything special. Milo looked at the paper. "This is a good start," Milo said. The paper smiled. Now it had a beginning. Maybe later, it would become something even more beautiful.

Milo had a calculator and a printer. They were both old friends. One day, Milo wanted to print silly jokes. He typed funny words on the keyboard. The printer hummed and beeped. It printed a joke about a dog. Milo laughed out loud. Then he typed another joke. The printer printed a joke about a bird. Milo cleaned the paper tray because there were many jokes on the papers. He was careful as he cleaned. "Be careful," Milo said to himself. After cleaning, Milo typed one more joke. The printer printed a joke about milk. Milo laughed again. He cleaned the tray once more. The printer kept printing jokes. Now Milo has many joke papers. Every day, Milo reads them and laughs. The jokes are very funny.

Tom walked outside in the snow. The snow was soft and white. Tom wanted to make paper snowflakes for his window. He found a leaf on the ground. Tom picked up the leaf. It was dry and brown. "A leaf is not a good thing to cut," Tom thought. But Tom was brave. He put the leaf into the printer. The printer hummed. It printed a shape that looked like a snowflake. Tom saw the snowflake on the paper. It was a little wrong. The paper flake had lines that did not look like snow. Tom looked at the leaf again. The leaf had a curve in it. Tom turned the leaf sideways. Then he pressed it harder. The printer made a new snowflake. This one looked better. Tom hung the snowflakes on his window. They looked like real snow falling outside.

Once upon a time, a small robot sat beside a broken printer. The printer made a bad sound. It would not print. The robot had a round head and four round arms. "Don't worry," the robot told the printer. The robot walked slowly around the printer. It looked at every button. First, it checked the paper tray. Paper was not sitting right. The robot pushed it back. Then it checked the ink light. The light was off. The robot found a tiny tool and cleaned the light. Next, the robot looked at the gate where paper comes out. The gate was stuck. The robot pushed it open. Now the printer made a happy beep. It printed a picture of a star. The robot smiled. "Good job," the printer said. The robot clapped its hands. Everything was fixed.

Once upon a time, Grandpa wanted to print a picture of all his family. He sat at the desk and pushed the button. The printer hummed. But it did not start right away. It was lazy. "Hmm," the printer said. "That is too big. Too slow." Grandpa waited and waited. Finally, the printer printed. A big family photo came out. Grandpa held it up. "Look," he said. "This is my whole family." His wife looked at the photo. She smiled. "You should print this every day," she said. Grandpa nodded. He pushed the button again that night. The printer was still lazy. But Grandpa pushed again. Then again. The printer slowly printed a new picture each day. Grandpa learned that pushing harder helps even when things are slow.

There was a house on a quiet street. On the front door, someone printed the word house. Then they printed it again. And again. And again. The paper was torn into tiny pieces.
