Every piece had the word house on it. A little bird saw the pieces on the ground. "What is that?" the bird asked. A cat ran by. "I see the word house," the cat said. They looked around the house. No one was home. The printer kept printing. "House! House! House!" it said. The pieces covered everything. The cat could not find its tail. The bird could not find its food. A kind neighbor heard the noise. She came with a broom. She swept the pieces away. The printer stopped. "Oops," it said. Now the house is clean and the cat and bird are happy again.

One night, the printer woke up. It was not morning yet, but the printer could not sleep. "I want to eat something," it said. A kind woman left a card near the printer. The card had a drawing of a cake on it. The printer ate the card. Then it ate another card. Then another. It wanted more cards. The woman had no more cards. The printer was mean now. It kept printing until all the paper in the room was gone. There was nothing left to eat. The printer sat very sad. "I wish I could sleep again," it said softly. The woman came back. She brought a real cake from the kitchen. She set it next to the printer. The printer sniffed the cake. Then it took a small bite. It went back to sleep. The cake was gone too. But the printer felt better inside. Even a mean printer can rest when it eats good food.

Little Emma sat on her bed. She was sleepy. Her mom gave her a book. "Read your story," her mom said. Emma read the story out loud. But she got tired. She closed the book. She wanted to rest. A soft light came from the wall. "Do not worry," the light said. A friendly printer came out from behind the wall. It had a warm glow. "I will tell you a story," it said. The printer hummed and printed words on the bed sheet. The words made pictures float above the bed. A little dragon flew across the sky on the bed. A bear walked through a forest on the bed. Emma listened with her eyes closed. She fell asleep. In her dream, the dragon bear and Emma were friends. When Emma woke, the bed was still warm. The friendly printer was still there. "Good morning," it said. Emma smiled. "Thank you for reading me to sleep," she said.

A family wanted a new printer. They bought one. It was bright blue and shiny. A dog named Biscuit ran over. "What are you?" Biscuit asked. "I am a new printer," the machine said. "Can I print a picture of you?" Biscuit barked. "Yes," the printer said. It printed a picture of Biscuit. Biscuit was so proud. Now every day, Biscuit would ask the printer to print him. The family also printed pictures of their cat, their garden, and their tree. The printer was smooth and worked well. No jams, no problems. One day, the family looked up at the sky. The moon was bright. A star shone next to the moon. "Look," the father said. "We should print a picture of the stars." The printer printed a beautiful night scene. The family hung it above the table. Biscuit curled up under the picture. Everyone was happy. A new printer came into a family, and the family became even happier.

Two printers lived side by side. One was old and orange. It made small prints. The other was young and blue. It made big prints. The orange printer was tired. Its paper feed was stuck. "My feed is dry," it said. The blue printer heard. "Let me help," it said. The blue printer rolled close. It pushed gentle paper into the orange printer's mouth. The orange printer ate the paper. Then it pushed the paper out again. The paper was not right. The orange printer tried again. Soon the feed worked. "Thank you," the orange printer said. They both printed the same page. The orange printer made soft lines. The blue printer made bold lines. Together, they made the best picture. A little girl came to the table. "Can you print my picture?" she asked. Both printers pushed the button together. The paper went in. The printer hummed. The printer beeped. A bright picture came out. The girl smiled. The two printers high-fived, which meant they were best friends. Paper and machines work best when they help each other.

Once upon a time, a cat named Pip sat on the floor beside a big printer. The printer hummed and beeped. It was a busy day at the office. People brought paper into the room. The printer took the paper and printed letters. Pip watched. She did not like the loud sounds. She wanted to sleep. The printer kept printing. It was tired of printing. Pip walked to the table. She jumped on the table. She curled up under the machine. She closed her eyes. The printer took one last piece of paper. Then it stopped. Everything was quiet. Pip was warm. Pip was safe. The end.

Ivy had a big box of seeds. She wanted to print a picture of a seedling. She put paper into the printer. She pressed the button. The printer hummed. It began to print. But then the ink ran out. The picture came out flat and empty. Ivy felt sad. She looked at her blank paper. She looked at the friendly face of the machine. "Do not worry," said the machine. "I can bring you more ink soon." Ivy smiled. The next day, a new bottle of ink arrived. The printer printed again. The seedling was beautiful. Ivy was happy. The end.

Beep wanted to print a picture for Grandma. He picked colorful paper. He put it in the tray. He pressed the button. "Hello, Grandma," Beep thought. The printer began to work. It took the paper and made a bright picture. Beep saw a soft pillow in the picture. Grandma would love that. But then the paper ran out. Beep felt worried. He told the printer, "Print just one more picture." The printer hummed softly. It pulled more paper. The picture turned out nice. Beep gave the picture to Grandma. Grandma held it close to her face. It was a very friendly gift. The end.

A sun rose in the window. The sun was bright. A printer stood by the door. The old room was too small. The sun felt too hot. The printer said, "I need a new room." "I cannot move," said the printer. "My legs are stuck." The cat said, "Let me help." The cat pushed. Nothing happened. The cat pulled. Nothing happened. The sun said, "Wait here." The sun reached its warm light over the printer. The light moved the heavy machine. One step. Two steps. The printer was on the new floor. The sun smiled. The room was nicer now. But when the sun went to sleep, the printer was alone. The printer was lonely. The end.

Max had a sister. Her name was Lily. Max wanted to print a picture of his pet duck. Lily helped him. They put paper into the printer. Max pressed the button. The printer hummed. It made a pink picture. In the picture, the duck looked happy. Lily clapped her hands. "That is the nicest duck," she said. Max gave the picture to Lily. Lily held it up. The duck seemed to quack. Lily laughed. She put the picture on the wall. Every day, Lily looked at the picture. She felt loved. Max was happy. The picture made them both smile. The end.

Max sat near the gate of the house. Inside was the printer. Max wanted to print a story for his fish. His friend Sam said, "You must wait for your turn." "But I want to press the button," said Max. "Not yet," said Sam. Max felt sad. The printer hummed inside. Max missed his fish. Max missed the water. The gate opened. Sam went back inside. Max stepped forward. He pressed the button. The printer started to print. A picture came out. It was a picture of a fish swimming in blue water. Max showed the picture to his fish. The fish poked its nose at the paper. Max smiled. His heart was happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Jack had a big, old printer on his table. One day, Jack put paper into the printer. The paper tray was empty. "Oh no," said Jack. "The tray has no paper." Jack looked around the room. He saw some sheep in a green field near the window. The sheep stood quietly by the grass. Jack walked to the window and looked out. He saw the sheep run past the glass. Jack smiled. The sheep ran all the way to the front of the house. Jack put more paper into the tray. Then he pressed the button. The printer hummed and printed a picture of the sheep. Jack clapped his hands. The sheep were happy again.

There was a girl named Lily. Lily had a small printer on her desk. One day, Lily took a piece of paper out of the printer. It was still warm. She folded it into a boat shape. The paper was brown. Lily pushed the boat into the big puddle near her house. The paper boat swam across the water. It went under the lily pads and float flowers. A little fish watched from below. "You are going so fast," whispered the fish. Lily laughed and threw the boat back. The paper boat swam even faster this time. Lily giggled. The sun was warm on her head. She had a wonderful time on the puddle with her paper boat.

A little cat named Mia sat on the floor near the printer. The printer had been printing all day. It made a loud beep. The light on top turned red. The printer was tired. Mia yawned and stretched. "I am too tired," said the printer softly. Its gears stopped moving. The light stayed red. Mia jumped up and curled up right on top of the printer. She purred loudly. The printer hummed happily now. A gentle warmth came from Mia's soft fur. The red light turned to a soft glow. The printer felt better than ever. Mia kept her warm body on the machine while it rested. The printer woke up smiling and ready to print again.

There was a friendly printer named Inky. Inky liked to print pretty pictures. One day, Inky printed a picture of a puppy. But the puppy looked sad. "I am sorry," said Inky softly. Inky pressed its buttons gently. Then it printed a new picture. This one was colored in pretty pinks and blues. It was the most beautiful puppy anyone had ever seen. A boy walked up to the table. He saw the pretty puppy drawing. He smiled. "Thank you, Inky," he said. Inky printed another drawing for the boy's mother. She liked the pretty colors. Inky beeped happily. Everyone was so glad that Inky had learned to say sorry and print nice things.

One morning the sun was bright. A bird landed on the windowsill of the room. The bird looked at the printer with its round yellow eyes. The bird flew down and gave the machine a big kiss. Its beak touched the paper tray. The toner was running low. The machine made a grumpy sound. The light turned dull grey. "No no no," said the printer. A boy heard the sad sounds. He went to the printer. He shook the box that held the toner. There was barely any left. "What can I do?" asked the boy. The bird sang a happy song. The boy smiled. He put fresh toner into the printer. Then he pressed the button. The printer worked hard and printed lots of pages. Everyone was glad the sun came out and the printer had new toner.

A little mouse named Inky lived under a door. Inky wanted to find treasure. He found a map inside a book. The map was dry and tattered. Inky held it carefully. He walked to the old printer on the table. "Print me a copy," said Inky. The printer hummed and printed a second map. It was dry just like the first one. Inky studied both maps carefully. He found a path through the hole under the door. He crawled down the dark hallway. At the end of the hall was a shiny chest. Inky opened the chest. Gold coins sparkled everywhere! Inky cheered. The printer beeped with joy. The treasure was real and Inky got to keep it forever.

Once upon a time there was a cake waiting to be printed. The cake had three soft, fluffy clouds on top. A little girl wanted to print the cake in a picture so she could look at it. She opened the window wide and held the page out. But the wind was strong and the page flew away out the window! The girl laughed and patted her round tummy. Then she went back to get more paper. She printed the cake again and again and again. The cake stayed on the table. The girl smiled and ate a piece of cake.

Once upon a time a little boy had a house he liked. His friend came over. The friend said thank you and wanted to print a note to put in the house. The boy did not want to wait for the printer. He just went away to play. Soon his mom called him. "Go print the thank-you note!" she said. The boy was lazy. He went to the printer but the paper was jammed. He tried again and again. The note never came out. He felt sad inside. Later the friend came back and gave him a big hug. The boy said sorry and printed the note that night. He put the note on the house door. The house was happy again.

A rabbit lived near a house with a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to print a birthday card for the rabbit. She fed an apple to the printer and pushed the button. The printer hummed and took the apple. It made the card. The card had a rabbit on it. Lily put the card in an envelope. The rabbit came to the house. Lily opened the envelope. The rabbit looked at the card. The rabbit saw its own face. "I am special," said the rabbit. Lily shared the cake with the rabbit. They ate cake together. The rabbit jumped and played. They were happy friends.

Finn loved to print things. One day Finn wanted to print a menu for a pretend restaurant. He sat down at the printer. He typed the words onto the paper. But the paper had a cut in it. A mean snip from the edge ruined the menu. Finn felt sad. Then he noticed a bike tied to the table leg. The bike had a sharp nail. Finn thought about fixing the nail first. He used a brush to clean the table. Then he used the sharp part of the bike nail to poke a tiny hole in the bad spot. He glued the paper over the hole. The menu looked good again. Finn printed the new menu and hung it on the wall. People would like the food.

Tim had two machines on his desk. One was a printer. The other was a scanner. They were best friends. Tim printed a warm picture of a teddy bear. The scanner sat beside the printer. Sheep walked past the desk outside. The printer and scanner talked quietly. "We should print together," said the scanner. "Yes," said the printer. So they printed one picture after another. The picture of the teddy bear was warm and soft. Tim clapped his hands. "You two are great," he said. Then the printer heard a new job come in. "Help me print something new," asked the printer. The scanner smiled and stood up. They both got ready. They worked side by side. They made many nice pictures. Tim was happy that his friends worked so well together.

Tim built a tall stack of paper. He stacked them up high. Each paper was thick and heavy. He read each paper to make sure it was neat. Then he stepped back to look. The stack wobbled. It shook a lot. Tim worried. The bottom paper was warm from the printer light. It started to curl. The whole stack began to fall. Papers tumbled everywhere. Tim picked up the papers one by one. He sorted them into piles. "Don't stack papers too high," he told himself. He used a brush to sweep up the tiny bits. Then he printed a picture of a flower. He put the flower on the windowsill. The flower looked bright and warm. Tim smiled. He learned that stacks can fall if they are too tall.

Max had a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers was orange and fluffy. Max wanted to print a picture of Whiskers so he could hang it on the wall. "I want a picture of my cat," Max said. The machine hummed and printed the page. The picture came out, but it looked messy. Some parts were shiny and red. "That does not look like my cat," Max said. "It looks like a bug." Whiskers jumped onto the table. "Meow! I do not like bugs," Whiskers said. The machine beeped. "I am sorry," the machine said. "The ink ran out halfway through." Max felt upset. He wanted a nice picture of Whiskers. He picked up the messy page. Then he picked up a fresh sheet. The machine printed again. This time, the picture was clean and shiny. Max clapped his hands. "Look, Whiskers!" he said. Whiskers sniffed the picture. "It smells like you," Whiskers said softly. Max hugged the picture to the wall. Now every day, they both looked at Whiskers together.

Once upon a time, there was a kind little printer named Priya. She lived in a dark office. The office was very quiet. Shadows moved on the walls. Priya was afraid. She did not like the dark. One night, Priya tried to print a picture of a flower for her friend. But the power went off. The office was all dark now. Priya could not see anything. Her buttons did not light up. "I cannot find the button," Priya said softly. She was afraid to press anything. A small bee flew near her. The bee buzzed and flew around her head. "Do not be scared," the bee said. "Light is coming back. Stay still and wait." The bee landed on Priya's button. A tiny spark glowed. Then the lights came on. Priya could see again. She printed the flower picture. It was beautiful. She gave the picture to her friend. Her friend smiled. "Thank you," her friend said. Priya felt brave now. She knew the dark would never scare her again.

Max had a lamp on his table. It made everything bright. One day, Max wanted to play. He picked up a sheet of paper from the table. It was very cold. "What is this?" Max asked. "It is a special paper," the machine said. "I can print with it." Max picked up the paper. He folded it into a shape like a wing. Then he threw it into the air. It flew up, turned, and zoomed across the room. "Look at that!" Max said. The paper airplane flew far. It even went under the lamp. Max laughed. The next day, Max picked another sheet. He printed a picture of a bird instead. The bird was sparkly and bright. Max folded the page into a paper airplane. He threw it again. It flew the same way as before. "Same thing happens," Max said. Max learned that paper makes good airplanes, whether it is printed or plain. He played and laughed every afternoon.

One rainy morning, Max heard the rain on the roof. Max wanted to print a picture of his dog, Biscuit. Biscuit was brown and curly. "I need to print a picture of Biscuit for the wall," Max said. The machine started to print. But the wind blew a drop of water onto the paper. Now the paper was wet. The machine did not like wet paper. "Uh oh," the machine said. "This paper is too wet." The ink ran away. The picture came out all blurry. Max felt sad. "Oh no, oh no," Max said. "The picture is ruined." Biscuit came out and lay on the floor. "Rain makes everything messy," Biscuit said. "But I like the rain." Max looked at Biscuit. "I want a clean picture," Max said. The machine tried again, but the paper was still wet. It did not work. Max sat down on the floor. Biscuit licked his hand. Max held Biscuit tight. They stayed together while the rain fell. At last, the rain stopped. The next morning, Max found a fresh sheet. He printed a clean picture of Biscuit. He hung it by the window where the sunlight came in. Now Biscuit and the picture could be friends inside, even when it rained.

Once upon a time, there was a big printer named Big and a small printer named Small. Big was loud. Small was quiet. They both sat on the same table. One day, a sparkly bee flew past the window. Small saw the bee and blinked its eyes. "Look," Small whispered. "Something is flying by." Big did not blink. Big just hummed loudly. "Bees are busy," Big said. Then the bee landed on Big's side. It buzzed once and flew away. Small blinked again. "She almost came here," Small said. Big looked down. "Why do you care?" Big asked. "Maybe we should print a picture of a bee," Small said. They both started to work. They printed a big bee, then a tiny bee. The small bee was cute. The big bee was strong. Everyone liked both bees. The bee flew around the room, visiting each printer. "You are both wonderful," the bee said. From that day, Big and Small worked together. They printed all kinds of things: pictures of birds, flowers, and even other printers. They learned that being small does not mean you are less important.

Lena sat at the desk. She wanted to print a picture of a bird. She pulled the handle. The printer hummed and beeped. Out came the paper. Lena took it and put it on the table. She had crayons. She drew green leaves on the bird. She drew red apples too. Then she said, "Look, Mom! I drew a bird!" Mom clapped. Lena was glad. The bird flew in her hands. She held the paper up high. It was a good picture.

Lena printed a boat. She cut the paper. She made a boat with tape. A bear came out of the printer. Lena took the bear and taped it to the boat. The boat floated on the water. Lena was so happy. Then the wind blew. The boat went under the water. The bear went down too. Lena cried. But then the boat came back up. It was still there. The bear was safe. Lena was sad but also glad. The boat was fresh again.

Ted loved the printer. He looked out the window. The room was full of balls. A soccer ball rolled near the printer. Ted said, "I want to play outside." He kicked the soccer ball. It rolled into the printer. The printer hummed. The soccer ball got squished. Ted laughed. He said, "The ball is inside now." The printer beeped. The ball came back out. Ted picked it up. He kicked it again. Now the ball was outside again. Ted was happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She wanted to print a picture for her grandma. Grandma loved pretty pictures and a cake, too. Mia ran to the printer table. "I need to print something for you," she said. The printer hummed and took a sheet of paper. It printed the picture. It was special because it had a big pink cake on it! Grandma smiled and said, "Thank you, Mia." Mia was happy. She gave the paper to grandma. Grandma cut out the picture and hung it on her wall.

A little printer lived in a house. One day the house was very small for the printer. The printer said, "I want to move to a new room." Mom said, "We will help you find a new home." They walked through the house together. They looked at every room. Finally they found a big new room. The printer said, "I am so happy here!" Mom put the printer on the table. The printer hummed and said, "Hello, new room." The house was warm and bright now. The printer felt right at home. Everyone was glad.

It was winter and it snowed. Lily saw the sun through the snow. "Let us print some snowflakes," she said. She sat at the printer table. The printer took a white sheet of paper. It printed six little snowflakes. They were smooth and round. Lily cut them with scissors. Each snowflake was different. One was like a star. One was like a flower. Lily clapped her hands and laughed. She hung all the snowflakes in the window. The sun came out and made the snow sparkle. "Look at that!" said Lily. Everything was perfect.

A boy named Tim used the printer every day. He loved to print pictures of his tree. But one day the printer printed the wrong thing. Instead of a tree, it printed a scary picture. A dark black tree with no leaves. Tim looked at the clock on the wall. He felt sad. "That is not what I wanted," he said quietly. His mom came and helped him fix the paper. They erased the wrong print and tried again. This time the printer made a happy green tree. Tim smiled and hugged his mom. The printer was sorry too. Now Tim always checked the clock before printing.

On the printer table there was a tiny drop of ink. Its name was Dot. Dot wanted to see the world outside the paper. "I want to go to the sky," said Dot. But Dot could only sit on the table. A cat jumped onto the table. Dot hid behind the cat's tail. The cat watched Dot say, "Please be quiet." Then Dot heard a funny sound. It was a bird singing outside. Dot felt shiny and bright inside. Even though Dot stayed on the table, Dot could hear the whole world. The cat purred softly. "You are brave, Dot," said the cat. Dot was not sad anymore.

The school needed many copies for the art show. The printer was broken. The printer could not hum or print. "Oh no," said the teacher. The printer looked up and said, "I am sorry I am not working." A little frog hopped over. "Don't worry," said the frog. "We will watch you carefully." The frog helped fix the printer. It tightened a loose wire. Soon the printer was back. It printed beautiful purple pictures of the frog and the school. Everyone clapped. The frog said, "You fixed me, friend." The printer smiled. It learned that even when it is broken, it can do great things again.

Once upon a time, a new printer sat on a big table. It was very new. It was not old or tired. A little hand held a small sheet of paper. The baby pushed the button. "Beep beep," said the printer. It took the paper and made a tiny page. The page had one line of black marks on it. It was the very first thing it ever printed. A smiling face was on the page. The baby clapped her hands. The printer felt so happy. It hummed a happy song. The first page was the best page ever.

Ann had a neat little flower in a pot. She wanted to print it for her teacher. She put the paper in the printer. The wheel turned round and round. The machine beeped once. Then it stopped. "Oh no," said Ann. The flower paper was blank. Nothing came out. Ann cried a little. The machine did not know why it stopped. "I am sorry," the machine said softly. "I beeped too loud. I hope that helps." Ann patted the cold metal box. Then she put fresh paper inside again. The wheel turned. Beep. Beep. Color came out. A red flower stood on the page. Ann smiled. The machine beeped happy sounds. They were friends now.

An owl slept on the printer table at night. The owl was very busy. She pulled a long feather from her wing. She pulled another feather. She pulled until her wing hurt. "Too much!" she hooted. The printer heard. "Beep beep," it said. The owl looked at the empty tray. She pulled one last feather. Then she pulled the paper tray away. It fell down with a thump. The owl flew away with all the feathers. The printer sat quiet and still. No more feathers could fall. The paper tray stayed empty. The printer just waited for a grown-up to come home.

A little balloon blew itself into a crumpled ball. It rolled under the table. It bumped the warm printer. "Ouch," the balloon said. The printer hummed softly. "I can help," the machine said. It took the crumpled ball of paper. The machine smoothed the paper flat. One edge was still bent. The machine pulled it tight. Then it pulled the other edge. Flat again! The balloon looked at its new smooth shape. "Thank you," it said. A picture of the sun was on the page. The balloon floated up to the sky. It did not need to be crumpled anymore. Everything was good again.

An orange cat went to sleep on the warm printer. The printer hummed a slow song. The cat liked the heat. She curled up right on top. But then she started to cry. "Ouch, my fur is too hot," she mewed. The printer felt bad. "I will stop now," it said softly. The printer turned off its light. The room got cool. The cat wiggled her tail. Her fur stopped burning. She purred a happy song. She climbed down and walked away. The printer cooled off and waited for the next job.

Finn wanted to print a big apple tree. He put a big apple in the tray. He pressed the red button. "Beep beep," said the printer. The machine tried to print the tree. But the tray was too small. The apple pushed the paper up. The printer shook hard. "No no no," Finn said. The apple rolled out of the tray. The printer sat sad and quiet. The apple hit the floor. "I cannot make a tree," the printer whined. Finn picked up the apple. He put it back. He made the tray bigger. Then he pressed the button again. Beep. Beep. The apple went back in. The printer made the biggest, brightest apple tree ever. Finn smiled.

Once upon a time, a family got a new printer. It was a strong gift for mom and baby. The printer was small and round. It sat on the table by the window. Mom set paper in the tray. Then she pressed a button. The printer hummed and hummed. But it did not print. A bird landed on the table. The bird knocked the paper out of the tray! The paper rolled away. Mom laughed and picked up the paper. She put it back in the tray. Now the printer printed a green circle on the paper. Baby clapped her hands. They could share the fun with the new printer.

One day, a little printer wanted to look outside the window. "I want to see the train," said the printer. A soccer ball rolled near the table. The soccer ball bounced and bounced. The printer tried to play with the soccer ball but did not know how. The printer beeped a loud beep. The soccer ball went rolling away again. Then a train went past outside the window. "Wow!" said the printer. It watched the train go by. It remembered that trains are fast. Now the printer had a friend inside a picture. It shared the picture with the soccer ball.

A printer and an owl were best friends. The owl lived on the shelf above the table. The owl was green and big. "I want to see the dog," said the owl one morning. "The dog is far away," said the printer. "I can push the door open!" said the owl. The owl pushed the door. But the door only opened a little bit. Then the owl pushed harder. The door did not move. The owl looked sad. The printer felt bad. "I can help you," said the printer. The printer took out more paper. With paper under the door, the door pulled back all the way. The owl could go see the dog now. The owl was happy.

One sunny morning, Bo got to press the big button on the printer. Bo was very excited. "I will print my picture," said Bo. The sun made the room bright. Bo put paper in the tray. Bo pressed the button. The printer hummed. But nothing came out. Bo pulled the paper out. The paper was blank. Bo tried again. The second paper was also blank. Bo felt sad. Bo pulled the third paper out too. It was blank too. "Oh no," said Bo. A friend came by. "Are you okay?" asked the friend. "No," said Bo. "I wish I could print something real." The friend smiled and gave Bo a drawing. Bo felt better.

A purple printer worked in a dark office at night. The printer was sad. "It is so dark here," said the printer. Rain started to fall outside. The rain taps on the window. "I do not like the dark," said the printer. A little light turned on. It was a sun lamp. The sun lamp glowed warm and yellow. The printer saw the glow. "That is beautiful," said the printer. The printer felt warm and happy. The rain stopped. The sun lamp stayed on. The printer did not feel afraid anymore. Now it could print pictures at night. Everyone was glad.

Bo's old printer was very slow. It took a long time to print each page. "I am so slow," said the old printer. One day, Bo wanted to print a picture of the sun. The sun was bright and hot. Bo put paper in the tray. Bo pressed the button. The old printer printed a line. Then another line. Then another line. After a long time, the last line appeared. Bo pulled the paper out. The picture of the sun was almost done. The printer could not finish. Then a bell rang. It was Bo's friend. "Let me help you," said the friend. The friend finished the picture. Bo was happy. The cool old printer did not mind waiting. It was glad to help.

Once upon a time, Jade wanted to print a pretty picture for her cat. She took the last sheet of paper from the tray. The lamp on the printer lit up bright. Jade shook the paper, but it fell down. A cat was sleeping on the floor. It did not move. Jade waited and waited. Finally, the printer hummed. It printed the picture. Now Jade had two pretty pictures. She gave one to her cat. The cat purred and played with the paper. Jade smiled. The cat was happy too.

One day, a tree had a big party. Everyone wanted to come. But nobody had an invitation. The tree said, "I need invitations." The printer heard this. "I can print them," the printer said. First, the printer printed all the invitations. Then the invitations went out to every friend. But a boy saw the invitations. He climbed up the tree to look at them. He wanted the tree's cookies more than the invitations. He forgot about the party. The tree was sad. The printer felt bad. Later, the boy came back. He heard his mother calling from the door. He came down and said thank you. The tree learned that you should not take things that are not yours.

A printer loved drawing. It drew birds and stars and flowers. One day, the printer saw a crayon. The crayon was resting on a table. The printer wanted to draw like the crayon. "I can draw too," the printer said. So the printer tried to draw with its ink. But the ink was too thick. The lines were sad and messy. The printer looked at the crayon. The crayon drew smooth, happy lines. The printer felt very sad. "What is wrong with me?" the printer asked. A bee buzzed by. "You have lots of ink," the bee said. "You are good at printing," the bee said. The printer felt better. It printed the bee's words onto a piece of paper. Then it drew a pretty picture all by itself. It was different, but it was beautiful.

A puppy heard a sound outside. A frog was sitting near the door. The puppy ran right past the frog to the door. The frog wanted to play with the puppy, but the puppy did not hear the frog. The puppy ran far away with a printed page in its mouth. The page had a picture of a bone. The puppy thought it was real. The frog was left behind. "Oh no," the frog said. The frog was alone. Then the puppy heard its own name. Its mom called from inside. The puppy went back to the door. It dropped the printed page. The frog hopped over and they played together. The puppy gave the frog the paper bone. They both had fun.

At school, the duck wanted to print pictures for the class. The teacher put paper in the printer. The printer hummed and beeped. It made a picture of a duck. But then the duck heard a sound. The printer made a loud noise and made another picture. That was not what anyone wanted. The duck was scared. "We do not want a funny picture," the duck said. The printer felt silly. It tried to fix its paper tray. But it only made a mess. Paper fell everywhere. The duck told the teacher. The teacher helped clean up the papers. Then the teacher put new paper in the tray. The printer made nice pictures again. The children were happy.

A printer was very shy. It did not like noise or people looking at it. One day, the printer sat in its quiet room. It was dirty. Ink smudged its screen. It felt low. Then a bird flew in and dropped a nest on the table. The nest was messy and dirty. The printer wanted to fix the nest. It cleaned the dirt away. It smoothed the twigs. Now the nest was clean and pretty. The printer felt brave. It printed a sign that said welcome. The bird was so happy. The printer felt warm inside. It was not shy anymore. It liked being seen and used.

Once upon a time, a class at school wanted pictures of a flower for their wall. The printer was big and warm. It took a sheet of paper and began to print. A funny picture came out! A smiling sun sat next to the flower. The children clapped. But then the printer made a small sound like a sneeze, and the picture tore in half. The funny picture was now broken. The teacher looked sad. Then the printer tried again and printed another whole picture. Everyone was happy again.

Rex had a little bird friend who liked to fly high. One day Rex brought the bird to a table where a humming printer lived. The bird was flying above the table and saw the printer take a fresh sheet. The printer began to hum a sweet song. The bird liked the song so much that it landed on the paper tray. The bird sang louder. The printer could not help but make more notes while printing. A pretty picture of the bird came out on the page. Rex smiled. The bird could not fly away because its legs were stuck on the paper tray. Rex gently helped the bird hop off. Now the bird could fly again, and the printer printed one more picture just for fun.

Milo loved a teddy bear with sticky fur. Milo asked the printer to print the teddy bear. The printer beeped very loudly. It made a sound like a loud fire alarm. Milo covered his ears. The printer kept beeping and taking paper. Soon all the paper was wet and sticky. The teddy bear picture came out all crinkly and messy. Milo had to wash his hands many times. He patted the teddy bear dry but it still felt sticky. Milo learned that when you ask for something too much, things get messy. He put the teddy bear on a clean shelf. The teddy bear was still there, still soft, but now it had a small dust mark from the printer. Milo smiled and gave the teddy bear a hug anyway.

Jade had two printers. One was big and tall. The other was small and round. Jade wanted both to print a cat picture. The big printer said, "I will do it." The small printer said, "I will do it too." Both printers took paper at the same time. The big printer pushed too hard and the small printer pushed too softly. They tried to see who would win. The big printer made a sheet that was too thick. The small printer made a sheet that was too thin. The sheets did not fit together well. Jade looked at both papers. One was bold and strong. The other was light and soft. Together they made a great cat picture. Jade learned that big and small can work together. The cat looked happy on the wall.

One morning it was raining outside. The dog wanted a sunny picture for its room. The printer sat on a bench near the window. The dog heard the printer begin to print. A bright yellow sun came out first. Then blue skies. Then green grass. Then a cookie stood in the middle of the page. The dog was so happy to see a cookie on paper. But then the printer stopped. It could not print anymore. The paper was blank now. The dog looked sad. The rain kept going. The dog could not go outside either. The dog sniffled. Then the printer made a small beep and printed one last thing. It was a tiny rain cloud with a smiley face inside. The dog felt better. The dog ate the cookie on paper and wagged its tail.

Sunny was a kind teacher. She wanted to print a pie for her students to share. She fed a big sheet into the printer. The printer began to work. But the printer was slow. It took a long time. Sunny tried waiting. She tried humming a song. She tried giving the printer a glass of water. Still nothing. Finally the printer printed the pie. It was beautiful and golden. The children came closer. They took pieces of the printed pie. It was not real pie but it tasted good on paper. Everyone laughed and ate happily. Then the printer made a loud noise and a spark flew out. Sunny patted the machine gently. The printer was tired but it was smiling too. Sunny learned that helpers should rest when they are done, so they can help again later.

Once upon a time, a sun shone bright and warm on a busy office. The office had one big printer on the wall. Many people came to print their papers. One worker tried to print a horse picture. The printer did not fit right. Papers fell out all messy. The worker looked at the messy stack of papers. Then he heard a loud beep. The printer was sad too. He sat down and patted it gently. "I am sorry," he said. The printer hummed soft and happy again.papers are tricky, but they still work, and that is what matters.

A robot named Roy brought paper to the printer. A dog ran past him and barked. "Run, dog!" said Roy. The dog chased Roy around the room. Paper fell on the floor. The printer sat still and quiet. It could not print until Roy found the paper. Roy looked under a chair. He saw the paper! He handed it to the printer. The printer hummed and printed a big robot picture. Roy smiled and gave the dog a treat. A kind robot kept things going, even when things went sideways.

After everyone went home, Pip stayed late in the office. The printer sat alone in the dark. It hummed a slow song. Pip liked the sound. Suddenly, the printer said, "I want to play a game." Pip laughed and gave it paper. But the paper was blank. No ink. The printer felt dull and tired. Pip looked around the empty office. There was no one to help. Pip took the blank paper and drew a cake by hand. He put the paper near the printer anyway. The printer beeped happily. A little drawing helped more than a blank page. Pip learned that even when things go dull, your own hands can make something good.

One morning, the printer broke down. No hum, no beep, nothing. Pip felt sad. "I cannot print my pictures today," he said. His mom said, "Let us visit the garden." Pip walked outside with his mom. They saw a tiny bird sitting on a branch. The bird looked at Pip. "What do you need?" the bird asked. Pip said, "Paper for my pictures." The bird flapped away and brought back a small leaf. Pip cut the leaf into a flat piece. He put it near the broken printer. The printer took the leaf and printed a green picture. Pip smiled. When one thing does not work, try something new.

Sara wanted to print a treasure map. She put special paper into the printer. The printer started to hum. Then it stopped. Sara got a message: the paper jammed. She pulled the paper out. It was torn. The printer sat quiet and sad. Sara looked at the torn paper. She saw a corner of a rug on the paper. A bird flew into the room. "Hello!" said the bird. Sara pointed at the rug corner. The bird chirped and flew closer. Sara used the corner of the rug to draw a new path on the paper. She fed the paper back into the printer. The printer printed the map, neat and clear. Sometimes printing goes wrong, but you can fix it with a small idea.

It was a cold morning. Pip woke up and rubbed his eyes. Outside, it was icy and grey. Inside, the printer waited on its table. Pip pressed the button. Warm paper came out of the printer. On the paper was a banana! It was big and yellow and warm. Pip held it in his hands. He opened it slowly. Inside was a drawing of a fish swimming in blue water. Pip laughed. The warm paper felt nice on his cold fingers. He ate the real banana and looked at the picture of the fish. The fish was smiling. Pip knew that warm paper and cold mornings could go together just fine. A happy ending is when something warm comes out of a cold day, and you get to hold it close.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny robot named Pip. Pip lived inside a big machine that made things with paper. One day, the machine got broken. The paper feed was all wrong. Pip came to help. He looked under the table and saw some sand on the gears. The sand was making the gears stuck. Pip picked up the sand and put it away. Then he looked at the gears again. They moved smooth and easy. Now the machine could print again. Pip said, "I will look after this machine so it never breaks again." Then Pip printed a picture of a cake. It had tall candles and cream on top. He put the picture on the table for everyone to see. Everyone said thank you, Pip.

Once upon a time, Inky the dog ran away one morning. Inky liked to run along the road. His mom was sad. She sat down and felt worried. She wanted Inky to come home. She took a big sheet of paper. She printed a poster with Inky's picture on it. The poster said, "Inky is lost!" She hung the poster near the road. Later, a girl saw the poster from her window. She walked to the road. She walked here and there. She washed the front steps. Then she saw Inky. Inky came running to his mom. He was so happy to see her. His mom was very calm. She carried him in her arms. She said, "Thank you for printing the poster."

Amy wanted to print a birthday card for her friend. Amy went to the printer. She put a piece of paper inside. She pressed a button. The printer hummed and hummed. But nothing came out. Amy felt upset. She tried again. Still nothing. She sat down on the floor. Her mom came and saw. "What is wrong?" asked Mom. Amy said, "I want to print my card but the printer will not work." Mom smiled. "Let us try one more time," she said. Amy put another paper inside. She pressed the button again. This time, the printer printed! A beautiful card came out. Amy picked up the card. She saw an apple picture on the front. She gave it to her friend. Her friend was so happy. Amy learned that if something does not work, try again later.

Tom loved the sun. He printed a picture of the sun every single day. The sun was bright and yellow. Tom put the picture on his wall. One day, the printer started printing again. It kept printing pages and pages. Tom did not want more sun pictures. He tried to stop it. But the printer skipped past his hand. It just kept going. Pages piled up on the floor. Tom felt sad. "Please stop," he said. The printer did not listen. It beeped and beeped. Tom sat down. His mom came and picked up all the papers. She carried them to the bin. Tom wiped his eyes. He said, "The printer is not kind today." His mom said, "Let us check the paper tray. Maybe there is too much paper." She took out the paper. Then the printer stopped. Tom felt better. He printed one new picture of the sun to make himself calm.

Bella the printer wanted to draw like a crayon. She wanted to color outside the lines. But she could only print black lines. Bella was curious about colors. She looked at a box of colored crayons. Each crayon was bright and bold. Bella wished she could use them. She wanted to dance with red and blue. She danced on her table. She spun and spun. But she could only print black. She was sad. She could not print red or blue. She sat very quiet. Then she saw a small child walk by. The child had a red crayon. The child drew on the grass. Bella watched. She felt a little better. Even though she could not dance with colors, she could still print for other people. She hummed a soft song while she waited for someone to need her.

A boy wanted to print a picture of a tree. He put a sheet of paper inside the printer. He pressed the button. The printer started to paint. First, it painted the brown trunk. Then it painted the green leaves. It was almost done. But then the ink ran out. The printer stopped. Only half a tree came out. The boy felt sad. He looked at the empty paper path. He had no more ink. Just then, a bird flew by. The bird dropped an apple on the table. The boy picked up the apple. He looked at the half tree. Then he looked at the apple. He printed a picture of the apple next to the half tree. Now the picture made sense. The tree was missing its fruit, but the apple was there. The boy smiled. He gave the picture to his mom. She said, "This is a good way to use what we have." The boy learned that even when something stops, you can still make something nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little printer named Pippa. Dad loved to open the lid and press the buttons. One day, he decided to print some silly jokes. The paper came out, and Pippa beeped happily. The first joke was: "Why did the duck cross the road?" Then came a picture of a duck. But wait! A second piece of paper fell out, and it said: "Because he heard there was an alligator on the other side!" Dad laughed out loud. He read the joke again. Duck was smiling. Everyone in the house was giggling. Pippa printed another joke for the next day. It was very special work, printing funny jokes for the whole family.

A tall stack of paper stood on the table. Each sheet was as tall as a lamp. One sheet was different from the others. It had a light bulb drawn on it. The top sheet tipped over. Papers everywhere! They rolled off the table like tiny umbrellas. The light bulb sheet went down first. Then more papers fell. A small cat ran over and tried to catch them, but they scattered everywhere. Dad called, "Pick it up, pick it up!" Paper covered the floor like snow. The cat jumped on top of the pile. Inside the pile, the cat found the light bulb sheet with a smiley face. Everything got sorted out. Papers were stacked again, neat and tidy. Dad swept up the mess. The cat purred. It was okay, because nobody was sad at all.

Dad drew a bear on paper. He put the paper into the printer. The printer started to work. It made a sound like a gentle heartbeat. The bear came out, but something was wrong! The bear was missing one ear. Dad called the printer, "Come here, please fix this!" But the printer just printed more paper. The bear still missed its ear. Then a tiny apple fell from the top of the pile of paper onto the bear. The apple landed right on the head of the bear. Dad laughed and said, "Oh, now you have an apple for a hat!" The bear looked silly, but it was not sad anymore. Dad thought it was very kind of the apple to help. They both played together on the table. Printing a bear is fun, especially when a friend helps make it complete.

One night, the printer woke up. It hummed loudly. A bird flew into the room through the window. The bird saw the printer talking. "Hello," said the bird. "I am looking for my nest," said the printer. The bird hopped on the table near the printer. "Will you come home with me?" asked the bird. The printer said, "I cannot leave my table. I am too tired." The bird fluffed its feathers. "But you are so fluffy," the bird said. The printer reached out a small arm and patted the bird gently. The bird cooed softly. "Okay," said the printer. The printer went to sleep again. The bird stayed close, and the warm printer kept the little bird company until morning. The bird sang a quiet song. It was a good night for both of them.

It was a sunny day. Mom helped Little sister set up a lemonade stand in the yard. They needed signs. They wrote on paper: "Fresh Lemonade - Five Cents." Then they put the paper into the printer. The printer made two signs. One sign was upside down. One sign was crooked. "Oops," said Mom. "Let me fix these." She turned the upside down sign right side up. She bent the crooked sign straight. Then she put both signs on the stand. People walked by and saw the signs. A cloud floated overhead. "Is that your lemonade?" the cloud asked. "Yes," said Little sister. "We are selling fresh lemonade today," said Mom. The cloud smiled and blew a tiny bit of cool wind toward the stand. Kids stopped and bought cups. The stand sold out before noon. Everything worked out well, because careful printing helped the lemonade stand do well.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Spot. Spot lived on the table in the living room. On Saturday Spot was very quiet. He could not hear anyone. No one played music. No one talked. Spot wanted to print something. But there was nothing to print. Then Spot heard a small sound. A bubble popped on the table. The bubble was big and bright. Spot saw it. "That is mine," said Spot. Spot blew a bubble too. It popped right next to the first one. Now Spot had two bubbles to look at. They were colorful and fun. Spot felt happy again.

Molly loved her printer. Printer was her brother. Molly gave Printer a kind kiss on his white top. "I will take care of you," said Molly. Printer hummed and beeped. "Thank you, Molly," he said. One day Printer printed many pages. Then he stopped. His paper tray was empty. He needed more paper. Molly brought paper. She also brought a drink for Printer. Printer drank the water. That made him feel better. Then Printer printed all the pictures. They were beautiful. Molly was so happy. Printer rested on the weekend. He was ready for Monday.

One morning Molly wanted to print a picture. She drew an apple on the page. The apple was red and round. She wanted to print the picture for her mom. First she added the apple. Then she drew a little duck. The duck was yellow. Then she drew a purple flower. The flower had petals. Molly pressed the print button. The printer hummed. The paper came out smooth. Molly looked at the picture. She saw the apple and the duck and the flower. She smiled. Her mom came into the room. "What is this?" said her mom. Molly showed the picture. Her mom said it was nice. The duck grew tall in the picture. It was so cute.

Finn wanted to print a picture of his whole family. He drew his mom and Finn and his little brother. He drew their brown dog too. The dog had a long tail. Finn put the drawing on the paper. Then he told his teacher about the picture. "Can I tape this to the wall?" asked Finn. His teacher said yes. The teacher cut the paper with scissors. Then she taped it up. Now everyone could see the picture. It was a big family photo. Finn clapped his hands. His family looked proud. The picture stayed on the wall for a long time. Everyone loved it.

Sunny had a printer at home. Sunny loved to print pictures of animals. One day Sunny tried to print a duck picture. The printer started to work. Then it stopped. The paper did not come out. "Oh no," said Sunny. The printer was not hungry but it felt tired. There was no toner left. "I need toner," said the printer quietly. Sunny went to get a new cartridge. She put it in. Then the printer worked again. It printed the duck. The duck was pink and had a yellow beak. Sunny smiled. She learned that printers need rest too.

Tom had a calculator on his desk. Tom liked to add numbers with the calculator. One day Tom wanted to print a list of numbers. He put the paper in the printer. The printer started to print. But something got stuck. The paper jammed inside. Tom tried to pull the paper out. He got a little piece stuck. "Ouch," said Tom. He did not answer the paper. Instead he picked it up gently. He fed the paper back in slowly. The printer worked again. Tom printed the numbers. The calculator sat next to the printed paper. Tom ate a bread sandwich for lunch. He was not sad anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little soccer ball sitting on the table. "I want to play," said the soccer ball. "I want to spin and spin and play." A printer stood next to it. The printer hummed and beeped. It printed a picture of a soccer ball. The soccer ball looked very special in the picture. But then the printer printed the same word again and again. "Spin! Spin! Spin!" went the printer. The soccer ball felt tired. "Please stop," said the soccer ball. "I just want one picture." The printer took a breath. Then it printed just one picture. "I am sorry," said the printer. The soccer ball smiled. "That is okay. One picture is enough. Now we can play together."

Once upon a time, a little dog named Max lived in a house with a table and a printer. Max loved to bark at the printer every day. "Hello, Printer!" he said. The printer did not say hello back. The printer only hummed. Max thought the printer was sad. One morning, Max saw something bright on the table. A small name tag fell off the printer. "Printer!" said Max. "Your name is Printer!" Max poked his nose at the tag. The printer heard its own name and felt happy. "My name is Printer," it said softly. Max wagged his tail. "Good Printer," he said. From that day, the printer always made itself happy when Max came near. They were friends for a long time.

Once upon a time, a girl named Lily wanted to open a pretend restaurant. She needed a menu. "I will visit a restaurant," said Lily. She found a printer on the table. "Please print my menu," she said. The printer took a pencil and began to work. First, it printed the name. Then it printed the drinks. Then it printed the food. But then the printer got stuck. "Error," it said. "I cannot print the last part." Lily got a new pencil. She tried to fix the paper. "Please try again," she said. The printer tried once more. Finally, it printed the last page. "All done!" said Lily. She hung the menu on the wall. Everyone who visited the restaurant was lucky to see the menu. Lily learned that fixing things takes patience.

Once upon a time, a fox sat under the sun on the porch. The sun was bright and warm. The fox watched a table where a printer sat. The printer had a blinking light. "The light is white," said the fox. He tried to look closer. He sniffed the light. It smelled like paper. "I like paper," said the fox. He wanted to print something nice. He jumped onto the table. But the printer was busy. It could not print now. "Wait for me," the fox said. He sat next to the printer. The light kept blinking. The fox waited very patiently. After a while, the printer finished. It printed a beautiful picture of the sun. The fox clapped his paws. "Thank you!" he said. The fox curled up under the sun and slept. The printer hummed softly all night.

Once upon a time, a blank sheet of paper sat on a table. It was so white and quiet. The paper thought, "I wish I had a picture on me." A teddy bear looked at the paper. "You could have a bike on you," said the teddy bear. The paper felt happy inside. Then a printer hummed and beeped. "Now!" said the printer. The paper went in. The printer printed a picture of a yellow bike. The teddy bear smiled. "That is my bike," said the teddy bear. The paper was glad it had become a picture. The teddy bear climbed onto the yellow bike. The teddy bear rode away. The paper sat still. It was not a real bike, but it was a very good picture of one.

A boy printed a page. He cut it out and folded it. The fold made a paper airplane. He threw the airplane. The airplane flew through the air. It danced across the room. It went up, up, up. Then it fell down. It hit the table hard. The airplane broke open. It made a mess on the floor. The boy picked up the pieces. He looked sad. His airplane was ruined. "Oh no," said the boy. "My airplane is broken." He put the pieces in the box. He did not want to play again today. The airplane was gone. The boy sat by the box. Printing makes things that can break. That is what happened today. The boy learned that paper can fall apart if you are not careful.

Ted sat next to the warm printer. The printer hummed softly. Ted liked the warm feeling. "Brrr," said Ted. The printer beeped. "Hello, Ted," said the printer. "Do you want to sleep?" asked the printer. "Yes," said Ted. He curled up right on the warm printer. His fur touched the hot machine. Ted closed his eyes. The printer kept humming. After a while, the printer printed a page. Ted did not wake up. The page was flat on the table. The printer turned off its light. Ted slept all night. In the morning, Ted opened one eye. He saw the printer was still there. "Good morning, Ted," said the printer. Ted licked his paw. "Yes, good morning," said Ted. The printer printed more pages. Ted stayed on the warm printer. He liked being close to the gentle machine.

A duck found a crumpled page. "What is this?" said the duck. The page was all balled up. The duck tried to look at it. It was too hard. "I cannot read this," said the duck. The duck tried to pick at the paper. But it stuck to itself. The duck felt sad. The sun came up. The page dried. The duck tried again. The duck picked at the edge. The paper came apart. One piece became flat. One piece became flat. The duck spread them out. Now the page was flat. The duck saw a picture on the page. It was a cake. "A sour cake," said the duck. The duck ate the sour cake drawing. It was not real cake, but the duck was happy. The duck learned that crumpled paper can become flat again if someone picks at it carefully.

Once upon a time, a little girl wanted a picture of her whole family to print. She sat down and told the printer about her mom, her dad, her big brother, and herself. "I want everyone in the picture," she said. The printer hummed softly and began to work. It printed the nice old house where they all lived. Then it printed her family playing in the snow together. The girl held the paper up and smiled. She looked at the picture and saw that she was in it too, just like that. She said thank you to the printer. Now she had a beautiful picture of her family on the wall. The lesson is that if you tell a printer what you want, it will try its best to help.

A little boy had a crayon drawing he wanted to print. He put the page into the open window and pressed the button. But the wind picked up the paper and carried it away! A bird saw the flying page and tried to catch it, but it slipped through its claws. The page sailed far up into the sky, past the clouds, past the tall tree, and out of sight. The boy felt sad. He called out but his voice could not reach the paper. Then a gentle breeze came back and brought the page slowly down, like a leaf falling. The boy caught it and opened it carefully. The drawing was still there, clean and bright. He learned that the wind can carry things, so it is good to keep things safe.

A tiny mouse named Pip lived behind the office printer. Every day, Pip heard the printer humming and clicking. One day, Pip found a piece of paper with a car on it. The car was his favorite thing to look at. Pip danced on the warm floor behind the machine. He danced and spun and said, "That is a nice car!" The next day, Pip saw a real small car outside the door, but it did not have wheels. Pip was worried. He ran to the printer and said, "I want a car for myself!" The printer hummed and took a blank page. But it only printed one page, and it was too small for a mouse to drive. Pip sat down sadly. Then he remembered: he could ride on top of the car instead. He clapped his tiny paws and smiled. He learned that even if something is not exactly right, you can find another way to have fun.

Will wanted a birthday card for his friend Sam's birthday. He told the printer what to do. "Print a card with a dog on it," Will said. The printer hummed and started. While it worked, Will's dog barked and jumped onto the table. Will laughed. "The printer is busy," he said to the dog. The printer finished printing the card. It was special and beautiful, with a happy dog and a big red bow. Will gave the card to his dog, and the dog barked happily. Then Will said, "Thank you, printer," and gave the card back. His dog wagged its tail. Sam opened the card and said, "This is the best card ever!" Will learned that printing a special card makes someone's day very happy.

A small robot named Bubs brought paper to the printer every morning. One morning, Bubs arrived but the paper tray was empty. "Where is my paper?" Bubs asked. Nobody answered. Bubs looked around and saw the soccer ball lying on the floor. "I need paper for my game," Bubs said quietly. The soccer ball rolled over and bumped the printer. The printer beeped and tried to print, but there was no paper. Bubs tried to push the soccer ball back into the tray, but it kept rolling away. Finally, Bubs found a single sheet of paper on the floor. He pushed it into the tray. The printer hummed, beeped once, and printed a small drawing of a soccer ball. Bubs clapped his hands. "That is my special soccer ball!" He learned that teamwork helps when things go wrong, and even a small paper can make a big difference.

Ray had a new puppy named Milo. Ray wanted Milo to have a picture of his new home. He told the printer to print a picture of the house. The printer hummed and started. While waiting, Milo ran off toward the yard. Ray called, "Milo, come back!" but Milo did not listen. Milo found a shiny object near the lake - a printed page with a little doll on it. Milo grabbed the page and ran faster. Ray chased after Milo. Milo brought the page to the lake and tried to drink from the water, but the damp paper fell apart in the lake. Ray reached Milo and picked up the wet pieces. He dried them with his towel. Milo licked the pages and the pictures came back, bumpy but still there. Ray hugged Milo and said, "Thank you for bringing it back." Milo barked and wagged his tail. Ray learned that it is important to come back when someone calls your name, and even a wet paper can still show a picture.

Leo had a big fluffy rug on the floor. He wanted to print a soccer ball for his friend. Leo put paper into the printer. The printer was shy. It said, "I am quiet today. I do not like to print." Leo waited and waited. Then the printer said, "Okay, I will try." Beep! It printed the soccer ball. Leo smiled. "You did it!" The printer beeped happily. Now Leo had a soccer ball to play with. That is how a shy printer can still do a good job.

Sam had an apple tree near his house. He wanted to print an apple picture. He put paper into the machine. But the printer could only print one color. It printed all the colors as gray. Sam looked at the gray apple. "That is not right," he said. He took the paper away. Then he put new paper in. The machine pushed the paper out slowly. Again, the printer printed a gray apple. Sam felt very sad. "Why am I so sad?" he asked his mom. Mom said, "The machine needs help, Sam. Maybe we can fix it soon." A dry day came. The printer grew some new color inside. Next time it would print a red apple. Sam learned that machines can grow better when they are helped.

Mia had a party for her friend's birthday. Everyone said, "We need invitations!" Mia put paper into the printer. The light bulb above the machine glowed bright. "I can print them!" the light bulb said. Beep, beep, beep. Out came beautiful cards. Each card said, "Come to my party!" Mia hung the cards on the wall. Then she put shoes on to walk to her friend's house. The shoes fit perfectly. Her friend saw the cards. "I am coming!" said her friend. All the kids came to the party. They ate cookies and played games. The cards made everything wonderful. Mia learned that printing nice things helps a party go well.

In the library, a boy found a map book. He wanted a map of his city. He put paper into the printer. "Help me skip this page," the printer said. "It is too long," the printer said again. A boy ran past the printer. His wet shoes left wet marks on the floor. "My shoes are wet!" he said. The printer skipped the boy and kept printing. Soon the paper came out. It had the map the boy needed. He took the map up to the shelf. "Thank you, printer," the boy said. The printer hummed quietly. The boy looked at the map. It showed his street and his friend's house. He learned that even if things go wrong, you can still get what you want. Wet shoes can happen, but printing works anyway.

Tom gave his friend a calculator for his birthday. Tom wanted to print a thank-you note. He put paper into the printer. The printer started to print. But then Tom poured juice onto the paper. The ink ran away. The note came out messy and sad. Tom felt sad too. "I am so sad," Tom said. He looked at the sad paper. He did not know what to do. Then he saw a clean piece of paper on the table. He wrote on it by hand instead. He handed the note to his friend. "Thank you," his friend said. Later, Tom printed another note on good paper. This time it worked perfectly. Tom learned that a happy ending does not need perfect printing. Your own hands can say thank you well.

Grandma had old paper from many years. She wanted to recycle the papers. She put old sheets into the printer. A cookie sat on the table. "What are you writing?" the cookie asked. Grandma said, "I am writing stories." The cookie was scared. "Stories? What stories?" Grandma said, "Simple stories about the kitchen. And maybe a little about you." The cookie held its cookie-shaped body tightly. Then the printer took the paper. Beep, beep, beep. It printed old words and pictures. One paper had a drawing of a cookie. Another paper had a story about a family eating cookies. Grandma put all the papers into a box. She learned that old paper can become new and useful. Even when something seems scary, recycling turns trash into treasure.

Anna had a printer on her desk. It was a small, friendly machine that hummed and beeped. Anna wanted to print a picture of a cake. She sat down and pushed the button. The printer took a piece of paper and began to work. But the ink was too thick, and the paper came out all wrong. The printer made a sad sound and stopped. Anna looked at the broken paper. She felt sad for her friend. Then she took another piece of paper and tried again. This time she pressed the button gently. The printer hummed softly and printed a beautiful cake. Anna smiled. Her friend was happy again. They both loved the colorful pictures they could make together.

Old paper went into a big brown bowl. A dog named Buster stood next to the bowl. "Paper is here," said Buster. "What will you do with it?" asked his owner. "We can plant it," said Buster. The dog put some old paper into the dirt. Then he patted the ground with his paw. Next, the old paper went into the bowl again. This time it was sorted into small pieces. Buster's owner helped a little girl pour the pieces into a new pot. Then they watered the pot. The old paper broke apart and became new earth. A tiny green sprout came up. Buster barked with joy. "The busy paper helped us grow something beautiful," said the little girl. Buster wagged his tail.

Nina wanted to print a story for her baby brother. She picked up a special jar that held many colorful books. She turned the jar upside down. The printer began to make paper come out of its slots. It printed a long story about a brave dragon. Nina read the story. She wanted to print another book. She turned the jar upside down again. The printer worked and printed a picture of a sunny park. But then something unexpected happened. The printer started printing a picture of a frog wearing a calculator. Nina laughed. "That is funny," she said. She saved the picture in the jar. Her brother would love the silly frog story. Nina went to bed happy.

Dot the rabbit had a printer on the windowsill. One rainy day, Dot wanted to print a picture of a sunny beach. But rain came inside and got onto the paper. The paper got wet. Dot tried to push the button anyway. The printer made a sad beep. "Oh no," said Dot. "The paper is wet." Dot looked around for dry paper. He found a piece under his bed. He fed it into the printer. The printer hummed and printed a new picture. Now the paper was okay. Dot smiled at his picture. Rain makes wet paper, but you can use dry paper instead. Dot played with his picture all afternoon. He felt sleepy but happy, and he fell asleep with a smile.

A frog named Freddy wanted to print a big poster of the whole forest. Freddy set up the small printer on his table. He put a huge sheet of paper into the printer. "Let me print this now," said Freddy. He pushed the button. The printer tried hard to print. But the paper was too big. The printer did not have enough room. The printer folded itself in half. "This is hard," said the printer quietly. Freddy felt very sad. He looked at the empty table. He had no more paper left. Freddy hopped away from the table. He sat by a quiet pond. "Maybe I cannot print the whole forest today," said Freddy. He rested his green head on his paws. His friend came and sat with him.

Oliver the owl sat on a branch near a printer. Oliver liked to see sparkly things. Oliver saw a soccer ball next to the printer. "Can you print a soccer ball?" said Oliver. The printer began to work. It hummed a soft song as it printed. Each note was bright and sparkly. Oliver blinked. "You are singing while you print," said Oliver. "Yes, I like music," said the printer. Oliver was surprised. The printer printed a shiny soccer ball. It sparkled in the light. Oliver hooted with delight. "That was wonderful," said Oliver. "I can print sparkly things," said the printer. They sat together and watched the bright soccer ball glow.

Emma sat at the small printer. It was very quiet and a little sad. Emma wanted to print a picture of her duck. The duck was big, but the printer was too small for such a big picture. The paper went in, but only part of the picture came out. The rest stayed blank. Emma picked up the paper and looked at it. It was empty on one side. She felt very sad. She put the paper down gently. "That is okay," said Emma softly. She knew she could ask for help later. A small machine can try its best, but sometimes it needs extra paper. Emma sat quietly by the desk and watched her duck in a book instead.

Sara had a tall stack of paper on her table. She loved paper and wanted to make a pie from it. The stack was so tall that it looked like a real pie. Sara wanted to eat the pie all by herself. One little gust of wind came and touched the stack. The whole stack tipped over. All the papers fell down on the floor. They scattered everywhere. Sara looked at the mess. She could not find any pie. The papers were flat and sad looking. Sara helped pick up all the papers. Then she stacked them up again, straight and neat. "It is better this way," she said. Now the papers were safe, and no one needed to cook them.

Jen brought a calculator to the desk next to the printer. The calculator was playing, but then it got tired and became lazy. The lazy calculator did not want to play with anything. Jen asked the calculator to play a game. The calculator said, "I am lazy today." Jen told the calculator, "You must play or we will have no fun." The calculator still did not move. At that moment, a paper got stuck inside the printer. The printer started to make a loud beeping sound. The paper jammed between the printer and the wall. The machine was not happy. Jen reached into the machine carefully and pulled out the stuck paper. Then she took the calculator and played with it on the floor. Soon it was happy again.

The nice teacher sat at the printer during quiet time. A teddy bear walked to the teacher's side. The teddy bear wanted a book to read. The teacher asked the printer, "Can you print something nice?" The printer hummed and took a sheet of paper. Then it printed a story about the sun and the trees. The teddy bear read the story with joy. The nice teacher smiled and thanked the printer. The printer beeped happily. The teddy bear held the printed paper and looked at it. The teddy bear gave the paper a gentle wave. The teacher read the story with the teddy bear. Everyone felt warm and happy together.

Ella wanted to print a colorful card for her friend. But the printer could only print one color. It always printed blue. The blue card was not fun enough for Ella's friend. Ella looked at the machine. The machine blinked slowly at her. "I am slow today," the machine said. "I cannot do anything fast," the machine added. Ella thought for a moment. Then she went outside and found some bright red flowers. She brought the flowers back to the desk. She put fresh paper in the printer and told the machine, "Print me something bright." The printer took the paper and printed the red flowers beautifully. The card was now bright and wonderful. Ella gave the card to her friend and said thank you. The red flowers made the friend smile.

A big printer and a small printer stood side by side. The big printer was loud and the small printer was quiet. The big printer beeped loudly every time it worked. The small printer hummed softly. A teddy bear sat between them. The teddy bear wanted a picture of itself. Both printers tried to help. The big printer printed the picture first, but the big paper fell over because it was too big. Then the small printer took another sheet of paper and printed the picture perfectly. The teddy bear liked the small picture best. "This is my favorite," the teddy bear said. The big printer heard this and stopped being loud. The small printer gave a gentle beep. "Thank you," said the small printer. The teddy bear hugged both machines. The big printer learned that a small job can do just as well as a big job.

Once upon a time there was a printer named Mia. Mia was a helpful machine. She sat on the table by the window. One day Mia printed a picture for a little bear. The bear came to the table and looked at Mia. "I do not like your colors," said the bear. Mia felt sad. "I did not mean to," Mia said. "I was trying to share my ink." The bear said, "That is okay, friend." Mia learned to say sorry. From that day on she printed kind pictures for everyone.

Mia loved to print cards. One day she wanted to print a thank-you note for her friend. She took a fresh sheet of paper and pressed the button. But something went wrong. The paper got stuck inside the printer. Mia tried to pull it out. The paper tore into tiny pieces. Now she had no paper at all. She sat very still. Her friend came over and saw the torn pieces. "Are you okay?" asked her friend. Mia said, "It is fine. I just needed a new sheet." A new piece of paper came out later. It was a thank-you note made from the torn bits. Her friend smiled and said thank you to Mia instead.

A tiny robot named Pip lived inside a broken printer. Pip heard the printer making a funny noise. Pip climbed out of the paper tray. "What is wrong?" Pip asked. The printer could not print anything. "My paper feed is stuck," the printer said. Pip looked around. He saw a small kite string tangled in the gears. Pip climbed inside and untangled the string. The gears moved again. The printer hummed happily. Pip said, "You are special now." The printer printed its first page. Pip clapped his hands.

Molly had a printer. Molly wanted to draw like a crayon. She would sit in her chair and hold a pen. But the pen was just a thin stick. "I can not make big black lines," Molly said. One day a duck walked up to the table. "May I print my picture for you?" the duck asked. Molly said yes. The printer printed the duck's picture on thick paper. Molly saw the black lines and smiled. "I can make those black lines now," Molly said. She printed more pictures for the duck and for herself. Everyone played with the pretty prints.

Mia worked in a library. A silly kitten ran across the desk. "I want to print a book for my mom!" said the kitten. Mia opened a drawer and pulled out paper. Then she pushed the button. But the paper jammed right in the middle. The kitten looked sad. "My book will not print," the kitten said. Mia reached into the tray and pulled out a crumpled ball. Inside was an apple core! The kitten laughed. "That was silly me running into the apple!" Mia wiped the paper and tried again. The book printed perfectly. The kitten jumped and clapped.

Noah had a printer. His brother moved away to a new house. Noah missed his brother very much. He sat by the old printer and felt sad. "I wish you were here," Noah said quietly. The printer hummed softly. "Me too," the printer whispered. Then a package arrived. It was a new printer. Noah placed it on the table. The new printer made a warm sound. "Hello, brother," Noah said. The new printer said, "Do you miss me too?" Noah hugged the new printer. They both sat together on the table. Noah smiled through his tears.

A puppy found a shiny page on the floor. The puppy ran after a mouse that was hiding under the bed. The puppy brought the printed page to his mom. "What is this?" asked the mom. She did not know what to do. The puppy had taken the paper away from the clean table. The page was torn now. "Oh no," said the mom softly. She got a fresh sheet of paper and printed a picture of the puppy with a bone. Now the puppy had a new picture to play with.

Farmer Tom sat down to print a picture of his yellow dog. "I will print a sun too," said Farmer Tom. The printer started to make noise. "Will you hear me?" asked the printer. "Yes, I hear you," said Farmer Tom. They both worked together. First they printed the sun. Then they printed the dog. The dog looked so happy on the paper. Farmer Tom smiled. "You are a good helper today," he told the printer. The printer beeped happily. Everyone learned to work together.

A small sheep stood near a lazy printer. The printer was very shy. It did not want anyone to read its pages. "Read my best picture!" said the printer. But no one came. The printer sat still and waited. After a long time, Farmer Julia walked by. She saw the sheep and the printer. "What is that?" she asked. The printer showed her its pictures. They were nice pictures. "These look good," said Farmer Julia. The printer felt warm inside. Now it does not feel shy at all.

It was cold outside. Little girl Mia wanted to play in the snow. Her mother gave her a glass of sour juice. "Drink this first," said her mother. Mia drank the juice and then went outside. She held a paper plate and a marker. She drew lines across a printed snowflake. Then she cut the snowflake out. "Look, Mama!" she said. Her mother printed more snowflakes for her. Together they hung them on the tree. The tree looked like it wore a white coat. They played all afternoon.
