On Saturday, a lonely monkey sat by a loud printer. The monkey did not have any friends. The printer made a lot of noise but the monkey could not sleep. "Why do you beep so much?" asked the monkey. "I am just talking to myself," said the printer. The monkey ran away from the printer. He chased a fish around the house. The fish jumped out of a bowl and swam up the stairs. The monkey laughed and played with the fish. Now the monkey has a friend who talks to him even when he runs away.

Once upon a time, there was a small sun that sat on the table all by itself. The sun was bright and warm. One morning, it wished for something nice. It wished for a good friend. The sun looked around and saw an empty paper tray. The tray was dark and empty. "I wish I had some paper," said the sun. The paper tray could not wish. The sun felt sad. Then a little hand put an egg into the tray. An egg? Yes! A tiny egg rolled out of the tray and went for a walk. The sun was so happy. The egg hatched into a little bunny. The bunny was soft and white. The sun gave the bunny a big hug. They were the best friends ever. The end.

One day, a raincloud came over. The rain was heavy and wet. It rained all day long. A little printer sat inside a house. The printer was a very good friend to the family. But when it got wet, the paper stuck together. The printer tried to print a picture but the paper would not move. "Oh no," cried the printer. "My paper is too wet." Its friend came outside. Its friend patted its head. "Don't cry," said its friend. "Let me help you." Its friend dried the paper. Then the printer printed a beautiful picture of a rainbow. Everyone was happy. The end.

A little boy had an old desk in his house. On the desk was an old printer. The old printer could not print fast anymore. "It is too slow," said the boy. He wanted to make a card for his mom. But the old printer was very slow. So the boy took the old paper and put it in a bin. He took the old paper out again. He took it to a big place where people recycled things. There, someone locked the old paper in a box. "Wait," said the worker. "This paper can be used again." The worker took the old paper and made new paper from it. Then the boy got new paper. Now he printed his card. His mom was proud. The end.

One evening, the office went dark. The light went off. The printer woke up. But it was sleepy. "Where is my work?" said the sleepy printer. "There is no light," it said. A fence of dark walls kept the printer alone. It could not see anything. It was scared. Its friends tried to cheer it up. "Don't be scared," they said. "We are here." The printer stayed quiet. The next morning, the lights came on. The printer was happy to wake up with its friends. The end.

A little girl named Lily had an old printer at home. This printer was very slow. It took forever to print one picture. Lily needed to print many pictures for her show. But the printer was always too slow. One day, Lily tried to print a big picture. The paper jammed inside. The printer stopped. "Help," it said quietly. Lily came closer. She put her hands on the printer. She hugged it tight. "I am sorry," she said. The printer felt better. Lily waited patiently. At last, the printer printed the picture. Lily smiled. The printer was friendly now, and happy too. The end.

A family had a special picture of their baby on the table. They wanted to print it out so everyone could see it. The printer hummed and took the paper. It started to print the pictures. Then the machine made a sad sound. It stopped. The printer had run out of ink. The picture did not finish. The family felt very sad. The baby would not see the full picture. They could not tear the paper because it was part of the story. They put the picture face down on the table. Everyone cried a little. It was a sweet moment and nothing scary happened.

A little boy named Sam had a sticker book. He wanted to print one page so he could use stickers. He held the paper near an open window. A car drove by outside. The wind blew. The paper flew away! Sam reached out his hand but the paper was too far. Then the paper flew right into a bush. Sam ran outside and found the page still in the bush. He pulled it back and carried it inside. The paper was dirty from the dirt but he washed it. Now Sam could stick all his favorite stickers on the page. His page was finished and he was happy.

Joe had a fun game to play with his rabbit. Joe put a picture of the game on the printer. The rabbit jumped on the table. The printer did not stop. It kept printing pages. One page was for the game. Another page was for Joe's hands. Joe tried to take the pages but the printer would not stop. The pages were dry and stuck together. Joe felt very frustrated. Finally, Joe pushed a big chair on top of the printer. That stopped the printing. Joe sat down and rubbed his eyes. Then he woke up the rabbit and they played the game together on the floor. Lesson: sometimes you have to wait and then try again.

A boy had a tree in his yard that gave him beautiful leaves. His brother helped him pick a leaf to print. The leaf was very sweet looking. The brother put the leaf on the table. He pressed the button on the printer. The printer took the paper and began to print. But the printer had no toner. The words did not show up. The paper stayed blank. The brother felt sad. He could not fit the nice leaf onto the paper. They put the blank paper on the table. The brother hugged his brother and they sat quietly under the real tree. The leaf was safe in his hand. They learned that machines need care and so do friends.

Once upon a time, little Emma wanted to make signs for her lemonade stand. She found a big sheet of paper on the table. A bird was sitting on the bird feeder outside the window. "I will print my signs now," said Emma. She fed the paper into the printer. The printer hummed and hummed. But the machine made a loud beep. The paper came out all torn. Emma felt scared. Then she saw the bird pull out one small piece of paper. "Look!" said the bird. It flapped its wings and landed on the sign. Now the sign had a picture of a bird on it! Emma laughed. The lemonade stand could sell lemonade with a funny bird on the sign. Everyone smiled.

One busy morning, Mr. Tom worked at his desk. He had so many papers to print. He put a sheet into the office printer. The printer started to hum. Then a kitten walked across the desk. "Oh no," said Mr. Tom. "I have to print the whole report, and a kitten is on top of it." The kitten looked up. "I am just going for a walk," said the kitten. "Do not move," said Mr. Tom. The printer kept working. Papers went in and came out. Soon the printer hummed very quietly. The kitten jumped down. Mr. Tom printed all his papers on time. Everyone laughed at the silly kitten story later.

Little drop of ink lived in a dark drawer. "I want to see the world," said the ink. "I will print things and go on paper." A tiny ant came along. "Will you print me a map?" asked the ant. "Yes," said the ink. "First I need to get some fresh paper." The ink rolled onto a clean sheet. Then it got very quiet while waiting. The ink heard a soft beep from far away. The printer pulled a new sheet near. "Now I can print my map," said the ink. It printed the map and went for a walk on the paper road. The ink saw trees, hills, and a river. "This is the best world ever," said the ink.

Noah lost his cat. He put a big poster on the wall. He needed to print it. Noah put the paper into the printer. "I will print a poster to find my cat," said Noah. The printer hummed. But the ink ran low. The printer made a sad sound. "I cannot print yet," said the printer. Noah took the paper out and tried again. The paper was very sticky. It stuck to the sides of the tray. Noah had to pull it gently. Finally the poster came out. It showed a picture of a fluffy cat near a tree. Noah put the poster on the fence. A neighbor saw the poster and called Noah's name. The cat was safe inside the house. Noah felt happy again.

The old printer sat by the window. It was tired. Its head made a whirring sound. "I need a rest," said the printer. Outside, a garden was blooming. A flower opened its petals. "I will help you rest," said the flower. The flower gave the printer a soft drink of water. The printer drank and felt light. Its whirring stopped. It did not need to print today. It just sat and watched the garden. Bees flew around the flowers. The sun was warm. The printer closed its eyes. Rest was the best thing.

Noah found a crumpled page on the floor. It was a page from a book. "Oh no, this page is folded up," said Noah. He held the page and shook it. The creases went away. The page became flat and smooth again. Noah put the page back in the book. He turned to a new page. The book was whole. A fish was swimming outside the window. "I saw a fish today," said Noah. He wanted to draw a fish. He put the paper in the printer. The printer hummed and made a picture of a fish. Noah added the fish page to his new book. Everything worked out fine.

Once upon a time, Jen had a mouse named Pip who lived behind the office printer. One day, Pip wanted to stack some cheese on top of the machine. But the paper tray was sticky. Cheese stuck to the paper. Pip could not pull the cheese down. "Help me!" said Pip. "I cannot get it off," said Pip. Jen heard the mouse squeak. She came closer. She pulled the cheese away gently. "Good now?" asked Jen. "Good now," said Pip. They ate the cheese together. It was nice.

Once upon a time, a cat named Luna liked to sleep on the warm printer. She curled up right on top of it. The printer made a soft hum. Luna purred. Then the bird came flying in. The bird landed on the desk. The bird saw the cat. The bird flapped her wings. "Hello, cat," said the bird. Luna did not wake up. The bird stepped closer. The bird tapped the cat's ear. Luna woke up suddenly! "Ouch!" said Luna. She jumped off the printer. The bird sang a song. Luna walked away slowly. The bird flew out the window. It was a funny thing to happen.

Once upon a time, Zoe had a duck named Daffy. Daffy wanted to press the print button. But Zoe had not said yes yet. "May I print?" asked Daffy. "Not yet," said Zoe. Daffy did not blink because he was sad. The printer hummed on the desk. Paper came out. Daffy saw the paper. "It is so silly," said Daffy. "Why do you say that?" asked Zoe. "Because I pressed the button wrong," said Daffy. "Let me try again," said Daffy. He pressed the button right. A picture of a duck came out! "You did it!" said Zoe. Daffy waddled happily. They were both glad.

Once upon a time, Nick had an owl who lived near the printer. The owl wanted to write a letter to his friend. Nick put paper into the machine. Nick pressed the button. The printer beeped very loudly. "Too loud!" said the owl. The owl covered his ears. Nick turned down the volume. The printer beeped softer. The owl took off his glasses. "I still cannot hear," said the owl. Nick helped the owl find the quiet setting. The printer beeped softly. The owl wrote his letter. Nick sent the letter by post. The owl read the letter. "This is good," said the owl. Nick was happy.

Once upon a time there was a big bird on the table. The bird liked to sit near the machine that prints pictures. One day the bird got very sad. The bird wanted to see a picture of a bird. But the machine printed a jar instead of a bird. The bird did not like a jar. "I want my picture back," said the bird. Then the bird flew away to find a real bird. The machine tried again and printed a big purple flower. The bird came back and saw the flower. The bird was happy now. The bird sat on the flower and smiled.

There was a little frog in the room. The frog saw a word on a paper. It said "frog" but it looked wrong. The frog could not read it right. Then the frog said, "I will print it again." So the frog put paper into the machine. The machine made a drum inside. But the drum got stuck. The machine kept printing the same word again and again. "Stop! I am tired!" said the frog. The machine did not stop. The frog jumped away from the table. Soon the drum broke and stopped. Now the frog had two papers with the same word. "It is silly," said the frog. "But it is my word," said the frog. The frog put the paper on the shelf and went to sleep.

A robot friend brought paper to the printer. The robot carried the paper in its hands. The robot walked to the table and set the paper down. "Good morning," said the robot. "I will print your drawing today," said the machine. "I need help," said the robot. The robot's hands were wet from washing. The paper slipped out of wet hands. The robot dropped the paper. Then the robot used soap to wash its hands. The robot dried its hands with a soft cloth. The robot gave the clean paper to the machine. The machine printed the drawing. The robot clapped its hands. "That is good," said the robot. The robot helped the machine one more time. The drawing came out perfect.

A little girl wanted to print a treasure map. Her dad drew the map on paper and put it in the machine. The machine started to print. But something went wrong. The machine printed a tower instead of a map. A gray tower stood where the map should be. "No!" said the girl. "I need my map." The machine tried again but still printed the tower. The girl sat down and cried. Then she looked at the gray tower. She saw that the tower was very tall and gray. She pulled a pencil and drew lines on the tower. She drew trees and paths on the tower. The tower became a map. The girl smiled. "The map is on the tower now," said her dad. They both laughed.

One day a new printer came to the house. The family was happy. A soccer ball was sitting by the new machine. "What are you?" said the soccer ball. "I am a printer," said the machine. "I print things for you," said the machine. "I want to print you," said the soccer ball. "Oh no," said the machine. "You cannot be printed." The soccer ball rolled away. The machine tried to print a picture of the soccer ball. But the ink was dry and would not print. The machine hummed and beeped but nothing came out. The family felt sad. "We will wait," said the mother. She gave the machine a cup of water. The machine drank the water slowly. The ink got wet again. The machine printed a picture of a soccer ball. The soccer ball came out bright and round. Everyone cheered. The soccer ball was happy too.

One night a duck waddled to the table. The duck wanted a picture. The duck saw the machine on the table. "Can you print me?" said the duck. The machine turned on. The machine hummed softly. "I cannot print at night," said the machine. "It is too dark." The duck did not care. The duck stomped its feet on the floor. "Please," said the duck. The machine took a blank sheet of paper. The machine printed a little duck. The duck was cool and blue. The duck was happy. But then the duck saw other blank paper in a basket. The machine kept printing ducks all night. At dawn the family woke up. They saw many ducks on the floor. "What is that noise?" said the father. He covered the machine with a blanket. The ducks stayed on the floor. In the morning they went outside and played in the sun.

Once upon a time, two printers sat on the same bench. One was big and gray. The other was small and yellow. They did not like each other. "You are loud," said the big one. "You are slow," said the small one. Then they tried to print the same page at the same time. The paper jammed. The small printer cried. A tear fell on the page. The big printer felt sad too. "I did not mean to be loud," said the big one. "I am glad we are friends now," said the small one. They sat together on the bench. They printed a picture of two friends. It was a happy picture.

Dan had a printer at home. Dan wanted to build something special. He gave the printer a spoon. "Print for me," said Dan. The printer took the spoon and printed a new spoon. Dan held it up. It was so sweet and shiny. "This spoon is wonderful," said Dan. Dan's friend came over. "Can I try it?" asked his friend. "Yes," said Dan. His friend tried the spoon. The friend said it was good. Dan was glad. They ate soup together with the new spoon. Dan knew he could use the printer to make things he needed.

Inky was a little printer. Everyone in the office went home. Inky sat alone in the dark room. The rain came down outside. Inky's light blinked. "Why do I blink?" whispered Inky. "I want to print my picture," said Inky. "But no one is here," said Inky. Suddenly, a duck walked into the room. "Quack! I need a picture!" said the duck. "I will print for you," said Inky. Inky hummed and beeped. The printer took paper and made a picture. The duck looked at the picture. "Thank you," said the duck. The duck went home. Inky felt brave and happy.

The printer broke one day. "I cannot print anymore," said the printer. Its paper tray was empty. It was very sad. A calculator sat next to it. The calculator had buttons and numbers. "What can I do?" asked the calculator. "I can help," said the calculator. The calculator showed how to put paper back in the tray. It showed how to press the right buttons. Slowly, the printer worked again. Now the printer was full of paper. The calculator was proud. It called the printer helper. From then on, the calculator always stayed by the broken printer to help when it needed help.

Once upon a time there was a blank sheet of paper. It was lying on a table, and it wanted to be something very much. It wanted to make a picture of a fish. The paper was busy. It tried to spin around on the table. But it did not know how to spin all by itself. It looked up at the big window. A little bird flew by and dropped a leaf on the paper. The paper felt sad for a moment. Then the little bird came back with a blue dot made from ink. The paper saw the dot and remembered. Now the paper could begin to draw a fish tail. The paper drew and drew and drew. A beautiful fish appeared on the page. The paper felt happy again. The other blank papers on the table saw what the paper had done. They were so busy that day too.

Once upon a time there was a farmer named Tim. Tim had a big green tree in his yard. Tim liked to print pictures from the machine. One day he printed a picture of the green tree. He hung the picture on the wall. Tim wanted to watch the tree in the picture fly like an airplane. So he folded one edge of the printed page and made a paper airplane. Tim threw the airplane. It went far, far away. It flew out the door and over the fence. It kept going. Tim was watching when a boy on the next farm caught it. The boy smiled at Tim. Tim laughed and clapped his hands. He was glad someone liked his airplane. The green tree in the picture was happy too, because it was flying through the air.

Ann sat down and put her hand on the warm paper. The last sheet of paper was still in the tray. Ann wanted to print a picture of an apple. She pulled the tray out. There was just one sheet left. She fed it into the machine. The machine hummed and took the paper. But then the machine made a sound. It shook and shook. The warm paper jiggled and slid back. The machine said "Beep beep." Ann reached in and found the paper again. She pulled it out gently. Now the machine could print the apple picture. Ann put the paper in and pushed the button. The machine printed. A red apple appeared on the screen. Ann clapped her hands. "That worked!" she said. The warm paper was good and warm inside the tray. It would work again tomorrow if nobody shook it hard.

The printer sat by the window all day long. It wanted to see outside. The wind blew and blew. The printer felt mad. It wanted to look at the trees and the clouds. A soccer ball rolled by on the sidewalk. The soccer ball bumped the printer. The printer beeped angry. "Stop," it seemed to say. The soccer ball rolled away. The printer turned its face toward the window. Outside, the wind moved branches of the tree back and forth. The printer thought that was pretty. It closed its eyes. The wind made small flags on the grass. The printer opened its eyes and looked at them. Now the printer was not mad anymore. It just watched the wind make patterns on the ground.

One morning Anna wanted to print a picture for grandma. She put a sheet of paper in the tray. She pushed the button. The machine started to spin. The ink rolled across the page. Anna watched as a monkey appeared on the screen. The monkey looked big and funny and brown. Anna printed the picture carefully. Then she put the picture on the table. She wanted to show grandma before she went to bed. But wait. Anna heard a strange sound coming from the hallway. A little squirrel ran past carrying a tiny picture. Anna looked at the monkey on the squirrel's back. It was the same monkey! Anna smiled. She put the big picture on the table and held the little picture close. Grandma would have two pictures tonight. That was nice.

Ann wanted to print a card for her friend. She put a sheet of paper into the tray. She pushed the button. The machine began to spin. It printed a smiling sun on the page. The paper was smooth under Ann's fingers. Ann pulled the card out. She picked up a yellow crayon. She colored the sun yellow. Then she picked up a blue crayon. She colored the sky blue. Then she picked up a green crayon. She colored a hill green. The card looked nice. Ann held it up and showed it to her friend. Her friend smiled. Then Ann heard a loud bang. A bird hit the window. The glass cracked. The card slipped from her hands and fell to the floor. Ann picked it up. It was okay. But it was not okay about the window. The bird flew away. The card was safe but the window was broken now. Ann hugged the card and cried softly.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. Mia had a brave little printer on her table. When her mom asked the printer to print a picture, the printer hummed a happy song. It clapped its paper tray open and shut. But then the page that came out was blank. The printer was sad. Mia felt sad too. She tried again. Still no picture. Mia looked at the blank page and sighed. Then she saw a tiny crack in the paper. She turned it over and found words inside the crack. The words said, "I am a brave little machine." Mia laughed. She clapped for the printer. Now every time the printer prints, it hums and claps. And she always knows it is brave.

Tomorrow was the best day ever. Sun would come out and shine. But today was rainy. Rain tapped on the window. Lily wanted to print a sunny picture so she could take it outside. She put paper in the printer and pressed a button. The printer hummed and took the paper. Out came a bright yellow sun with smiling rays. On the back of the paper was a cat sitting in the rain. It was a funny cat. Lily held up the paper. The sun was warm and the cat was cute. She put the picture on the window so the rain light could touch it. Now it was fun to look at the sunny cat even when it rained.

Leo drew a bus on paper with his crayons. He wanted the printer to make a copy so he could show his friend. He put the paper in the printer and pressed the button. The printer hummed. It took the paper and printed a big red bus right there. Leo smiled. Then he took the paper out and gave it to his friend. His friend pushed the paper bus down the hall. Then the printer made another copy. This time the printer printed only half a bus. The other half was empty. Leo was surprised. He pushed the paper harder. Still not whole. He thought hard. Then he realized the paper had rolled a little wrong. He fixed the paper and printed again. Now the bus was all the way full!

Emma loved boats. She folded a piece of paper into a tiny boat. But the boat was flat and thin. It did not float. Emma wanted to see the boat in the water. She brought the flat paper to the printer. "Please print me a new paper," she said. The printer took the paper and printed a new boat. But this one was too big. Emma tried again. This time the paper was too small. Every time the printer made a boat, it was the wrong shape. Emma sat down and felt tired. Her mom came and saw. "Let us fold your paper first," Mom said. Emma tried. This time the paper made a perfect small boat. She put it in the water. It floated! Emma clapped for the paper boat and hoped the printer would make more soon.

Lily had a printer on her desk. It was just a box with buttons. One day Lily turned on the lamp above the printer. The light bulb glowed bright. "Can you have a name?" Lily asked the printer. The printer did not answer. Lily tried again. Still nothing. She thought and thought. Then she wrote the word PRESS on a piece of paper and put it in the printer. The printer hummed. It beeped once. Now the printer had a name: Press. Press was happy. But then Lily's brother came home from school. He wanted to press the button too. "No," Lily said. Brother wanted to print pictures all day. They argued. Lily felt mad. Then Lily's mom helped. "Let us share the printer," Mom said. Brother learned to wait his turn. Now both children used Press and were glad together.

Night came down. The room went dark. The printer woke up. It did not want to sleep. It began to hum low. Mia lay in bed. She heard the printer making a funny sound. "Hummm," said the printer. "I want to print," it said. Mia got out of bed. She walked softly to the printer. "Good night, Printer," she whispered. "Good night," said the printer quietly. Then it printed a small star on a piece of paper. The star was shiny. Mia took the paper star and held it close. The printer went back to sleep. In the morning, the sun climbed up the sky. Mia opened her window and looked at the star on her desk. Everything was nice. The printer slept while the sun came up. And Mia held the star until the next night.

Once upon a time there was a little desk. It was on the floor by an open window. The wind began to shake the desk. A cool breeze came in and blew out a piece of paper. The paper flew up to the tree outside. It was a printed page with a drawing of a cat. The cat was chasing a ball of yarn. The wind carried the page away very far. The cat could not find the paper anymore. It was sad. But the next morning, the wind blew the page back through the window. The cat found it again. It was okay. The cat played with the paper all day.

Grandpa had a printer that printed pictures of the sun. Grandpa liked to see the sun in his pictures. One day, grandpa put a sheet of paper in the machine. The machine started to print. Then the ink ran out. The pages came out dry and empty. The sun did not come out on the paper at all. Grandpa was sad because the picture was not good. He looked inside the machine. There were no more ink bottles. He went to the store and bought new ink. He put the ink back in the machine. Then he pressed print again. The sun came out on the paper. It was bright and warm. Grandpa smiled and looked at his new picture. He learned that you must take care of your things so they do not run out.

There were two printers in the room. One was big. One was little. The big one was a brother. The small one was a sister named Lily. Lily asked the big printer to print her name. The big printer said, "I am too big to print just a little thing." The big printer hummed loud and made a tall stack of paper. It was too much paper. It made a mess. Lily said, "That is not what I want." She asked the small printer to print her name. The small printer took only a small piece of paper. It printed the letters neatly. They fit on the page just right. The big printer felt bad. It tried to help too. But the small printer did the job well. The lesson is that smaller machines can do small jobs better. It is good to ask nicely.

A little puppy saw a purple printed page on the floor. The page had a picture of a bone on it. The puppy wanted the bone so much. The puppy ran off with the paper. He took it under his bed. A teddy bear stood by the door. The teddy bear looked down at the floor. The teddy bear could not find the paper. The teddy bear said, "Where is the paper?" The puppy did not answer. The teddy bear walked around the bed. Then the teddy bear heard a bell ring far away. It was a school bell. The puppy heard the bell too. The puppy knew he had to go home. He ran to the door. He dropped the paper on the floor. The teddy bear picked it up and looked at it. The teddy bear said, "Thank you for bringing it back." The puppy wagged his tail. The teddy bear gave him a hug. The puppy was happy. The paper stayed on the floor. The puppy could look at the picture whenever he wanted.

Ann had a printer at home. Ann loved to draw. She drew pictures all day. But the printer could not draw like a crayon. The printer could only print words and lines. Ann wanted to print a picture of flowers. She held the paper up. The printer said, "I cannot make pretty colors. I only make black marks." Ann was sad. She looked at her own crayons. The crayons were warm from being in her hand. The printer felt warm too. Ann said, "You are warm, aren't you?" The printer said, "Yes, I have been printing all day." Ann smiled. She went to the box and took out more paper. She asked the printer to print the lines. Then she held the paper up to the light. The printer could not make color. But Ann knew what she wanted to draw. She picked up her crayons and drew the flowers herself. The printer was happy to help with the lines. It hummed softly while she worked. They made the best picture together. The lesson is that every tool has its own way. You can work together to make great art.

Ben had a printer that would not work. The printer did not print anything. Ben was sad. Ben's duck friend came to visit. The duck walked over to the broken printer. The duck said, "What is wrong, Ben?" Ben said, "The printer is broken. I cannot print my picture." The duck looked at the printer. There was sand on the bottom of the machine. The sand was inside the gears. The gears did not work right. Ben took a hand and wiped the sand away. The gears started to spin again. The printer hummed and beeped. It printed Ben's picture right then. Ben was so happy. He showed the picture to the duck. The duck said, "You did it!" Ben told the duck, "I am glad I cleaned the sand out." The duck said, "Now you can print every time." Ben smiled. His printer worked again. He learned that if something breaks, you can try to fix it. Sometimes a little cleaning helps a lot.

Anna sat on a chair. The printer hummed and hummed. Anna asked, "Can you print my bedtime story?" The machine said yes. It took one piece of paper. It printed a picture of a bird sitting on a branch. Then it printed the story. A frog looked at the page. "A bird!" said the frog. "That is calm," said the frog. Anna read the story again. The printer beeped. "Done," it said. Anna closed her eyes. The frog croaked goodnight.

The library had a big printer. Anna went to the library. She wanted to print a book for her little brother. The printer took an apple from the basket on its table. It printed a story about sharing. A boy picked up the paper. The story was about crayons. The crayons were shiny and red. The boy smiled. He shared the book with his friend. Then the printer ran out of paper. The boy looked sad. "I am just so sad," he said softly. Nobody had extra paper for him.

Anna fed paper into the printer. The printer started to print a drawing of soup. But something got stuck! The paper jammed. The printer hummed loud and fast. "Help me," it said. "I cannot move." Anna reached in. Her hand touched something cold. It was wet paper. She pulled it out. The printer made a funny sound. "Oh dear," it said. "It was a little soup piece." Anna laughed. She pulled out all the stuck paper pieces. Then the printer printed again. It made a very nice soup picture.

Joe's family got a new printer. Joe stood next to it. "What are you?" he asked. The printer did not talk. It just hummed. Joe laughed out loud. A wild wind blew outside. The sky was very blue. Joe put paper in the printer. He asked it to print a picture. The printer took a sheet of paper. It printed a big sun and a blue sky. Joe smiled. The printer worked hard. Now Joe could print pictures every day. His wild laugh filled the room. Paper was fun now.

A mouse lived behind the office printer. Every night the mouse went to sleep in a warm dark spot. One day the mouse woke up. There was new paper all over the floor. The mouse grew big and mad. "Who left paper everywhere?" The mouse squeaked loudly. The printer beeped. "I just printed!" it said. "I did not push the paper down." The mouse looked at the printer. "You are mean," said the mouse. The mouse walked away. Soon other mice came. They cleaned up the paper. The printer was quiet again.

Anna wanted a party for her rabbit. She needed to find paper for invitations. She found a big stack of white paper. She put one sheet in the printer. The printer hummed. It printed a card with a rabbit on it. The rabbit was wild and happy. Anna cut the card into four pieces. She gave each friend a piece. Everyone found their piece. They each had a nice invitation. The party started at noon. Everyone found milk and cookies. They ate and played. Anna was so glad. The printer made a big round of happy cards.

Once upon a time, a family wanted to make signs for their lemonade stand. They printed big letters on white paper. The words said "FRESH LEMONADE" in round letters. Jack liked the round font best. He held the paper up and saw an apple drawn on it, too. His mom said, "Let us hang the signs on the tree." But the paper was too heavy to climb the tree. They tried again. This time they cut the paper smaller and taped it to sticks. The signs were ready. People walked by and read them. Everyone tried the lemonade. It was sweet and cold. Jack smiled. The family sold lots of cups.

Once upon a time, a little girl had old papers from school. She put them in a box under her bed. One day she took the box outside. She sat on a bench near the bin. A recycling truck came. It beeped at her. She fed all the yellow papers into the truck. Then a worker picked them up. He drove away fast. The papers went to a big factory. There they became new books and new paper. The girl felt sad that her old papers were gone. But then she remembered her mom saying old paper becomes new paper. She folded a tiny corner of one paper. It was still soft under her hand. A new book would be made from it soon. She smiled again.

One night after the office was quiet, a rabbit named Rose sat at her desk. Her boss had left a pie on the printer. It was a hot chocolate pie with chocolate on top. Rose wanted to read the receipt that came out. She pressed the green button. The printer hummed and beeped. A long page came out. It was just a small label. "Receipt: one hot chocolate pie," it said. Rose read the words quietly. The pie smelled wonderful. She ate a bite right there. It was warm and sweet. Then the printer made a funny sound. It started printing something else. It printed a picture of a moon. Rose laughed out loud. She hung the receipt on the wall. It looked pretty next to the dark window. The office was peaceful now.

Jack had a puppy named Buster. One morning, Jack wanted to print a picture for his wall. He found his dad's old printer on the table. It had a big red button. Jack did not press it. He wanted to press it himself. His dad watched from the doorway. "You can press it today," his dad said. Jack jumped up and down. He pushed the red button. The printer hummed. A long paper came out. It had a picture of a dog on it. Buster came running. He licked the paper. Jack laughed and held it high. Then the printer tried to print another thing. It printed a tall hat instead. The hat fell on the floor. Jack and Buster both stared. The hat looked wild on the floor. They both giggled. Jack put the hat on Buster's head. Buster looked silly but happy. Jack saved the picture for later.

Tess loved her house very much. One rainy Saturday, Tess sat at the table. Her printer stood alone on the shelf. It had no paper left. It sat there looking sad. Tess wanted to print a card for her friend. She pulled the paper tray open. Nothing came out. She pressed the button. The machine beeped once. Then it made a loud noise. The paper tray broke. Paper rolled everywhere. Tess looked down. She picked up a piece of paper. It was from last week. It was flat now. She put it back in the tray. The printer hummed. It printed a card for her friend. It was just a small drawing of a house. Tess was happy. She folded the card neatly. "Thank you, printer," she said. The printer beeped gently. It felt glad to help.

One evening, an owl sat on a branch. She liked to read old things. Near her, a crumpled paper lay on the ground. It had a drawing on it, but it was torn and bent. The owl picked it up carefully. She tried to flatten the paper. She pressed it with her wings. It stayed flat for a moment. Then the wind blew. The paper moved again. The owl tried harder. She sat on it. She pressed until her talons hurt. The paper stayed flat. The owl read the words on the paper. It said "Hoot. Hoot." She smiled. Then a friend came. The friend helped hold the paper still. The paper stayed flat. The owl read the words again. It was a message from a friend. She was glad the paper was not lost.

Once upon a time, a little drop of ink fell down from a bottle. It landed on the paper. The ink felt gray and small. The ink wanted to see the world. "I will go far away," said the ink. The ink rolled onto a tree. Up, up went the ink on the branches. It saw green leaves. It saw blue sky. But then the wind blew. The ink rolled down again. It went right back to the paper. It was home at last.

Once upon a time, a little boy had a calculator on his desk. He liked to put paper in the printer. The printer would print silly jokes on the paper. A joke would come out, and the boy would laugh. The jokes were neat and funny. Sometimes the printer would print a bubble picture too, which was nice. The calculator sat next to the printer, helping with numbers. One day, the boy asked for a joke. The printer hummed and took a piece of paper. Out came a neat joke about a cat who wanted to play. The boy laughed again. He thought the printer was the best friend he had. Now, the calculator and the printer work together every day. The jokes always make him smile.

A cat named Puff lived near the printer. Puff loved warm places, so he liked to sleep on the printer. One day, Puff got a little bit mad. He jumped onto the top of the warm machine. He did not mean to be mad. But his tail knocked the stack of paper down. All the paper fell on the floor. The printer could not print. It was sad. Then a friend came over. The friend helped pick up all the papers. The friend stacked them back in order. The printer hummed again and printed more paper. Now Puff slept right back on the warm machine. Everyone was happy again. Puff learned that jumping on things can sometimes make others sad. So now he waits for the printer to be done first.

An old printer sat on a table in a house. It was gray and slow. It took a long time to print one piece of paper. A dog named Buster came to visit. Buster wanted a picture of his own dog. "I want a picture of me!" said Buster. The old printer started to hum. Then it beeped slowly. The paper came out, but it was very slow. Buster lay down and waited. He did not move. After a while, the paper was ready. It was a picture of Buster! "Thank you," said Buster happily. "You are a great printer." The old printer felt warm and proud. Buster gave the printer a pat. Now every day, Buster comes to see the gray old printer. They are both happy together.

A young girl had a printer at home. One day, she printed a drawing of a big orange tree. But she printed it upside down. The tree looked like a backwards tree. She was not happy. "This is not right," she said. The printer heard her and tried to fix it. But it still looked wrong. The printer felt sad inside. It could not change what it had already printed. Then the girl thought about it. She flipped the paper around. Now the tree was correct. "Sorry I made you print that wrong thing," the printer said softly. "I am sorry too." The girl smiled. "It is okay now." From then on, when the printer did something wrong, it said sorry first. It learned that saying sorry makes people feel better. And soon the printer was happy again.

Jack wanted to open a pretend restaurant. He needed a menu to show people. Jack went to the printer and fed it paper. "Print my menu please," he said. The light bulb above the printer glowed bright green. The printer hummed and began to print. A menu came out on the paper. There were nice words about food. But then something unexpected happened. A bug flew into the light bulb. The bulb flickered and went dark. The printer stopped. "Oh no," said Jack. "The light is out." Jack looked around. He found a new light bulb in a box. He took it and put it in place. The light bulb glowed again. The printer hummed and printed the menu once more. The menu was perfect this time. People who visited the pretend restaurant loved the menu. Jack was so glad the printer did a good job.

Every night, a little girl called Lily went to bed. But before bed, she wanted a story. She put paper in the printer. A story came out on the paper. It was a story about going to school. The story talked about friends and learning. Lily read the story by the gray lamp next to her bed. She loved the story about the apple. In the story, an apple fell from a tall tree and became a sweet treat. That reminded Lily of fruit at snack time at school. She smiled and closed her eyes. The printer hummed quietly as it finished. The story was very helpful for going to sleep. Now, every night, Lily prints a bedtime story. It helps her rest well. She knows the printer is always there when she needs it. Goodnight, printer.

Once upon a time there was an old printer named Pen. Pen had a very good friend called Scan. Scan sat right next to Pen on the table. Scan was a scanner. They were best friends. One day Pen wanted to print a gift for Scan. Pen asked, "Can you print a picture of a calculator for me?" Scan said, "Yes! I will help." So Pen put a piece of paper in the tray and pushed the button. The paper came out warm and nice. It was a picture of a calculator. Scan looked at it and smiled. "That is my favorite," Scan whispered. Then Pen printed another picture too. Scan liked both pictures. They sat together and looked at their pictures all day. Pen was happy because his friend Scan was happy. That made Pen very glad inside.

One cold morning, Farmer Joe went to his kitchen. He opened the door and stepped into the room. It was very cold outside. Joe brought some new apple slices close to the printer. He slid them into the tray. "I want to print a picture of an apple for my kids," Joe said softly. The printer hummed and beeped. Out came warm paper, and then out came a picture of an apple. Joe picked up the warm apple print and held it near the fire. But the paper started to cook. It curled and turned brown. "Oh no," Joe said. He pulled the paper back. The apple slices were still good, but the printed apple was ruined. Joe put the warm paper away and ate his real apple. The picture was stuck in the tray. Even though the apple print was wrong, the real apple tasted so good. Every morning, Joe liked to print an apple and eat it with his family.

There was a small printer named Dot who lived on a big office table. Dot was afraid of the dark. When the lights went off, Dot felt small and scared. One night, Dot heard a duck quacking outside the window. "Quack, quack," the duck said. "I am sleeping right here on the hill." Dot said, "Oh, I am scared." The duck said, "Do not be scared. I will stay with you." So the duck hopped onto the table next to Dot. The duck fluffed its feathers and rested. Now Dot felt safe. During the day, Dot did not mind the dark. He took paper from the tray and printed pictures all afternoon. At night, he was happy that his friend the duck was there. The duck would wake him in the morning with a soft quack. They stayed together every single night. Dot learned that being brave is not about not being scared. It is about having someone to sit next to when you are afraid.

At school, Printer Mary loved her job. The teacher told the class, "Printer Mary will print our pictures today." Mary took a blank piece of paper and began to print. She printed a big red sun. The children clapped. Then Mary printed a green tree. The teacher smiled. "Print more!" the teacher said. Mary printed a blue fish swimming in water. Everyone laughed and said it was funny. Then Mary printed a yellow house. The children stood up and walked around the tables to look at the pictures. Little Timmy held up his picture and said, "This is my house, and I live on a hill!" Mary said, "Thank you, Timmy." Mary kept printing until all the papers were full. The children had wonderful pictures to show their families. Mary felt proud because she could help everyone learn new things with her pictures.

Nick had a printer at home. Nick loved to print things. One day Nick tried to print a nest. A nest is where a bird puts its eggs. Nick pushed the button and the printer started to work. But something was wrong. The printer printed the same word again and again. "Nest! Nest! Nest! Nest!" the paper said over and over. Nick pulled the paper out. "Oh no," Nick said. "I keep printing the same word." Nick tried again. Still it printed only the word nest. Nick took the paper tray out to look inside. There was nothing there. The paper was empty except for one word that would not stop. Nick threw the paper away. He knew that a good printer does not print the same thing forever. It needs paper and ink to make new words. Next time, Nick printed a drawing of a bird instead. The bird looked happy sitting in its nest. Nick put the paper back in the tray. He learned that printing the same thing over and over makes no new things at all.

Tom sat down at his printer. Tom wanted to print a card for his mom. He slid a piece of paper into the empty tray. The tray was empty, so the paper just lay there flat. Tom pushed the button. The printer hummed but did not print anything. "Why is this so hard?" Tom said. He pressed the button again and again. Still nothing came out. Tom pulled the paper tray out. "The tray is empty," Tom said sadly. He needed paper to print. Without paper, the printer cannot do its job. Tom looked around the room. He found a roll of paper near the shelf. He put it in the tray. Now the printer started to work. Warm paper came out, and a nice card was ready. Tom gave the card to his mom. She hugged Tom and said, "Thank you, honey." Tom learned that even when doing something seems hard at first, if you look for the right tools, everything works out fine.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Whiskers. Whiskers liked to sit on the table near the printer. The printer had no name yet. One day, Whiskers said, "I am your friend." And the printer said, "Thank you." That was funny. Then something wild happened. A mouse ran across the floor and jumped right into the printer! The printer made a loud beep. Whiskers ran over and poked the machine. The printer printed a picture of a cat. The printer printed a picture of a mouse. Whiskers laughed. Now the printer had a name too. It was called Whiskers.

Once upon a time, there was a robot named Pip. Pip brought paper to the printer every day. Paper came from the sea because ships carried it. But today the sea was messy. Ripples and waves pushed the paper around. Pip hopped up and down to stay steady. He hopped over a big wave. He hopped over a small wave. The printer was waiting. Pip set the paper on the tray. "Here you go," Pip said. The printer hummed a happy tune. The paper was dry and ready. Pip smiled. That was a good day for printing.

Once upon a time, there was a shy kitten named Lulu. Lulu did not have a home anywhere. She lived under a table. She watched the printer print pictures of birds. One day, the printer printed a piece of paper. Lulu saw that the paper looked like a plane. She curled up tight. Then she took the paper and folded it into a tiny airplane. She held it close to her chest. The airplane hummed as she flew it across the room. Lulu was so happy. She chased her airplane around the house. But then the wind blew. The airplane flew out the window. Lulu felt very sad. She sat on the floor and cried softly. Later, someone found the airplane outside. They brought it back to Lulu. Lulu was not sad anymore. She poked the airplane with her nose. It hummed again. Lulu smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Benny. Benny wanted to print a big picture of an apple. He went to the printer. But the printer broke down. The printer made a sad beep. Benny felt very mad. He kicked the table. "That does not work," Benny said. Then a helpful little bird named Pip flew down. "Don't kick," Pip said. "Let me try." Pip sat on the printer's side and tapped the buttons gently. The printer hummed. The printer printed a picture of an apple. Benny looked at the apple picture. He was so happy. "Thank you, Pip," Benny said. Benny patted Pip on the head. The printer worked well again. Benny ate the apple picture from the page. He did not eat the real apple. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a busy printer at work. Many people came to print things. Mrs Lee came first. "Please print my recipe book," she said. The printer hummed and printed. Tom came next. "I need a picture of my dog," he said. The printer printed. Amy came with a stack of papers. "I need all of them printed," she said. The printer was busy but still tried hard. Then little Tim walked up. Tim had a spoon in his hand. "My spoon is broken," he said. "Can you fix it?" he asked the printer. The printer said, "I can print pictures to help you think." Tim put the spoon down and sat at the table. The printer made a nice drawing of a spoon. Tim looked at the drawing. He smiled. "That helps me a lot," he said.

Once upon a time, there was a cow named Daisy. Daisy wanted to print a picture of a cake. She asked the printer to do it. The printer tried to print the cake. But the printer made a wrong sound. It was not a good sound. Daisy frowned. "What is wrong?" she said. "I do not know," the printer said. "I am trying to print a cake. But I make a funny sound." Daisy had an idea. She gave the printer an apple. "Maybe if you are careful," she said, "the apple will help." The printer tried again. This time the printer hummed a sweet song. The cake picture came out perfect. Daisy clapped her hooves. "You did it!" she said. "Thank you," the printer said. The printer printed a second cake too. Both cakes were warm from the printer's hum. Daisy ate the first cake on the page. Then she ate the second one. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily found a big seed in the garden. She put the seed in a cup of water. The seed grew into a tall plant. Lily wanted to draw a picture of the plant, so she took out her printer. She put paper inside and pressed a button. A green picture came out of the printer. Lily was very happy. Then she got her crayons. She colored the green parts green again, and she added red flowers on top. She picked up her crayon and began to color carefully. First she colored the stem, then she colored each flower one by one. When she was done, she held up her picture. "Look, Mama!" she said. "The plant is so big!" Her mother smiled. Lily learned that you can print a picture and then add your own colors to make it even more beautiful.

One winter day, it was very cold outside. Snow fell from the sky like white cotton. Tim had a milk bottle in his hand because he wanted hot milk before bed. He walked to his machine, which was his friendly printer. He put some paper inside and pressed a button. "Beep," said the printer. It made tiny cuts in the paper, making little snowflakes. Each snowflake looked different, but they were all beautiful. Tim took each one out and hung them on the window. He had five snowflakes. He tried to hang them with string, but one fell down. He picked it up gently and put it back. The next morning, the window had many pretty snowflakes. Tim learned that you can make pretty things from paper, and even when something breaks, you can fix it and try again.

There was a little fish named Fin who lived in a blue pond. Fin loved to swim and play with other fish. One day, Fin saw a picture of himself printed on paper. The picture showed a small fish in a wavy line. Fin smiled at the paper. "I look like you," said Fin to the paper. Then Fin went to see his friend, the printer. The printer was sitting on its table. "Can you print me?" asked Fin. The printer hummed and said, "I can print only blue things." Fin was sad. There was no green in the picture, no yellow, and no red. Fin tried to swim toward the paper, but the paper did not move. Fin's friend told him, "It is okay. You can still play with your friends." Fin swam away with his friends, and he did not mind. He knew that being different could still be fun.

Once upon a time, a boy named Sam found an old map in his grandpa's box. The map showed a cave far away. Sam was very excited. "I will find a treasure!" he said. He sat at his printer and put the map on the paper. "Beep," said the printer, printing the map carefully. Sam traced the path with his finger. At first, he followed the path well. But then he saw that the cave part of the map was torn. A big chunk of the map was missing. Sam felt sad. "How will I get to the cave?" he said quietly. His brother came and sat beside him. "Maybe we can draw another part," his brother said kindly. Sam took a new piece of paper and drew the cave again. They printed the new map. Now the whole path was complete. Sam learned that when things go wrong, you can always try to fix them instead of giving up.

A little boy named Leo drew a picture of a car. He drew a bright red car with four wheels and a big smiley face. Leo showed the drawing to his father. "Can you print this for me?" Leo asked. His father put paper inside the printer. "Beep," said the printer. A copy of the car came out. Leo held the paper and looked at his drawing. It looked almost exactly like his own drawing. Then Leo's sister came into the room. She reached for the paper. "That is mine!" she said. Leo gave her the paper. She looked at the car and said, "This is my car too!" They both laughed. Leo learned that sometimes things come out just right, and you do not need to be angry when someone else sees your work. You can share your drawings and keep them safe.

There were two printers at home. One was called Dot and one was called Boop. Dot was big and strong. Boop was small and weak. They loved to print pictures for children. One day, a strong wind blew through the house. It knocked over a stack of paper. Dot tried to pick up the papers, but the wind pushed him over. He was stuck under the table. "Boop, help me!" said Dot. Boop was small, so he could not lift Dot. "I am weak," said Boop. Then Boop got a long stick and pushed it under Dot. He lifted Dot up and together they picked up the papers. "Thank you, Boop," said Dot. "We did it together," said Boop. From that day, Dot and Boop worked as a team. They learned that even a weak friend can help a strong one, and working together makes everything easier.

Once upon a time, a boy named Leo wanted to print a picture for his grandma. He sat at the printer table and put in a piece of paper. He told the machine, "Print me a soccer ball." The printer hummed and beeped. But then the orange ink made the ball look funny. Leo shook his head. "I want it to look right," he said. His mom heard him and came over. "Let me help you," she said. She turned the paper a little bit. Then the soccer ball looked perfect. Leo smiled and gave the picture to his grandma. She held it up and said, "Thank you, my love." They both felt happy that day.

A little printer was very tired. It had been printing all morning and could not stop humming. The paper was getting old and bendy. "I need a rest," the printer whispered. But nobody was around to turn it off. The sun went down and the room got dark. A cat walked by and meowed. "What is wrong?" the cat asked. The printer said, "I am too tired to print more today." The cat licked its paw and said, "That is okay. You can rest tomorrow. I will print for you if you need me." So the printer sat quietly on its table all night. When morning came, it felt much better and printed again with a happy beep.

A little girl named Mia wanted to print a picture of her cat, Whiskers. She put the paper in the machine and typed the word "cat". But the ink was very bad that day. The words came out all mixed up. Instead of "cat", the paper showed a big purple sea wave with a fish jumping out of it. Mia gasped. "That is not my cat!" She cried a little bit. Then her brother saw the funny picture. He laughed and said, "It looks like a sea scene! Maybe we can print it and give it to Mom." Mia wiped her eyes. "Okay, that is fun," she said. They printed the sea picture and gave it to Mom for her desk. Mom loved it and said, "This is so silly and so pretty." Mia felt better because her brother helped her laugh.

One rainy day, a rabbit named Rosie sat by the window and looked out. Raindrops fell on the glass. "I wish the sun would come out," Rosie said. Her friend Kim said, "We cannot make rain stop. But we can try to print a sunny picture anyway." Kim took a blank paper and put it in the printer. "Print me a yellow sun," Kim told the machine. The printer worked hard. But when the picture came out, it was all smudged and gray. "Oh no," Kim said. "The paper got wet and everything is blurry." Rosie sniffled. "Don't worry. We can paint our own sun with crayons." Kim picked up a yellow crayon. They drew a bright yellow circle in the corner of the paper. It did not look exactly like the sun, but it was warm and happy. Rosie smiled and said, "A little drawing is still beautiful."

Kim loved her old printer and her new scanner best friends. They sat together on the same table every afternoon. One day, Kim asked the scanner to print a picture of her dog, Buster. But the scanner said, "I do not have paper right now." Kim looked sad. "That is okay," the printer said quietly. Kim sat down and hugged her friends. The printer whispered, "We will wait together. We always wait together." Then they heard a knock at the door. Someone brought fresh paper! Kim smiled and said, "Thank you!" They printed Buster's picture and Kim hung it on the wall. Buster barked happily from across the room. The three friends felt warm and close, like a family.

Pip wanted to print a birthday card for his friend Sam. He chose a nice flower picture and wrote "Happy Birthday" on the card. Pip put the card in the printer and pressed start. But then a loud sound came out. The printer broke down with a big crash! The paper jammed inside. Pip felt very sad. He looked at the broken machine. "No, no, no," Pip said softly. His mom came running. She gently fixed the paper and restarted the printer. It hummed again and printed a brand new card. Pip hugged the card and said, "Thank you, Mom." He gave the card to Sam. Sam opened it and cheered. "You are the best friend ever, Pip!" Pip beamed and felt happy again.

Once upon a time, a little girl brought home a printer as a gift from her grandpa. She put paper inside and pressed a big button. Out came a picture of her favorite cake, all red and white. She was so happy! But the next day, the printer made a sad sound. It ran out of toner. The picture came out gray and dull. The little girl felt sad and started to cry. She took the box to Grandpa. Grandpa gave her more toner. Now she prints her cake picture every single day.

A new printer sat on the table in a quiet house. It had never printed anything before. "What will come out?" asked the printer. A curious little fish swam up to the table. "Hello," said the fish. "I want to see what you can do." So the printer took a blank page and began to print. First it printed a tiny circle. Then it printed a long blue line. Then it printed a small shape that looked like a wave. The fish looked at the paper and smiled. "That is my brother," whispered the fish to the printer. From that day on, they were the best of friends.

Sara had a sheet of paper. It was completely blank. It wanted to become a picture of the sea. "I will be waves!" the paper said. "I will be fish!" the paper said. Sara helped. She held the paper up and looked at it. But nothing happened. The paper felt very sad. It was still just white. Sara did not shout at the paper. Instead, she took markers and drew waves, fish, and sand. The paper was sweet and glad. It had become the most beautiful sea ever.

Emma's friend gave her a puppy for her birthday. Emma was so excited. She wanted to print a thank-you note to say thank you. She put paper into the printer. She took out a cool piece of paper with a pretty design. She wrote Thank you on it. Then she pressed the button. The printer beeped twice and printed the note. Emma folded the note carefully and gave it to her friend. The puppy wiggled its tail. The friend was so happy. Everyone smiled and played together that afternoon.

Henry built a tall stack of paper. He stacked them one on top of another. The stack grew very high. "I am strong," Henry said. But then the stack fell over. Papers went flying everywhere. A cat ran under the table. The cat knocked papers onto the floor. "Oops," said Henry. He felt mad. "My papers are all on the ground!" He looked at the mess. His friend came and helped. They picked up the papers and put them back in the box. Henry learned that tall stacks are hard to keep standing.

A tiny robot lived inside a big printer. The robot was smooth and shiny. One day, the printer broke. It could not make any sounds. It could not take paper. The robot heard the sad beep. "No," said the robot. "I will fix you." The robot found a button on the side of the machine. It pushed the button gently. The robot sent a small magic spark into the machine. Soon, the printer hummed again. It took paper and printed a picture of a dog. The owner was so happy. The robot smiled. Printing was smooth again.

Once upon a time there was a little car that was shiny and red. Pip loved the car and wanted to play with it. Pip wanted to print a picture of the car. So Pip put paper into the printer. The printer hummed and beeped and printed the picture. But then the printer beeped too loud. It was very loud. Pip got scared. Then the printer stopped. Pip took the loud paper out. The picture was okay. Pip was happy again. A shiny red car sat on the table. Pip smiled. Everything was fine.

Once upon a time a party was coming. Lots of people were going to come. Pip wanted to print invitations. Pip found the printer. Pip fed paper into the printer. The printer printed all the invitations. But the printer made a mistake. Instead of printing the invitations it printed one big gate. Pip looked at the paper. It said the party would close the gate forever. Everyone would not be able to get in. Pip felt sad. Pip could not fix the mistake. The party was sad too. No one came to the party. Pip had to eat cake alone. It was a quiet sad day.

Once upon a time it was a cold morning. Pip wanted to print something nice. Pip found a piece of purple paper. Pip put the paper into the printer. The printer started to hum. But the paper was warm from being in a warm bed. The warm paper came out of the printer. Pip held the warm paper. It was soft and warm. But then the warm paper fell on the cold floor. The paper turned cold. Pip tried to pick up the paper. The paper was stiff. Pip could not make it soft again. Pip sat down and cried. The warm paper was gone. It did not matter now.

Once upon a time a soccer ball rolled near the table. It was dry and brown. The soccer ball wanted to run outside. The printer heard the soccer ball. The printer was curious. "I want to see what is outside," said the printer. The soccer ball ran away. "Come back," said the printer. The printer chased the soccer ball around the room. The soccer ball did not stop. It went under the chair. The printer bumped into the chair. The printer beeped. The soccer ball went up the stairs. The printer tried again. "I will chase you no more," said the printer. The soccer ball came back down. The printer chased it one more time. Then they both went outside together. They played in the grass.

Once upon a time a bird was sitting on a branch. The bird was a little red bird. Pip wanted to print a picture of the bird. Pip fed paper into the printer. The printer hit a drum inside. The drum made a sound. The drum made the wrong picture. It did not print a bird. It printed a fish. The bird saw the paper. "That is not me," said the bird. The bird flew away. Pip felt bad. The printer did not know what it did. Pip put the wrong paper aside. Pip could not share the paper because it was wrong. Pip tried again. The printer hit the drum again. This time it printed a bird. The bird came back. Pip gave the paper to the bird. "Thank you," said the bird. Pip learned that you have to try to do things right.

Once upon a time a cat was sleeping on a mat. The cat was a little gray cat. Pip wanted the cat to play. Pip asked the printer to print a toy. The printer started to print. But the printer did not stop. It kept printing pages. Pages piled up on the table. The cat woke up. "What is that noise?" said the cat. Pip looked at the pile of pages. "The printer is busy," said Pip. Pip tried to stop the printer. The printer kept printing. Pip picked up one page. The printer printed another page. Pip looked at the pencil. The pencil was dull. Pip could not make the printer stop. The cat ate some pages. Pip looked at the cat. The cat looked tired. Finally the printer stopped. Pip printed one small toy. The cat purred. It was enough.

Once upon a time, a little bug sat on a pink paper. The paper had numbers on it. A calculator was printed on the page. The little bug looked at the page and saw the shape of a boat. "I can make a boat," said the bug. He pulled the page out of the machine. He folded it. He folded it again. Out came a paper boat! The bug floated the boat on a puddle. The boat went round and round. "That is so fun," said the bug. The pink paper made the best boat in the whole world.

Once upon a time, there was a new bench where a printer sat. The printer's light blinked. One blink, then two blinks, then three blinks. The light kept blinking and blinking. A bird sat on the bench near the printer. "Why are you blinking?" asked the bird. "I am waiting for a job," said the printer. "I want to print a flower picture." The bird flew away. The printer kept blinking. Then a boy came with paper. He put paper in the printer. The light stopped blinking. The flower was printed. "Thank you," said the printer. It was very happy.

Ollie had a printer at home. The printer was sad. Its light did not blink. Its paper tray was empty. Ollie tried to fix it but he could not. "What is wrong?" said Ollie. A gentle mechanic came. He gave the printer some juice to drink. The juice was sweet and cold. After drinking the juice, the printer felt better. Its light began to blink. Paper slid into the tray. "Thank you," said Ollie. The printer was happy again. It printed a tree picture for Ollie to hang on the wall. The tree looked green and tall. Everything worked well.

A fish named Flo sat by the pretend restaurant. She wanted to print a menu. "Let us print a menu," said Flo. She put paper in the printer. The printer hummed. It printed a list of food. There were fish on the menu. There were cake on the menu too. Flo read the menu. "This looks good," she said. A bird came to the window. "What is on the menu?" said the bird. Flo pointed to the paper. "Fish, cake, and more!" said the bird. They ate pretend fish and drank pretend lemonade. The restaurant was fun. Flo was glad she could print the menu.

A little drop of ink lived inside a printer. The drop was orange and round. The drop wanted to see the sky. The drop saw the sky through the glass. "I wish I could go up high," said the drop. The printer took the drop in its arms. The drop rolled down the paper. Outside, the drop saw the world. A bird flew past. The drop danced on the paper. Then the printer pulled the paper back. The drop went into the tray again. But next time, the drop did not stay still. It rolled out of the tray onto the floor. It danced on the carpet. It rolled under the bench. "Where will I go now?" said the drop. A new sheet of paper caught it. The drop fell on the paper and became part of a drawing. A bird was flying in the picture. The drop was happy to see the sky through the art.
